Central Police Station.

CRIME REGISTER No:—misc.201/38.
Diary Number:— 1.
Nature of Offence:—
Time at which investigation begun and concluded each day
2p.m. - 4.30p.m.
18-2-38.
Places visited in course of investigation each day
Avenue Joffre,
Detective Office.
RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
ASSISTANCE TO GERMAN CONSULAR AUTHORITIES:
RE TWO GERMAN SEAMEN DESERTED FROM THE S/S
"CLAUS RICKMERS".
At 3.40 p.m. on 18-2-38, D.S. Fitts, attached to
Special Branch, brought to this station two German
seamen, Johannes Neubert, age 18, and Willy C. Grzybowski,
age 25, whom he had located at the Elite Butchery Co.,
636-8 Avenue Joffre, at 2.45 p.m. on instructions from
the German Consulate General, they having deserted the
above vessel.
D.S. Fitts requested that they be detained at this
station until the arrival of a German Consular Official,
so they remained in the Detective Office until the
arrival of Mr. Betz, Vice Consul, at 4.30 p.m., to whom
the two men were handed over.
（印：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER 21 FEB. 1938 (CRI) E BRANCH）
D.D.O."A" Div.

调查记录。
协助德国领事当局：
关于两名从“克劳斯·里克默斯”号（S/S "CLAUS RICKMERS"）轮船逃走的德国海员。
1938年2月18日下午3时40分，附属于特务股的警佐菲茨（D.S. Fitts）将两名德国海员带至本巡捕房，此二人为约翰内斯·诺伊伯特（Johannes Neubert），18岁，以及威利·C·格日博夫斯基（Willy C. Grzybowski），25岁。菲茨是于当日下午2时45分在霞飞路636-8号精英肉铺公司（Elite Butchery Co.）找到他们的，此举系遵照德国总领事馆的指示，因上述二人已从该船逃走。
菲茨警佐请求将此二人在本巡捕房扣留，直至德国领事官员抵达，因此他们留在侦探股办公室，直到下午4时30分副领事贝茨先生（Mr. Betz）抵达，随后将此二人移交给贝茨先生。
（印：副总监 1938年2月21日 (刑事) E 股）
“A”分区副侦探长。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY
File No. S. B. D. 8354
Late 2/38
Date February 18, 1938.

Subject Two German seamen desert from the s.s. "Claus Rickmers."

Made by D. S. Pitts Forwarded by C Crawford. D. D.

With reference to the contents of the attached reports
I have to state that D.S. Pitts in company with D.S.I. Grell
of the French Police, visited 636-8 Avenue Joffre at 3 p.m.
this afternoon and located the two wanted men. They were
taken to Central Police Station immediately and Mr. Betz,
the German Vice-Consul, informed. The latter gentleman
came to the Station and the two seamen were handed over to
him by D.S. Barton (Central Station).
Mr. Betz, in expressing his thanks to the D. C.
(Special Branch) for the assistance rendered, handed the
undersigned the attached official letter addressed to the
Commissioner of Police.

Good
D. S. Pitts
D. S.

（批：D.C. (Special Branch)）
（批：P. A. to D. C. (Sp. Br.) 18/2）

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 18 FEB 1938）

主题 两名德国海员从“克劳斯·里克默斯”号轮船逃走。

由警佐皮茨（D. S. Pitts）撰写 由克劳福德（C Crawford）转呈。副侦探长。

鉴于所附报告的内容，本人须陈述，警佐皮茨会同法国警察局的督察格雷尔（D.S.I. Grell），于今日下午3时前往霞飞路636-8号，并找到了两名被通缉者。他们随即被带往中央巡捕房，并通知了德国副领事贝茨先生。后者来到巡捕房，两名海员由（中央巡捕房的）巴顿警佐（D.S. Barton）移交给 him。

好

Deutsches Generalkonsulat
Shanghai
Telegramm-Adresse: „Consugerma“

Sch.8.b.

Shanghai, February 19th, 1938.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 8854
Date 21- 2- 38

Sir,

With reference to my letter of the 15th
inst., I have the honour to thank you for the assist-
ance given by the Shanghai Municipal Police to this
Consulate-General in the search for the two German
sailors Naubert and Grzybowski from the S.S. "Claus
Rickmers".

As it may be necessaryto persuade Naubert
and Grzybowski to return to their ship, I beg to
ask you to make arrangements in order to have the
above-named sailors taken on board the S.S. "Claus
Rickmers" by a police escort.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,

[Signature]

German Consul-General a.i.

F.W. Gerrard, Esquire,
Commissioner of the
Shanghai Municipal Police,
Shanghai.

Consul-General for Germany,
Shanghai.

Sir,

I have the honour to refer to your
letters dated February 15 and February 19, 1938,
and to inform you that Johannes Naubert and
Willy O. Grzybowski, two sailors of the S.S.
"Claus Rickmers", were located at 636-8 Avenue
Joffre in the afternoon of February 18 and
subsequently handed over at Central Police Station
to Mr. Betz, Vice Consul of your Consulate.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,

(Sd) F. W. Garrard.

Shanghai, 15th February, 1938

Sir,

It has been reported to me by the
Captain of the German steamer "Claus
Rickmers" that two members of the ship's
company ,
(1) Johannes Naubert, 18 years of age,
tall , fair hair and complexion ,
(2) Willy O. Crzybowski, 25 years of age,
of medium height, very slim and boyish
looking,
left board yesterday without permission and
have not returned since.

On the instance of the Captain , I beg to
request you to issue orders to have the two
above named persons arrested and handed over
to the Captain on board the S.S."Claus Rick-
mers".

I have the honour to be,
Sir ,
Your obedient servant,
[Signature]
German Consul-General a.i.

F.W. Gerrard, Esquire,
Commissioner of the Shanghai
Municipal Police,
Shanghai.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S.C. REGISTRY File No. 8354 No. S. B. D. Station 38 Date February 18, 1938）
Subject Two German seamen desert from the s.s. "Claus Rickmers."
Made by D.S. Pitts Forwarded by C. Crawford D.S.

In accordance with the instructions of the D.C. (Special Branch) appearing on the attached report, Mr. Jobez was visited at 11 a.m., today. He was handed a copy of the report concerning the desertion of the two men in question, when he detailed D.S.I. Grell to render the required assistance.

D.S.I. Grell and D.S. Pitts then proceeded to the Elite Butchery Company's Restaurant, 636-8 Avenue Joffre, where the owner was interviewed and arrangements made for him to hold the two seamen on his premises, by any pretext, when and if they arrive this afternoon. Upon their arrival he will communicate with D.S.I. Grell, who, in turn, will advise the undersigned, who will proceed to the restaurant to take the men to Central Station, after which they can be handed over to the German Vice-Consul.

D.S. Pitts
D. S.

（批：S! / D.R. / 18/2）

D.C. (Special Branch)

（批：Further proceedings to manage can be trusted? Or could he be seen to pass on reliable member of a ships company to watch?）

D.S. Pitts
C. 18/2

主题 两名德国海员从“克劳斯·里克默斯”号轮船逃走。
由警佐皮茨撰写 由C. 克劳福德警佐转呈。

根据所附报告上特务股副总监的指示，于今日上午11时拜访了乔贝兹先生（Mr. Jobez）。向他递交了一份关于这两名男子逃走的报告副本，他随即指派督察格雷尔（D.S.I. Grell）提供所需协助。

随后，督察格雷尔和警佐皮茨前往霞飞路636-8号的精英肉铺公司餐厅，会见店主并作出安排，要求他在今天下午这两名海员到达时，以任何借口将他们留在店内。一旦他们到达，店主将与督察格雷尔联系，格雷尔进而通知签署人，签署人将前往餐厅将这些人带往中央巡捕房，之后可将他们移交给德国副领事。

警佐皮茨
警佐

特务股副总监

（批：后续行动能否妥善管理？或者能否安排一名可靠的船员成员进行监视？）

警佐皮茨
C. 2月18日

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. 8354
Special Branch - S. Station 38
REPORT
Date February 18, 1938.

Subject Two German seamen desert from the s.s. "Claus Rickmers."

Made by D.S. Pitts. Forwarded by C. Crawford. D. I.

Mr. Betz, German Vice-Consul, telephoned this office
this morning and stated that two German seamen named:
(1) Johannes NAUBERT, aged 18, tall, fresh complexion,
fair hair and
(2) Willy O. GRZYBOWSKI, aged 25, looks much younger,
slim, small build,
had deserted from the German s.s. "Claus Rickmers," which
is due to leave Shanghai on the afternoon of February 19
or morning of February 20, 1938.

Mr. Betz has received information from Captain
J. Prahm, the master of the vessel, to the effect that the
two seamen are likely to be located some time this afternoon
at the Elite Butchery Company's Restaurant, No. 636-8
Avenue Joffre. He requests the assistance of the Police
in having these men brought to the German Consulate-General
in order to have the matter thrashed out so that they may
go back to work on their ship and not remain unemployed
in Shanghai, as they probably will if they are allowed
to stay here.

The German Vice-Consul is prepared to address an
official communication to the Commissioner of Police on
this subject should it be deemed necessary, but in order
to save time he has first given the above details by
telephone.

（批：Please take up — D. S. Pitts
Mr Tobith cast any conflicts
& ask his assistance as to
D.C. (Special Branch). Briefly, & report
arrangements made）

（左侧批注：D.S. Pitts / D.S.P. / 18/2）

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / 18 FEB. 1938 / SPECIAL BRANCH）

报告
日期 1938年2月18日。

主题 两名德国海员从“克劳斯·里克默斯”号轮船逃走。

由警佐皮茨撰写。由克劳福德督察转呈。

德国副领事贝茨先生今早致电本办公室，称两名名为：
(1) 约翰内斯·诺伊伯特（Johannes NAUBERT），18岁，高个子，面色红润，金发，以及
(2) 威利·O·格日博夫斯基（Willy O. GRZYBOWSKI），25岁，看起来比实际年龄小很多，瘦削，身材矮小，
的德国海员已从德国轮船“克劳斯·里克默斯”号逃走，该船预计于1938年2月19日下午或2月20日上午离开上海。

贝茨先生已从该船船长J·普拉姆（J. Prahm）处获悉，这两名海员可能于今天下午某个时候出现在霞飞路636-8号精英肉铺公司餐厅。他请求警方协助将这些人带到德国总领事馆，以便彻底解决此事，使他们能回到船上工作，而不是在上海失业，因为如果允许他们留在这里，他们很可能会失业。

如有必要，德国副领事准备就此事项致函警务处处长，但为了节省时间，他先通过电话提供了上述详情。

（批：请处理 — 警佐皮茨
托比思先生是否有任何冲突
& 询问他的协助关于
特务股副总监。简要地，& 报告
已作出的安排）

（左侧批注：警佐皮茨 / D.S.P. / 2月18日）

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 / 1938年2月18日 / 特务股）

At 7.20 p.m. 28/5/39, F.S.227 Walker attached
to Wayside and then off duty brought to the station
the accused described on Sheet 1 and reported that
after a period of observation he had arrested the
accused on suspicion of being a pick-pocket further
that when he had just arrested him a wallet containing
$41.55 in cash and several personal papers had been
found on the ground near where accused had been
observed.

Enquiries by D.S.Muir ascertained that at
about 6.50 p.m. F.S. Walker had arrived at a bus stop
at the Broadway Mansions to wait for a bus to return
to Wayside. When the bus arrived, F.S.Walker observed
the accused attempt to board then apparently change
his mind to wait for another bus.

This tactic was repeated on the eventual arrival
of four other buses and although the accused was not
actually observed to pick the pocket of any intending
passenger he was observed to jostle amongst the
crowd unnecessarily and by this action F.S.Walker
decided that he would arrest him on suspicion.

Upon the accused being taken in custody from
amongst the crowd of passengers and these persons
having boarded the waiting bus a wallet was discovered
being on the ground near to where the accused had been
observed jostling passengers. This wallet was brought
to the station and upon being searched several
personal cards were found together with $41.55 cents
in notes and coins inside apparently indicating that
the wallet a Mr. S.Elliott, residing at 260...

1939年5月28日下午7时20分，隶属于路边巡逻队且当时已下班的警员沃克（F.S.227 Walker）将第1页所述的被告带至巡捕房，并报告称，经过一段时间的观察，他以涉嫌扒窃为由逮捕了该被告；此外，在他刚逮捕被告时，在观察到被告的位置附近的地面上发现了一个钱包，内有现金$41.55及若干个人文件。

经警司缪尔（D.S. Muir）查询查明，下午6时50分左右，沃克警员到达百老汇大厦的一个公交车站等候公交车返回路边巡逻队驻地。当公交车到达时，沃克警员观察到被告试图上车，随后显然改变主意等待另一辆公交车。

在随后四辆公交车到达时，这种策略重复出现，虽然并未实际观察到被告对任何有意乘车的乘客实施扒窃，但观察到他在人群中不必要地挤撞，沃克警员据此决定以嫌疑为由逮捕他。

当被告从乘客人群中被带走 custody，且这些人登上等候的公交车后，在观察到被告挤撞乘客的位置附近的地面上发现了一个钱包。该钱包被带至巡捕房，经搜查，发现内有数张个人名片以及$41.55美分的纸币和硬币，这显然表明该钱包属于居住在...260号的S·埃利奥特先生（Mr. S.Elliott）...

The accused was questioned regarding the crime but denied all knowledge however as he is well known as a pick-pocket he has been placed on a Writ of Detention to enable detectives to investigate whether he is responsible for the many reported cases of pocket-picking for bus passengers.

Remarks
(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be
commented on by investigating officer).

Complainant boarded an omnibus of the China
Central and Urban Company, a about 7.15 p.m. on the
27/8/39, outside of the Broadway Mansions to
proceed to Kunping Road. On the way he discovered
his wallet containing $7.50, an identification card
and two photographs of himself had been stolen from
his hip pocket. He returned to the bus-stop outside
of Broadway Mansions and kept observation with a
erman named Moral Max of 81/79 Ward Road. He then
observed a Russian male acting suspiciously among
persons boarding several buses of the company he
had travelled by. He approached this man and on
grasping him the man dropped a wallet, which was
picked up by another person, whom he cannot describe
and who ran away. Complainant brought the Russian
to this station. His particulars were ascertained
to be as described on Sheet 1. In the suspect's
possession was found to be one wallet containing
$ 1.10 in notes and ticket from the Shanghai Tram-
ways. The wallet so far has not been identified.

Interrogated at length the suspect denied
having, or being concerned in pocket-picking.

In view of the fact he is a known criminal
and specialises in pocket-picking, and under the
circumstances he was arrested he has been placed on
a writ of Detention.

Special Branch.

控告人于1939年8月27日晚上约7:15，在百老汇大厦外登上了华中都市公共汽车公司（China Central and Urban Company）的一辆公共汽车，前往昆平路（Kunping Road）。途中，他发现自己的钱包（内含7.50美元、一张身份证及两张本人照片）从臀部口袋中被盗。他返回百老汇大厦外的公交车站，并与住在华德路（Ward Road）79/81号的德国人莫拉尔·马克斯（Moral Max）（音译）一起进行监视。随后，他观察到一名俄罗斯男子在他乘坐的那几路公交车的乘客中行为可疑。他走近该男子，在抓住他时，该男子掉落了一个钱包，钱包被另一人捡起，此人特征无法描述并逃跑了。控告人将该俄罗斯人带至本捕房。经核实，其个人信息与第1页所述一致。在嫌疑人身上发现一个钱包，内有纸币1.10美元及一张上海电车公司车票。该钱包目前尚未被认领。

the accused described on Sheet 1, was arrested

During the period of remand the accused has
been interrogated at length by the undersigned, and
denied stealing the wallet of witness H. Pincus,
He also denied picking the pocket of another person.

The two witnesses H. Pincus, and Moral Max
have been again questioned and they maintain they
actually saw the accused remove a wallet from the
hip-pocket of another German refugee, whose particu-
lars are unknown, as he cannot be located. At the
time the witness arrested the accused he dropped the
wallet which was picked up by the unknown German who
left the scene.

The accused is well known to the Police to
be an active criminal in pocket-picking, and in view

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

On 28/9/39 the accused appeared before the S.S.D.Court and after preliminary trial the case was remanded until 6/9/39.

The accused has four previous convictions.

During the period of remand on several occasions the accused was removed from the station cells and questioned, but he strongly denied stealing the complainant's wallet.

He also denied picking the pocket of another person as stated in diary 1 of this report.

The complainant and witness were seen by the undersigned again and they repeated their previous statements that they actually saw the accused removing the wallet from the hip pocket of a German refugee. As it stated before the accused had discarded the wallet which was immediately picked up by the owner who then went away. Before departure this person spoke to the complainant in German language. The complainant had promised to bring this person to the station if he met him again, but so far without success.

However, on the strength of the evidence given by the complainant and witness he is being charged with the pocketpicking of a wallet from a person unknown which is referred at latter part of report and therefore becomes the subject of P.I.R.653/39.

他也否认如本报告日志1中所述扒窃另一人的口袋。

具名者再次会见控告人和证人，他们重申了之前的陈述，即确实看到被告从一名德国难民的臀部口袋中取出钱包。如前所述，被告丢弃了钱包，钱包随即被失主捡起并离开。离开前，此人与控告人用德语交谈。控告人曾承诺若再遇到此人会将其带至捕房，但至今未果。

然而，基于控告人和证人提供的证据，他被指控从一名身份不明者处扒窃钱包，此事在报告后半部分提及，因此成为初步调查报告（P.I.R.）653/39号的主题。

Remarks
(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be
commented on by investigating officer).

The accused described on sheet 1 of this
report arrested on the 30/6/39 in connection with
(H) Misc. No. 215/39 on being questioned by the under-
signed admitted that on the 25/6/39 they concerned
together decided to commit a theft from an evacuated
shop at 120 Broadway. At about 11 a.m. 25/6/39 they
entered the shop by breaking a pane of glass of a
small window situated under the show window of the
shop and then inserting the hand through the hole
in that glass released a latch securing the window
from inside and opened same. They reached the said
window which is about 10 feet from the ground by
scaling an iron grille securing the show window.

The accused then slept on the shop premises
and on the following day (26/6/39) examined the
premises selecting goods which they intended to
remove in the evening after dark fall. At about
8.15 p.m. 27/6/39 some of passers by observed the
accused through the window and informed members of
J.H.L.P. On arrival of J.H.L.P. the accused attempt-
ed to escape through the roof of the shop but were
arrested by above authorities and taken to J.H.L.P.
Headquarters, Hanover Road.

One cigarette lighter, 1 cigarette holder and
3 collar clips were found on the accused when they
were searched by members of J.H.L.P.

The said property was handed over by J.H.L.P.
authorities to Russian Emigrants Association on the
30/6/39 and all the accused alleged the hand over

本报告第1页所述的被告于1939年6月30日因涉及(H)杂项案第215/39号被捕，在接受本警员讯问时承认，他们于1939年6月25日共同决定盗窃百老汇路120号一家已撤离的商店。1939年6月25日上午11时许，他们通过打破位于商店橱窗下方的一扇小窗户的玻璃进入店内，随后将手穿过玻璃上的孔洞，松开从内部固定窗户的门闩并打开窗户。他们通过攀爬固定橱窗的铁栅栏到达了这扇离地约10英尺的窗户。

被告随后在商店 premises 过夜，并于次日（1939年6月26日）检查了该处所，挑选了他们打算在天黑后的傍晚搬走的货物。1939年6月27日晚上8点15分左右，一些路人透过窗户观察到被告，并通知了犹太人力警察队（J.H.L.P.）成员。犹太人力警察队抵达后，被告试图通过商店屋顶逃跑，但被上述当局逮捕并带至汉诺威路犹太人力警察队总部。

犹太人力警察队成员在搜查被告时，在他们身上发现了一个打火机、一个烟嘴和三个领夹。

上述物品由犹太人力警察队当局于1939年6月30日移交给俄国侨民协会，所有被告均声称移交……

Slobodchikoff, French Police, came to the station and requested assistance to arrest a Russian female named Marie Feoktistova, residing in Lane 12, House 32, Henfong Road, in connection with a larceny of U.S.$145 from an American sailor named Blays attached to U.S.S. "Chaumont". | |
| | Further enquiries revealed that the above named female, well known prostitute, had on 5/9/39, met the American sailor in the Shanghai Bar in the French Concession and whilst the sailor was heavily under the influence of drink she had relieved him of this amount of money, then left the sailor who later reported the offence to the French Police. | |
| | On 8/9/39 at 12 noon, D.S. Greenfield, Bubbling Well, accompanied by D.S.I. Belashenko brought this female to the station for enquiries in connection with a similar offence reported at B'Well. | |
| | Upon being questioned regarding this offence she strongly denied any knowledge however, she did admit accepting money for "wife-keeping" from a drunk American sailor in the French Concession. This money U.S.$13.00 already changed to N.C.$488.00 by her was handed over | |

| | 1939年9月9日下午2点30分，法国警察侦探 W. Slobodchikoff 来到巡捕房，请求协助逮捕一名名为 Marie Feoktistova 的俄国女子，她居住在恒丰路12弄32号，涉嫌盗窃隶属于美国军舰“肖蒙”号（U.S.S. "Chaumont"）的美国水手 Blays 的145美元。 | |
| | 进一步查询显示，上述女子是一名知名的妓女，她于1939年9月5日在法租界的上海酒吧遇见了这名美国水手，趁该水手严重醉酒之际，窃取了这笔钱，随后离开，该水手后来向法国警察报案。 | |
| | 1939年9月8日中午12点，静安寺巡捕房的侦探长 Greenfield 在侦探副督察 Belashenko 的陪同下，将该女子带到巡捕房，就一起在静安寺报告的类似罪行进行问询。 | |
| | 在接受关于此罪行的讯问时，她强烈否认知情，但她确实承认在法租界从一名醉酒的美国水手那里接受了“包养费”。这笔13.00美元的款项已被她兑换成488.00元国币，并已移交 | |

The requested assistance to the French Police detective was rendered by D.S. Muir and the female was brought to the station.

Upon being interrogated regarding the reported amount of U.S. $145.00 stolen she denied that this amount was correct however she did admit that since the theft she has bought a $55.00 wrist watch, redeemed property from pawnshops to the value of $33.00, paid 2 months house rent in advance and further having bought a quantity of new gramophone records. The female could when questioned produce no proof that the above transactions had been done with her own money.

The D.O. "C" was informed of the case and instructed that the female be handed over but that, she, if B'Well Station required, must be returned for further enquiries.

The undersigned has since learned that the money in the possession of D.S. Greenfield, has been handed over to the French Police.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
2 Russian Pick-pockets arrested for loitering on a omnibus stop.

At 9.30 a.m. on the 15-9-39, whilst on observation on Boone Road near Hanbury Road noticed 2 Russians, well known pick-pockets, loitering on a Japanese m/bus stop on above corner.

The above Russians were acting in a very suspicious manner and missed a few m/buses without boarding any of them evidently looking for a chance to commit a larceny.

On seeing the undersigned approaching them they immediately left the bus stop and proceeded in a hurry west along Woosung Road where they were arrested and brought to the station.

Their names and particulars are as follows:
1) Gregory Grunwald, 39, Russian, m/unemployed, 509 Route Vallon, F.C.
2) Leon Smiliansky, 49, Russian, m/unemployed, 64 Route Pichon, F.C.

Both the accused who are well known to Police criminals with previous record, on being questioned by detectives could not give any satisfactory explanations of their presence in this district, both being the residents of French Concession. The 2nd accused on being searched found to be in possession of $50.00 but when questioned re amount of his money stated that he has only $35.00.

2名俄罗斯扒手因在公共汽车站游荡被捕。

1939年9月15日上午9时30分，当本人在汉伯里路（Hanbury Road）附近的布恩路（Boone Road）进行监视时，注意到2名俄罗斯人，系众所周知的扒手，在上述路角的日本公共汽车站上闲逛。

上述俄罗斯人的行为非常可疑，错过了几辆公共汽车而未上车，显然是在寻找作案盗窃的机会。

当看到本人向他们走近时，他们立即离开车站，沿吴淞路向西匆忙走去，在那里他们被逮捕并带回巡捕房。

他们的姓名及详情如下：
1) 格里戈里·格伦瓦尔德（Gregory Grunwald），39岁，俄罗斯人，男/无业，法租界华伦路（Route Vallon）509号。
2) 莱昂·斯米利安斯基（Leon Smiliansky），49岁，俄罗斯人，男/无业，法租界皮雄路（Route Pichon）64号。

两名被告均为警方熟知的有前科罪犯，在接受侦探讯问时，无法对其出现在本辖区给出任何令人满意的解释，两人均系法租界居民。对第二名被告进行搜身时，发现其持有50.00美元，但在就其金钱数额接受讯问时，声称只有35.00美元。

At about 7 p.m. on the 27-8-39, complt. Mr. A. Braun, Russian, contractor, residing 156/47 Liaoyang Road, was in the act of boarding an omnibus, at the bus stop, outside of the Broadway Mansions, Broadway, when he had $35.00 taken from his pocket.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

One named M.A. Pritsker, Russian Pickpocket detained for enquiries.

At about 8.20 a.m. 14/9/39, D.S.I. Gigerson attached to Wayside Station brought to the station one named M.A. Pritsker, professional pickpocket, whom he had arrested on Broadway near Nanzing Road.

At the above time D.S.I. Gigerson was proceeding in the Japanese m/bus along Broadway towards Wayside.
The m/bus was overcrowded.

When near Boone Road the above detective observed M.A. Pritsker and one another. They were waiting for the m/bus and when about to board same they observed the detective in the m/bus and rushed away, but D.S.I. Gigerson gave a chase and arrested M.A. Pritsker near Nanzing Road whilst his companion made good his escape.

On being brought to the station and questioned M.A. Pritsker gave his address as House 15, Lane 114 off Route Vallen, but could not give any satisfactory explanation for his presence in this area.

Owing to the fact that pocketpicking complaints increased recently the suspect will be brought before the S.S.D. Court on Writ of Detention for the purpose of making further enquiries.

1939年9月14日上午8时20分左右，隶属于路边巡捕站（Wayside Station）的侦探副督察 Gigerson 将一名名为 M.A. Pritsker 的职业扒手带至捕房，此人系他在百老汇路（Broadway）靠近南京路（Nanzing Road）处逮捕。

在上述时间，侦探副督察 Gigerson 正乘坐日式机动巴士沿百老汇路向路边巡捕站方向行驶。
该机动巴士内拥挤不堪。

当接近布恩路（Boone Road）时，上述侦探观察到 M.A. Pritsker 和另一人。他们正在等候机动巴士，当准备上车时，他们发现了巴士内的侦探并迅速逃离，但侦探副督察 Gigerson 展开追捕，并在南京路附近逮捕了 M.A. Pritsker，而其同伙则成功逃脱。

被带至捕房并接受讯问后，M.A. Pritsker 供称其住址为瓦伦路（Route Vallen）114弄15号，但无法对其出现在该区域的原因给出任何令人满意的解释。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

One named P. Kravchenko, Russian, Pickpocket detained for enquiries.

On the morning of 23/9/39, the suspect was brought before the S.S.D. Court on a writ of Detention and was ordered to be detained till 30/9/39.

The accused has 8 previous convictions.

During the period of remand, the accused was removed from cells at regular intervals and thoroughly interrogated but strongly denied committing any offence recently. His residence at 613/12 A. Joffre, F.C. was visited by detectives with the assistance of French Police and his room thoroughly searched but nothing of an incriminating nature was found in there to connect him with any crime.

As it was mentioned in diary 1 of this report the accused was observed by the undersigned loitering on Broadway in the vicinity of the omnibus stops and on being arrested could not give any satisfactory explanation re his presence in this area.

Being himself the resident of French Concession it is quite evident that the accused was loitering with the intention to commit a crime, therefore he will be brought before the S.S.D. Court on the 30/9/39 when a charge of loitering will be preferred against him.

鉴于被告本人是法租界居民，其徘徊意图犯罪显而易见，因此他将于1939年9月30日被带至特别市政法庭 (S.S.D. Court)，届时将对他提出徘徊罪指控。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

One named P. Krarcheuno Russian Pickpocket detained for enquiries.

At about 4 p.m. 22/9/39 D.S.I. Beloshenko whilst on observation along Broadway near Woochang Rd. saw the above criminal walking Towards along Garden Bridge.

On being brought to the station and questioned he gave his particulars as follows:-

P. Krarcheuno, 35, Russian, S/Unemployed, residing 15 Linda terrace, French Concession.

Being a resident of French Concession he could not give any reasonable explanation for his presence in this area.

As there were many pocket picking cases were reported recently to wayside and this station, therefore on the 23/9/39, he will be brought before the S.S.D. Court on a writ of detention for one week to enable detectives to make further enquiries into the past activities of the suspect.

On 12-9-39, the three accused namely
2. Ivan Mashinsky, 42 Russian, s/unemployed, N.F.A.
4. Victor Smirnoff, 29 Russian, s/unemployed N.F.A.

During the period of remand they admitted committing this crime and led the detectives to the French Concession where all stolen clothing had been recovered from various pawn shops. The stolen property had been pawned for $16.00 by the 2nd accused.

Detention of two Russian Pickpockets.
On 21/9/39, the two suspects appeared before the S.S.D. Court and were ordered to be detained until 28/ /39.
The 1st. suspect has 5 previous convictions and the 2nd. suspect 1 p. c.
During the period of remand on several occasions they were removed from the station cells and interrogated but they strongly denied committing any crimes recently.
On 22/9/39, an identification parade was held at Hongkew Station which was attended by number of complainants from wayside and this station, but the suspects were not identified by any of them as persons responsible for thefts.
On 28/9/39, they will be brought before the S.S.D. Court when a charge of loitering will be preferred against them.

| | At 8.30 p.m. on the 26-9-39, a telephone message was received at Hongkew Police Station, from one named Kao Siau San Ts (葛小三子), residing No.116 Yuenfong Road, a macaroni shop, stating some Russians had been arrested for stealing. F.S. 101 Mitarevsky and C.D.C. 340 attended. On the roadway, outside of No.116 Yuenfong Road, they saw a wooden beam, which they learned had been carried from a demolished house in Wayside District, near Broadway, and Yuenfong Road, by some male Russians, who had left the scene. F.S. Mitarevsky then proceeded to a Chinese food-shop, No.172 Yuenfong Road, about 50 yards from where the beam had been left, and therein found | |
| | (1) S.P. Bezrodny, aged 41 years, married carpenter residing No.131 Woochang Road. | |
| | (2) C.S. Vasilenko, aged 29 years, single, R.F.A. | |
| | (3) S.N. Kravchenko, aged 29 years, single, R.F.A. whom he brought to Hongkew Police Station (Time 9 p.m.). | |

Continuing enquiries, D.S.I. Crowther accompanied by F.S. 101 Mitarevsky, and C.D.C. 340 proceeded to the scene with the four Russians suspected to have been concerned.
At the scene there was a large crowd of Chinese, mostly of the loafer class. Questioning of these persons failed to elicit anything definite of how the wooden beam came to be left outside of No.116 Yuenfong Road. During this enquiry, T. Fukushima, and three other male Japanese came to the scene. Owing to language difficulties, they could not be understood, therefore, D.S.I. Crowther, by telephone summoned D.P.S. 777 Furukawa to the scene, at about the time of telephoning, three Japanese marines arrived on the scene fully armed. No names were given of the Japanese marines, but through D.P.S. Furukawa, they informed D.S.I. Crowther, that the four Russians would be taken to the Hannen Road, Headquarters of the J.M.L. Party, for interrogation. During this time a Sergeant of the Japanese Gendarmerie arrived on the scene and took notes. He did not give his name.

Hongkew Station,
REPORT
Date Sept. 26th. 19 39.

Subject Arrest of three Russians.

Made by F.S. V. Mitarevsky Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

I beg to report that on 26-9-39, at 8.35 p.m. whilst on stand by duty in the station I was told by Sergeant on Charge Room Duty to attend a case on Yuenfong Road where a Chinese had telephoned to the station saying some Russians had been arrested.

On arriving at the scene I saw a wooden beam lying on the roadway outside 116 Yuenfong Road. I made enquiries with C.D.C. 340 and found out that it had been carried out from a demolished house in Wayside district by some Russians.

I proceeded to a nearby Chinese food shop No.178 Yuenfong Road and therein found the following persons:

1. S.P. Bezvodny, 41, m/carpenter, 131 Woochang Road.
2. G.S. Vasilenko, 29, single, N.F.A.
3. S.M. Kravchenko, 29, single, N.F.A.
4. E.P. Solodova, 31, married, N.F.A.

I brought them to the station and later assisted D.S.I. Crowther in making further inquiries at Yuenfong Road. The last name female, followed me to Hongkew Station. She was present in the foodshop, 178 Yuenfong Road, where I found the others.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,

[Signature] 26/9
F. S.
[Signature: Mitarevsky]

由外勤巡官 (F.S.) V. Mitarevsky 制作 转发者 [签名]

先生，

谨报告如下：1939年9月26日晚上8时35分，当我在捕房值班待命时，值班室警长告诉我前往源丰路处理一起案件，有一名中国人致电捕房称几名俄国人被捕。

到达现场后，我看到一根木梁躺在源丰路116号外的马路上。我与 C.D.C. 340 进行了查询，得知该木梁是由一些俄国人从路边区 (Wayside district) 一所被拆除的房屋中搬出的。

我前往附近的一家中式食品店，地址为源丰路178号，并在店内发现以下人员：

1. S.P. Bezvodny，41岁，已婚，木匠，武昌路131号。
2. G.S. Vasilenko，29岁，单身，无国籍外国人 (N.F.A.)。
3. S.M. Kravchenko，29岁，单身，无国籍外国人 (N.F.A.)。
4. E.P. Solodova，31岁，已婚，无国籍外国人 (N.F.A.)。

我将他们带到捕房，随后协助探目 (D.S.I.) Crowther 在源丰路进行进一步调查。最后提到的那名女子跟随我来到虹口捕房。她当时就在我发现其他人的那家位于源丰路178号的食品店里。

此致，
敬礼，

[签名] 9月26日
外勤巡官
[签名: Mitarevsky]

Remarks
(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be
commented on by investigating officer).

At 12.30 a.m. on the 6-9-39, in response to a
telephone message, F.P.S. Tajima, attended the
Japanese Consular Police, Woosung Road Sub-Station,
and received into his custody a male Russian, Pavel
Savchuk, aged 39 years, s/unemployed, residing No.
194 Ward Road.

Enquiries by D.P.S. 809 Masuda and the under-
signed ascertained that the arrested man at about
11.45 p.m. on the 5-9-39, was arrested by the
complainant Mr. Y. Ueda residing No.14 West End
Lane, at the latter address, and handed him over
to the Japanese Consular Police.

Complainant further stated at about 11.45 p.m.
on the 5-9-39, he was sleeping in a front room of
his house, No.14 West End Lane, and heard a noise.
He went to the verandah and there found the
accused.

The verandah is about 12 feet from the ground,
and can be easily gained by climbing a wall which
runs at the side of the house.

The accused denies attempting to get into the
house.

The accused has been charged with attempted
burglary.

Special Branch.

经副巡官（D.P.S.）809号增田（Masuda）及签署人查询查明，被捕男子于1939年9月5日晚11时45分左右，在西区路14号被居住于此的报案人Y. Ueda先生逮捕，并移交给日本领事馆警察。

报案人进一步陈述，1939年9月5日晚11时45分左右，他正在其位于西区路14号的住宅前屋睡觉，听到响声。他走到阳台，在那里发现了被告。

阳台离地约12英尺，攀爬房屋侧面的墙壁即可轻易到达。

Remarks
(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be

At about 2.10 a.m. on 25-10-39, S.I. Pawchinsky
brought to the station the now accused named G.R.
Muratoff, 33, s/unemployed, Russian, residing
N.F.A. whom he had found in a garage at No.97
Woochang Road.

Enquiries reveal that whilst S.I. Pawchinsky
was on patrol duty he observed the accused walking
along Woochang Road then enter a garage at No.97
after which then accused boarded a motor-truck in
the garage and commenced to create a hammering
noise.

The accused was then questioned regarding his
actions but could only give a reply that he wanted
a place to sleep.

Inside the motor-truck a hammer and screw
driver were found where the accused had been
sitting. These implements, he denied all knowledge
off, but enquiries at the garage also reveal that
only the hammer is the property of the garage
owner.

The accused is a well known criminal having
been released from gaol very recently.

In view of the fact that numerous "breakings"
have occurred in the district recently, the accused
has now been charged with Loitering with intent to
commit a felony and will appear before the S.P.M.
Court on the morning of 26-10-39, when a remand
will be requested to enable detectives to pursue
further enquiries.

（任何需由调查警官评论的显著或特殊特征）。

1939年10月25日凌晨2时10分左右，巡佐（S.I.）帕钦斯基（Pawchinsky）将现被告 G.R. Muratoff，33岁，职业：无业，俄罗斯人，住址：无固定住址 (N.F.A.) 带至巡捕房，此前他在武昌路97号的一个车库内发现了此人。

查询显示，当巡佐帕钦斯基执行巡逻任务时，观察到被告沿武昌路行走，随后进入97号的一个车库，之后被告登上车库内的一辆卡车，并开始制造敲击声。

随后就其行为讯问被告，但他仅回答说他想找个地方睡觉。

在被告坐过的卡车内部发现了一把锤子和一把螺丝刀。他对这些工具声称一无所知，但对车库的调查也显示，只有锤子是车库主人的财产。

被告是一名众所周知的罪犯，最近刚从监狱释放。

鉴于该地区近期发生多起“入室盗窃”案件，现以“游荡并意图犯重罪”起诉被告，他将于1939年10月26日上午出庭上海特区地方法院（S.P.M. Court），届时将请求还押，以便侦探进行进一步调查。

At 11.45 a.m. on the 9/9/39, a telephone call
was received from the J.N.L.Party, Chapoo Road
Sub-Station requesting station detectives to attend
to a pick-pocket case in which one Russian was
arrested by complainant and handed over to J.N.L.P.

D.P.S. Sameeshima and the undersigned attended
and brought to the station the accused described
on sheet 1 of this report together with complainant
one M. Matsumoto, Japanese, broker, residing 65
Chi Shing Li, off Dixwell Road, O.O.L. and one
witness named Au Tsang Pao (華春甫), attached to
the River Police, Pootung Station.

Enquiries ascertained that complainant and
above mentioned witness were proceeding in a
Japanese public m/bus along Broadway in Western
direction. At about 11.30 a.m. 9/9/39 when the
bus approaching Garden Bridge bus stop the complt.
got up from the bus seat with the intention to
leave the bus and noticed the accused who was
standing in front of the complainant and who (the
accused) in a moment came to a close contact with
the complainant's chest, pretending that he lost
his balance. Suspecting there was something wrong
the complainant examined the inside breast pocket
of his coat where he kept his wallet containing
$80.00 and discovered that same was stolen.

As the accused was only person standing close
to the complainant, he (complt) immediately got
a hold of him and observed that the accused

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Soong Zai Zung, age 28.
native of Ju-kao, Kompo. taken by me C.U.C.I.
at K.Rd. Stn. on the 6/11/39 and translated interpreted by Clerk Tsai.

At about 12 noon on the 29/10/39 when I was walking on
Tungchow Road near Hailar Road O.O.L.(Chapei) I encountered
two Russian males. On approaching me they stopped and one
of the Russians (the accused arrested in connection with this
case committed on the 5/11/39) produced a $10.00 banknote
He then asked me in Chinese language if I would change his
$10.00 banknote into 2 $5.00 banknotes. I agreed to do so
and took out thirteen $5.00 banknotes from my wallet. The
Russian then gave me the $10.00 banknotes first
and I in turn gave him two $5.00 banknotes. On receiving
my two $5.00 banknotes the Russian stated that the two
banknotes which I had given to the Russian were no good and
that he wished to select two banknotes himself, but before
having my permission he snatched my banknotes from my hand
and then looked them over. After he had done so he returned
the banknotes to me stating that he wished to have two new
Central Bank of China notes, and that as there were no
Central Bank of China notes, did not wish to change his
banknote. I then returned the $10.00 banknote to him. These
two Russians then rode away on their bicycles in an easterly
direction Shortly afterwards upon counting the banknotes again
I found $25.00 missing. At this time the two Russian males
had already gone away. At 4.30 p.m. on the 5/11/39 when two
Russian males were committing a like offence, I recognized a
Russian who was apprehended as the man who had previously
stolen my money. I therefore went to the Kashing Road Station
to report the offence. The above is my true statement.

Sd. Soong Zai Zung.

警方调查报告。

以下为宋才仁（Soong Zai Zung），28岁，江苏高邮人，于1939年11月6日在嘉兴路警局由我（中央捕房刑事调查股警探）录取，并由蔡姓书记员翻译的口供。

1939年10月29日中午12时许，当我在通州路靠近海拉尔路一带（越界筑路区域，闸北）行走时，遇到两名俄国男子。他们走近我并停下，其中一名俄国人（因本案于1939年11月5日被捕的被告）拿出一张10美元钞票。随后他用中文问我是否愿意将他的10美元钞票换成两张5美元钞票。我同意这样做，并从钱包里取出十三张5美元钞票。那名俄国人先把10美元钞票给我，我则递给他两张5美元钞票。收到我的两张5美元钞票后，该俄国人称我给他的这两张钞票不好，他想自己挑选两张，但在未获我允许的情况下，他从手中抢过我的钞票查看。看完后，他将钞票还给我，称想要两张新的中国银行钞票，因没有中国银行钞票，故不想兑换了。于是我将10美元钞票还给他。这两名俄国人随即骑自行车向东离去。不久后，我再次清点钞票时发现少了25美元。此时那两名俄国男子已经离开。1939年11月5日下午4时30分，当两名俄国男子实施类似犯罪行为时，我认出被捕的那名俄国人就是此前偷我钱的人。因此我前往嘉兴路警局报案。以上是我的真实陈述。

签署人：宋才仁。

three male Chinese had left the Shanghai Live Stock
Market and were proceeding along a footpath on the
side of a creek leading to Urga Road, when they were
accosted by the apprehended foreigner who was accom-
panied by another foreigner, and asked if they had

    The male Chinese Mau Ching Foo produced ten
$1.00 banknotes and handed them to the apprehended
foreigner who made pretence to count them, then
apparently being satisfied asked if the Chinese males
had any $5.00 banknotes to change for $10.00 banknotes.
    The Chinese male Tseu Kyih Yien (周智员) ✓
produced a number of $5.00 banknotes which were
immediately snatched from his hands by the apprehended
foreigner and handed to the accompanying foreigner
to count, who upon completing same handed the money
back including the $1.00 banknotes stating that Central
Bank of China notes were required.
    The two Chinese males involved, upon sorting
out their money found two $5.00 banknotes and five
$1.00 banknotes missing, from the total returned to

and apprehended the described foreigner, the accomplice
at this time making good his getaway.

三名中国男子离开上海牲畜市场，正沿着通往乌尔加路的一条小溪旁的人行道前行，此时被那名被捕的外籍男子及其另一名同伴拦住，询问他们是否有1美元钞票可兑换一张10美元钞票。
    中国男子苗金富拿出十张1美元钞票，递给那名被捕的外籍男子，该男子假装清点，随后似乎表示满意，又问这几名中国男子是否有5美元钞票可兑换10美元钞票。
    中国男子周智员（Tseu Kyih Yien）✓ 拿出若干张5美元钞票，随即被那名被捕的外籍男子从手中抢过，并交给同行的另一名外籍男子清点，后者清点完毕后把钱退还，其中包括那1美元钞票，并称需要中国银行的钞票。
    涉案的两名中国男子在整理钱财时，发现外国人退还的钱款中少了两张5美元钞票和五张1美元钞票，于是他们大吵大闹并抓住了那名外籍男子，而其同伙则趁机逃脱。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Tseu Kyih Ylen, age 28,
native of Ju-kao, Kompo. taken by me. S.D.C.I.
at K.Rd.Stn. on the 5/11/39 translated and interpreted by Clerk Tsai.

At 4.30 p.m. on the 5/11/39 I encountered two Russians
riding on bicycles on Tungchow Road near the Shanghai Live
Stock Market. On their approaching me, they stopped and in
a very polite and earnest manner asked me to change a $10.00 note,
which he was holding in his hand into $5.00 or $1.00 notes.
They were speaking Chinese language. At that moment one
Chinese named Mau Ching Foo saw this, and produced ten $1.00
notes and handed over same to one of the Russians (the accused)
After he had received same the same Russian asked me to
furnish some $5.00 banknotes for him. I, therefore, produced
seven $5.00 banknotes from my pocket and then gave the Russian
two $5.00 banknotes. The Russian then stated that he wished
to have Central Bank of China notes. He then snatched my
bank notes from me and looked over same. Afterwards giving
the money back to me stating that there was no Central Bank
of China notes. He also gave the $1.00 notes back to Mau Ching
Foo. On the money being counted again I found $10.00 missing,
whilst Mau Ching Foo also found $5.00 missing. We immediately
arrested the accused and then handed him over to the Indian
watchman No.430. The stolen money was taken away by the
absconded Russian.

The above is my true statement.

sd. Tseu Kyih Ylen,

警方调查报告。

以下为周啟賢（Tseu Kyih Ylen），28岁，江苏高邮人，于1939年11月5日在嘉兴路警局由我（特别处刑事调查股警探）录取，并由蔡姓书记员翻译的口供。

1939年11月5日下午4时30分，我在上海牲畜市场附近的通州路上遇到两名骑自行车的俄国人。他们走近我并停下，非常礼貌且诚恳地请求我将他手中持有的一张10美元钞票换成5美元或1美元钞票。他们讲的是中文。此时，一名叫苗金富的中国男子看到这一幕，拿出十张1美元钞票递给其中一名俄国人（被告）。接过钞票后，该名俄国人又让我提供一些5美元钞票。于是我从口袋里拿出七张5美元钞票，给了那名俄国人两张5美元钞票。那名俄国人随后称想要中国银行的钞票。他从我手中抢过钞票查看。随后将钱还给我，称没有中国银行的钞票。他也把1美元钞票还给了苗金富。再次清点钱款后，我发现少了10美元，而苗金富也发现少了5美元。我们立即逮捕了被告，并将其移交给印籍看守第430号。被盗款项被逃走的俄国人带走。

以上是我的真实陈述。

签署人：周啟賢，

commented on by investigating officer).

At 11.40 p.m. 10/11/39, a telephone message
was received from an unknown Chinese that a number
of loafers entered premises at 409 N. Seward Road.
P.S. Foster and C.D.C.191 attended and
arrested all the accused described on Sheet 1 of
this report.

P.S. Foster stated that there were some more
persons on the premises engaged in looting of wood
and fixtures etc. together with the arrested persons
but they managed to escape.

Enquiries made by the undersigned ascertained
that the premises in question were formerly occupied
by Japanese soldiers who recently removed from the
premises leaving same unsecured and unattended.

All the accused admitted that they entered the
premises in question with the intention to commit
a felony therein. All charged accordingly and will
appear before the S.S.D. Court on the morning of the
11/11/39.

备注
（由调查警官对任何突出或特殊情况进行评注）。

1939年11月10日晚上11点40分，接到一名身份不明的中国人的电话消息，称一群闲散人员进入了西华德路409号的处所。巡佐福斯特（Foster）和第191号中国侦探（C.D.C.191）到场，并逮捕了本报告第1页上描述的所有被告。

巡佐福斯特称，现场还有其他人正与被捕者一起从事盗窃木材和固定装置等行为，但他们设法逃脱了。

经签署人查询，查明上述处所此前由日本士兵占用，他们最近已搬离，导致该处所未加锁且无人看管。

所有被告均承认，他们进入上述处所的意图是在其中犯下重罪。据此对所有被告提出指控，他们将于1939年11月11日上午出庭受审于上海特别区法院（S.S.D. Court）。

At 4.50 p.m. 3-12-39, a telephone message was
received from the Japanese Consular Police requesting
to take custody of a Russian female detained by them
for larceny. P.S. 836 attended and brought to the
station the accused described on sheet 1 of this
report. One named Ts Sung Ding (complainant) also
accompanied party to the station and reported the
following:

He is godown-keeper in Pootung and on 3-12-39,
went to see his brother residing on N. Szechuen Road.
On his way back to Pootung the complainant boarded
the Japanese m/bus on N. Szechuen Road outside Foo
King Hospital (near Dixwell Road) to proceed to the
Garden Bridge. As there was no seat available the
complainant was compelled to stand and same time he
had noticed the accused and her companion (male
foreigner) were standing also beside him. There was
no necessity for the suspects to stand very close to
him as they did and beside that as soon as the
m/bus started they began to jostle him. When near
Jukong Road the two suspects suddenly left the m/bus
and disappeared. The complainant became suspicious
and on examining his pockets discovered that the
envelope containing $80.00 notes and kept by him in
the jacket pocket had disappeared. His fly button
was also unbuttoned. He reported the occurrence to
the m/bus driver and later alighted at him to go as
far as N. Szechuen Road Bridge and to report the
matter to the m/bus Inspector. The complainant
proceeded to the Bridge, but as no Inspector was

1939年12月3日下午4点50分，接到日本领事馆警察的电话留言，请求接管一名因盗窃被其拘留的俄罗斯女性。第836号巡佐（P.S. 836）到场，将本报告第1页描述的被告带至巡捕房。一名名为朱盛庭（投诉人）的人也随同前往巡捕房，并报告如下：

他是浦东的一名仓库管理员，于1939年12月3日去探望居住在四川北路的兄弟。在返回浦东的途中，投诉人在福民医院（靠近达威尔路）外的四川北路登上了日本公共汽车，前往外白渡桥。由于没有空座，投诉人被迫站立，同时他注意到被告及其同伴（一名外籍男子）也站在他旁边。嫌疑人没有必要像他们那样紧挨着他站立，而且公共汽车一启动，他们就开始挤撞他。当接近虬江路时，两名嫌疑人突然下车并消失。投诉人生疑，检查口袋后发现，放在夹克口袋里的装有80.00美元纸币的信封不见了。他的裤门襟纽扣也被解开。他将此事报告给公共汽车司机，随后下车，让司机开到四川路桥，并向公共汽车稽查员报告此事。投诉人前往大桥，但由于没有稽查员

Arrest of one named Sharifian Shahazardin
43 Russian, M.T.A. in possession of m/car tools.

At 4 p.m. 1/12/39, D.S.I. Ovsimikoff brought
to this station the above named person who was arrested
for being in possession of one wrench, one screw driver
and one hammer.

The suspect was arrested at 1.25 p.m. 1/12/39
by Havildar 364 (attached Central st) who saw the accused
disposing the above tools to a street hawker on Peiking
Road near Honan Road.

On being questioned the suspect stated that the
tools were given by him by a Russian known as "Misha"
whom he (suspect) met on Ysuchang Road.

It is strongly believed that the tools are
stolen property from some m/truck or car. Information
also was received by the undersigned and D.S. Fedoroff
to the effect that two Russian loafers (named at present
unknown) recently were active in stealing the parts and
tools from the m/cars in this area and probably they are
responsible for stealing the tools in this case.

On 2/12/39, the suspect will be brought before
the S.S.D. Court on a Writ of Detention for one week.

1939年12月1日下午4时，警佐 Ovsimikoff 将上述人员带至本捕房，该人因持有一把扳手、一把螺丝刀和一把锤子而被捕。

警方强烈相信这些工具是从某辆卡车或汽车上盗窃的赃物。下述签署人及警佐 Fedoroff 亦收到情报，称有两名俄国游民（姓名目前不详）近期在该区域活跃，从机动车上盗窃零件和工具，他们很可能对本案中的工具盗窃负责。

Remarks
(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be
commented on by investigating officer).

At 5 p.m. on the 4/12/39, a telephone message
was received from 341 Woosung Road Japanese piece
goods shop reporting the arrest of a Russian female
for larceny at above shop.

D.P.S. Sameshima and C.D.C.221 and the under-
signed attended and received into custody one named
Maria Kosin, 26, Russian, S/female of N.F.A..

Enquiries made by above detectives ascertained
that at about 4.45 p.m. on the 4/12/39, the above
female together with one other Russian female entered
the shop and were standing at the shop counter select-
ing some woollen jerseys. As their actions appeared to
the shop assistants quite suspicious they kept both
females under observation. Few minutes later the 2nd.
mentioned female suddenly left the shop and then one
of shop assistants named Chiu Zung Ming (沈長明),
noticed that the 1st. mentioned female put one woo-
llen jersey under her overcoat and was about to leave
the shop, when she was stopped by above shop assistant
who found the stolen jersey under her overcoat. She
was taken before the shop keeper and the latter in-
formed the station as already stated above.

On being brought to the station and questioned
the 1st. named accused admitted that she together
with one female known to her as Nadia and whom she
met at about 4 p.m. in a heroin den in Market Street
where they decided to steal something in a Japanese
shop on Woosung Road, proceeded together to the shop

1939年12月4日下午5时，接到吴淞路341号日本布匹店的电话报告，称在该店逮捕了一名涉嫌盗窃的俄国女性。

副巡佐 Sameshima 和第221号中国侦探以及下述签署人前往现场，并将一名名为 Maria Kosin、26岁、俄国人、单身女性、无固定住所（N.F.A.）的人收押。

经上述侦探查询查明，1939年12月4日下午4时45分左右，上述女性与另一名俄国女性进入店内，站在柜台前挑选一些羊毛运动衫。由于她们的举动在店员看来十分可疑，店员便对这两名女性进行监视。几分钟后，第二名提到的女性突然离开商店，随后一名名为沈長明（Chiu Zung Ming）的店员注意到，第一名提到的女性将一件羊毛运动衫塞入大衣下并准备离开商店，此时她被上述店员拦住，店员在其大衣下发现了被盗的运动衫。她被带到店主面前，后者正如上述已陈述的那样通知了捕房。

当第一名被告被带至捕房并接受讯问时，她承认她与一名她称为 Nadia 的女性一起行动，她是下午4点左右在市场街（Market Street）的一个海洛英馆遇见该女子的，她们决定去吴淞路的一家日本商店偷东西，随后一同前往该店

in question where the 2nd. named attempted to steal one woollen jersey from the counter but dropped that jersey on the floor and being afraid that her action was noticed by one of shop assistants left the shop. Then the 1st. accused took that jersey and put same under her overcoat when she was arrested by a shop assistant.

Acting on information received from the 1st. accused detectives succeeded in arresting one Nadejda Kosheleva, 39, s/female, of N.F.A. at about 8.10 p.m. on Range Road near Chapoo Road (now the 2nd. accused). On being brought to the station she was identified by the mentioned shop assistant as an accomplice of the 1st. accused who escaped from the shop prior to the arrest of the 1st. accused.

On being questioned the 2nd. accused admitted that she entered the shop in question with the 1st. accused with the intention to commit a larceny in there.

Written statements were taken from both the accused and will be produced in the Court as exhibits.

Both the accused are well known to Police heroin addicts and admitted that they intended to commit a larceny to obtain some money from the disposal of the stolen property to buy heroine.

Both were charged accordingly and will appear before the S.S.D. Court on the morning of the 5/12/39.

涉案商店，其中第二名被告企图从柜台偷走一件羊毛运动衫，但将运动衫掉在地上，因害怕其行为被某位店员察觉而离开商店。随后第一名被告拿起那件运动衫并塞入其大衣下，此时她被一名店员逮捕。

根据从第一名被告处获得的情报，侦探们成功于晚上8时10分左右在乍浦路（Chapoo Road）附近的 Range Road 逮捕了 Nadejda Kosheleva，39岁，单身女性，无固定住所（N.F.A.）（即现在的第二名被告）。当她被带至捕房时，前述店员指认她是第一名被告的同伙，后者在第一名被告被捕前逃离了商店。

经讯问，第二名被告承认她与第一名被告一起进入涉案商店，意图在那里实施盗窃。

已获取两名被告的书面供词，并将作为证物在法庭出示。

两名被告均为警方熟知的海洛英瘾君子，并承认她们意图实施盗窃，以便通过处置赃物获取钱财购买海洛英。

两人均被相应起诉，并将于1939年12月5日上午出庭受审于特别分部法庭。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of N. Kosheleva.
native of Russia. taken by me.
at Hongkew Stn. on the 4/12/39. and interpreted by D.S.I. Fedoroff.

My name Nadejda Kosheleva, Russian, 39 years, at
present unemployed of not fixed abode. At about 4 p.m. on the
4/12/39, I agreed with one named Maria Kosih, with whom I
met in a heroin den in Youngfong Road, to go to a Japanese
shop on Woosung Road to commit a theft therein.
About 5 p.m. we entered one shop on Woosung Road
corner Qiusan Road and started to select some jerseys lying on
the counter. Then Maria Kosih told me to take one jersey under
my coat but in doing so I dropped the jersey on the floor and
when I picked up the same I noticed that one of shop assistants
was watching me so I immediately left the shop.
This is my true statement signed by me.

Signed:- Kosheleva.

以下是 N. Kosheleva 的供词。
俄国人。由我于1939年12月4日在虹口捕房录取。
由警佐 Fedoroff 翻译。

我叫 Nadejda Kosheleva，俄国人，39岁，目前失业，无固定住所。1939年12月4日下午4点左右，我与一名名为 Maria Kosih 的女子达成协议，我是在元芳路（Youngfong Road）的一个海洛英馆遇见她的，我们要去吴淞路的一家日本商店实施盗窃。
下午5点左右，我们进入吴淞路与秋山路（Qiusan Road）(音译)转角处的一家商店，开始挑选放在柜台上的一些运动衫。随后 Maria Kosih 让我把一件运动衫藏在大衣下，但在操作过程中我将运动衫掉在地上，当我捡起它时，我注意到一名店员正在盯着我，所以我立即离开了商店。
这是我的真实供词，由我签署。

签署：- Kosheleva。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Maria Kosih.
native of Russia taken by me
at Hongkew Stn. on the 4/12/39 and interpreted by D.S.I. Fedoroff.

My name Maria, Kosih, 21 years, Russian, unemployed
of not fixed abode.
At about 4 p.m. on the 4/12/39, one female known to
me as Nadejda Kosheleva and whom I met in a heroin den in
Market Street told me if I am willing to go with her to a
Japanese shop on Woosung Road to commit a theft in that shop.
At about 5 p.m. even date we entered one shop on
Woosung Road corner of Quinsan Road where N. Kosheleva, who
speaks Japanese, started to talk with a shop assistant re prices
of goods and when the shop assistant left her she stole one
woollen jersey from the counter and put same under her coat.
But later on she put that jersey back on the counter stating
that she suspects that Japanese shop assistant was watching her.
Then she left the shop and I took that jersey myself and was
arrested by shop assistants who handed me over to Hongkew
Station.

It is my true statement signed by me.

Signed:- Maria Kosih.

警方调查报告。

以下是 Maria Kosih 的供词。
俄国人。由我于1939年12月4日在虹口捕房录取。
由警佐 Fedoroff 翻译。

我叫 Maria Kosih，21岁，俄国人，失业，无固定住所。
1939年12月4日下午4点左右，一名我称为 Nadejda Kosheleva 的女性（我是在市场街的一个海洛英馆遇见她的）问我是否愿意跟她去吴淞路的一家日本商店在那家店里实施盗窃。
当天下午5点左右，我们进入吴淞路与 Quinsan Road (音译) 转角处的一家商店，会说日语的 N. Kosheleva 开始就商品价格与一名店员交谈，当店员离开她时，她从柜台偷了一件羊毛运动衫并塞入大衣下。
但后来她又把那件运动衫放回柜台，声称她怀疑那名日本店员正在监视她。
随后她离开了商店，我自己拿起了那件运动衫，并被店员逮捕，店员将我移交给虹口捕房。

这是我的真实供词，由我签署。

签署：- Maria Kosih。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Arrest of one male Russian for looting O.O.L.
----------------------------------------------

At 5.30 p.m. on the 18/12/39, in response to a telephone message received from J.N.L. Party, P.S.836 brought to the station from Japanese Consular Police Sub-station, Woosung Rd. one Valentine Sorogin, 27, Russian, s/unemployed, of N.F.A. who was arrested by members of J.N.L.P. at about 12 noon 18/12/39 in one of empty houses off Dixwell Rd O.O.L. for looting fire wood from therein.

Enquiries made by D.S.I. Fedoroff and the above suspect on being questioned at the station admitted the offense as stated above.

It was ascertained that the house in question is situated off Dixwell Rd near Kashing Rd Bridge O.O.L. and is an evacuated and partly ruined Chinese dwelling house.

The suspect was carefully interrogated re other similar offenses committed in the Settlement but strongly denied having committed any crime.

The suspect is well known to Police as heroin addict who obtains money for his living and for buying heroin by disposing of fire wood and old iron scraps which he picks up amongst the ruins in Chapel O.O.L.

逮捕一名抢劫越界筑路区（O.O.L.）的俄国男子。
----------------------------------------------

1939年12月18日下午5时30分，接日本海军陆战队（J.N.L. Party）电话通知，第836号巡捕从吴淞路日本领事警察分驻所带至捕房一名 Valentine Sorogin，27岁，俄国人，无业，无固定住址（N.F.A.）。此人于1939年12月18日中午12时许，在狄思威路（Dixwell Rd）外越界筑路区（O.O.L.）的一间空屋内，因从中抢劫木柴而被日本海军陆战队成员逮捕。

经 D.S.I. Fedoroff 调查，上述嫌疑人在捕房受讯时承认了上述罪行。

经查，涉案房屋位于越界筑路区（O.O.L.）嘉善路（Kashing Rd）桥附近的狄思威路（Dixwell Rd）旁，是一栋已疏散且部分损毁的中式住宅。

就其在租界内犯下的其他类似罪行对嫌疑人进行了仔细讯问，但其强烈否认犯有任何罪行。

警方熟知该嫌疑人为海洛因成瘾者，他通过在闸北（Chapel）越界筑路区的废墟中捡拾木柴和废铁出售，以获取生活费和购买海洛因的资金。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

On 21-9-39, I. Paromeeff (6th accused) was brought before the S.S.D. Court and was ordered to be detained until 4-10-39, to be tried together with the suspects previously arrested.

The 6th accused has one previous conviction.

It should be mentioned that at the time when the original arrest of the suspects was made it was known that the 2nd, 4th and 5th accused were seen often visiting a Russian prostitute, residing at 6 Park Lane, the Boarding House owned by one Mrs. Antonoff (Russian), therefore immediately after apprehension of the suspects the above place was visited and room occupied by the prostitute was searched.

Several pawn tickets were found concealed behind the wall papers and under carpet and the occupant of the room was questioned re this, but she strongly denied having any knowledge of same saying that the tickets were placed by the suspects without her knowledge This could be believed for the reason that previous to the arrest of the suspects same prostitute had approached the undersigned and passed certain information re activities of the gang. The prostitute in question and 4th and 5th accused are heroin addicts and it was also learned that their expenses in narcotic

1939年9月21日，I. Paromeeff（第六被告）被带至特区地方法院，并被命令羁押至1939年10月4日，与此前逮捕的嫌疑人一同受审。

第六被告有一次前科。

需要提及的是，在最初逮捕嫌疑人时，已知第二、第四和第五被告经常拜访一名居住在派克弄6号（Park Lane）的俄国妓女，该寄宿处由一位 Antonoff 太太（俄国人）所有，因此在逮捕嫌疑人后立即走访了上述地点，并搜查了该妓女居住的房间。

在墙纸后面和地毯下发现了几张当票，就此讯问了房间 occupant（居住者），但她强烈否认知情，称这些当票是嫌疑人在她不知情的情况下放置的。这一点可信，因为在嫌疑人被捕之前，同一名妓女曾接触下文签署人，并提供了一些关于该团伙活动的信息。该妓女以及第四和第五被告均为海洛因成瘾者，还获悉他们在毒品方面的花费

One Mr. K. Kohara the proprietor of the above
company was interviewed and it was learned that during
the night of 14-8-39, his premises had been broken into
and one "Underwood" typewriter value $500.00 had been
stolen. The entry was gained by forcing the front door
with some sharp instrument. The 4th and 5th accused
admitted that at about 4 a.m. 15-8-39, they broke into
the complainant's premises and stole the machine. Same
morning the stolen machine was taken by the 2nd accused
to the French Concession and pawned in one of the pawn
shops for $65.00. On same date the 2nd accused had
redeemed the typewriter and sold for $250.00 to one
named V. Curilo, Persian merchant, residing Apt. 266
B'Well Court, 591/178 B'Well Road.

The following day V. Curilo had discovered that
the machine was not in order and could not be used by
him, but being in need of money he had pawned the
typewriter for $250.00 at the Hung Te Pawn Shop at
No.7 Rue Pere Robert. V. Curilo had produced the
receipt given to him by the 2nd accused and later
admitted the deal. The typewriter recovered and
further charge in connection with this case will be
preferred against the accused.

5th further Charge against the 4th and 5th accused.
3rd further Charge against the 2nd accused.

Brief particulars of the case are as follows:

On 26-7-39, Mr. R.W.G. Brook, House No.9 Lane 70
Tunsin Road reported larceny of his m/car licence 8814
value $1,000.00 from the compound of the Country Club,
B'Well Road.

On 27-7-39, a telephone message was received from
the Muirhead Road Licensing Depot informing that the
m/car in question was brought by a Japanese one named
Shibaishi Mushishika to the above Depot to be licensed.
From enquiries made it was ascertained that S.
Mushishika had bought the m/car for $840.00 from a
Russian named I. Shirovsky employed as a watchman in
one of the demolished houses on E. Hanbury Road and
who already had absconded at that time. The 4th accused
stated that at about 7 p.m. 26-7-39, whilst walking
along B'Well Road he observed a number of m/cars parked
outside the Country Club and unattended.

1939年7月26日，邓脱路（Tunsin Road）70弄9号的 R.W.G. Brook 先生报案，称其牌照号为8814、价值1,000.00元的机动车在倍开尔路（B'Well Road）乡村俱乐部的院落内被盗。

1939年7月27日，收到缪尔黑德路（Muirhead Road）车辆监理所的电话通知，称涉案机动车由一名叫 Shibaishi Mushishika（音译）的日本人带到上述监理所办理执照。经查询查明，S. Mushishika 以840.00元从一名叫 I. Shirovsky（音译）的俄罗斯人手中购买了该机动车，此人受雇于汉璧礼路东一处已拆除房屋担任看守，且当时已潜逃。第四被告称，1939年7月26日晚7点左右，他在沿倍开尔路行走时，观察到乡村俱乐部外停放着多辆无人看管的机动车。

of 8-9-39, they had broken into the "ISSA" tea room and

No hope of recovery.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

On the 20/9/39 the five suspects appeared before the S.S.D.Court and after the trial the case was remanded until the 4/10/39.

The 1st. and 3rd. suspects were ordered to be released.

Information was received by the undersigned that the 4th. suspect beside the cases mentioned in diary 2 of this report was also responsible for larceny of one m/car value $1000.00 (Ch.Rd.F.I.R.1080/39) and that one named Ivan Parameeff, 39, Russian, residing at 139 Ford Lane concerned in this crime. The m/car had been stolen between 5 and 7 p.m. 26/7/39 and disposed to a Japanese at 9 p.m. the same date.

At about 9.45 a.m. 20/9/39 I. Parameeff was arrested by the undersigned at his home.

On being brought to the station and questioned the suspect admitted riding together with 4th. suspect in the stolen m/car on that particular day but strongly denied taking any part in the disposal of the machine.

On 21/9/39, he will be brought before the S.S. D.Court on a Writ of Detention until 4/10/39 for the purpose of making further enquiries.

At first Boku could not give any reasons for arresting of Russian but eventually stated this Russian being connected with two more Russians tried to obtain from him a large sum of money by fraudulent means.

From further enquiries made by the detectives it was learned that the Koreans allegation is correct and it was also learned that same Korean with an unknown Japanese were planning to rob the Russians of a large quantity of heroin.

The Korean gives the following statement. A few days ago he met an old Russian who offered to him for sale a large quantity of heroin to the value of $15,000.00. SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Vatzlaw Philipovich Sikorsky
native of Warsaw, Poland taken by me
at Shanghai on the 11/12/39 and interpreted by D.S.I. Beloshenko.

I am Vatzlaw Philipovich Sikorsky, 35 years of age,
Polish, barber by profession and at present working in my
own barber shop at 833/12 Ave. Joffre.
At about 3 pm 7/12/39 I was on my way to Seward Rd
to see one of my friends by name Shirokoff and when I was
waiting for the m/bus outside the Hongkew Market, suddenly
I was approached by two Japanese one was wearing military
uniform and another was in civilian clothes. They had arrest-
ed me and brought to the Police Station.
Same day I was handed over to some Japanese Military
Headquarters and two days later I was removed to some Japanese
Jail situated somewhere near Range Road.
On 11/12/39 I was handed over to the Hongkew Police
Station. During first two days of my detention I was ques-
tioned re something but as I could not understand the lan-
guage I was beaten with the fists, butt of rifle and sticks.
On my removal to the jail the questioning was continued with
assistance (as interpreter) from a Russian prisoner when I was asked
if I had committed any theft. Having no knowledge of any
crime I did not admit anything and was assaulted again.
This is my true statement signed by me.

(Signed) V.Sikorsky.

警方调查报告。

以下为瓦茨拉夫·菲利波维奇·西科尔斯基（Vatzlaw Philipovich Sikorsky）的陈述，此人系波兰华沙人，由我于1939年12月11日在上海录取，由分区督察贝洛申科（Beloshenko）翻译。

我是瓦茨拉夫·菲利波维奇·西科尔斯基，35岁，波兰籍，职业为理发师，目前在霞飞路833/12号我自己的理发店工作。
1939年12月7日下午3点左右，我正前往西华德路（Seward Rd.）去见一位名叫 Shirokoff 的朋友，当我在虹口市场外等候无轨电车时，突然有两名日本人走近我，其中一人身穿军装，另一人身穿便服。他们逮捕了我，并将我带到警察局。
同日，我被移交给某日本军事总部，两天后，我被转移到位于朗格路（Range Road）附近某处的日本监狱。
1939年12月11日，我被移交给虹口捕房。在被拘留的头两天里，我就某些事情受到讯问，但由于我听不懂语言，我遭到拳打、枪托击打和棍棒殴打。
在我被转移到监狱后，讯问继续进行，并由一名俄国囚犯协助（作为翻译），当时他们问我是否犯有任何盗窃罪。由于我对任何犯罪行为均不知情，我没有承认任何事项，并再次遭到殴打。
这是我的真实陈述，由我签署。

（签名）V. Sikorsky。

| RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Arrest of one named V. Sikorsky, Polish by the members of the Japanese Navy Landing Party (Northern Area Headquarters).

At 3 p.m. 7-12-39, Sgt. Morita of the Japanese Navy Landing Party accompanied by his informant (name unknown, believed to be a Chinese) brought to this station one named V. Sikorsky, 35, Polish, residing at 883/12 Av. Joffre, whom they had arrested outside Hongkew Market on suspicion being a pick-pocket.

V. Sikorsky was observed by the above Sgt. standing alone near the m/bus stop. At first Sgt. Morita requested the S.M.P. to deal with the suspect accordingly but later changed his mind stating that he will consult his superior officer and inform the station re disposal of this suspect. About 20 minutes later a telephone message was received from the Japanese Navy Landing Party requesting handing over the suspect to them as he was brought to the Hongkew Police Station by mistake. They were informed that the suspect is wanted by this station for enquiries as being connected in case of pocket-picking (see H. 一名名为 V. Sikorsky 的波兰人被日本海军陆战队（北区司令部）成员逮捕。

1939年12月7日下午3时，日本海军陆战队的森田（Morita）警佐在其线人（姓名不详，据信为中国人）的陪同下，将一名名为 V. Sikorsky、35岁、波兰籍、居住于霞飞路883/12号的男子带至本捕房，此人因涉嫌扒窃在虹口市场外被捕。

上述警佐观察到 V. Sikorsky 独自站在无轨电车站附近。起初，森田警佐要求上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）相应处理该嫌疑人，但随后改变主意，称他将请示上级军官，并就如何处置该嫌疑人通知本捕房。约20分钟后，收到日本海军陆战队打来的电话，要求将嫌疑人移交给他们，因为将他带到虹口捕房是个错误。警方告知他们，本捕房因该嫌疑人涉及扒窃案件（参见 H. F.I.R. 1071/39）而需要对其进行讯问，但他们（日本海军陆战队）重复了其要求，并通知侦探，几名日本海军陆战队成员正在前来提取嫌疑人的路上。

“C”分区督察长和“C”分区副督察长已获悉上述情况

Date 24 2 39

Extract from a book entitled "THE GOAL OF JAPANESE
EXPANSION" published by Tatsuo Kawai in December, 1938.

CONCLUSION

Dawn of a New Asia.

That the Sino-Japanese problem should have been
thrown into the maelstrom of armed conflict is a most
deplorable and shameful thing for Asia. It is an
indelible blot on the history of the Asiatic race.

Nevertheless, if the China Af_air has brought a
black night upon Asia, the dawn of a new era is not far
ahead. In North China and the Yangtze Valley, wherever the
Sun flag,waves side by side with the five-coloured flag, we
see already signs of a new order for which the Japanese
Government's statement of January 16 is a solemn pledge.
The longer the Kuomintang Government persist in their
avowed opposition, the wider will be extended the territories
over which shall wave the Rising Sun and the old emblem of the
Chinese Republic. It may be that the pitiable and stubborn
manoeuvres of Chiang Kai-shek are nothing but a necessary
step towards the consolidation of Asia - a sort of churning
process that is to bring about a new and more solid Asiatic
unity.

At any rate, for this catastrophic development of
Sino-Japanese relations, Japan is not entirely free of blame.
Seeing which way the Kuomintang Government was drifting in
the turbulent waters of China's internal politics, she could
have acted, perhaps, in time to prevent Chiang Kai-shek from
dragging her into the abyss. For this failure on her part,
Japan owes an apology to mankind, but at the same time she is
obliged to wield her sword to remove all the forces of
treachery, iniquity and ruthless domination.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 24-2-39）
（批：acc.B. 342 342 S.L. C.J.L.K. Koll yfco...）
page_data.zh:
地点：
编号 S. H. (1). 8509
日期 1939年2月24日

摘录自川井达雄 (Tatsuo Kawai) 于1938年12月出版的题为《日本扩张的目标》一书。

结论

新亚洲的黎明。

中日问题陷入武装冲突的漩涡，这对亚洲而言是最令人遗憾和羞耻的事情。这是亚细亚种族历史上不可磨灭的污点。

然而，如果“中国事变”给亚洲带来了黑夜，那么新时代的黎明已不远矣。在华北和长江流域， wherever the Sun flag,waves side by side with the five-coloured flag, we see already signs of a new order for which the Japanese Government's statement of January 16 is a solemn pledge. The longer the Kuomintang Government persist in their avowed opposition, the wider will be extended the territories over which shall wave the Rising Sun and the old emblem of the Chinese Republic. It may be that the pitiable and stubborn manoeuvres of Chiang Kai-shek are nothing but a necessary step towards the consolidation of Asia - a sort of churning process that is to bring about a new and more solid Asiatic unity.

无论如何，对于中日关系的这一灾难性发展，日本并非完全没有责任。鉴于国民党政府在中国内部政治的湍流中漂移的方向，她本可以及时采取行动，或许能阻止蒋介石将她拖入深渊。为此失败，日本欠人类一个道歉，但与此同时，她有义务挥舞利剑，铲除所有背叛、不义和残酷统治的力量。

（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处 特别处 1939年2月24日）
（批注：acc.B. 342 342 S.L. C.J.L.K. Koll yfco...）

page_data.en:
- 2 -

The Kuomintang Government have feverishly and
frantically resorted to every possible device to enlist
outside assistance and to invite the intervention of third
Powers in a war which they themselves had started. The
machinery of the League of Nations was set in motion. The
Nine Power Treaty was invoked. The representatives of the
European Powers interested in preserving a quasi-colonial
China were readily led by false propaganda into outbursts of
sentimentalism. They failed utterly to take a long view
of things, in the interests of the real peace and tranquility
of Asia and the common welfare of mankind. Is it that a cultural
unification or fusion is impossible of attainment without war?
"Heaven lies", said Mohammed, "in the shadow of the sword".
It is the irony of fate that Japan's quest for peaceful co-
operation should have ended in open hostilities. It is to
be hoped that the present affair shall not prove to be only
one scene in a still more terrible tragedy - the conflict of
the East and West with China as the stage.

The Anglo-Saxons with their admirable practical
spirit may view the China Affair as an inevitable outcome
of Japan's expansion, which is bound to monopolize the field
to the exclusion of their own interests. Indeed, the Japan
Axes, representing the growth of the nation in the northern
Pacific, does, Proteus-like, assume varied forms in the
imagination of different observers.

Japan's position as the stabilizing force in East
Asia carries in itself a mission of historical significance
which must cause the natural extinction of the Nine Power
Treaty. In other words, between 1922, when that treaty was
concluded, and to-day, when Japan's axes have been completed,
there have occurred drastic changes the world over, and it
is not possible to settle any Asiatic problem without recogniz-
ing Japan's new position in the Far Eastern equation.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

国民政府狂热而疯狂地诉诸一切可能的手段，以争取外部援助，并邀请第三方势力介入这场由他们自己发动的战争。国际联盟的机制被启动。《九国公约》被援引。那些关心维持半殖民地状态中国的欧洲列强代表，轻易地被虚假宣传所误导，陷入感伤主义的爆发之中。他们完全未能从亚洲真正的和平与安宁以及人类共同福祉的长远角度来审视事态。难道没有战争就无法实现文化的统一或融合吗？穆罕默德曾说：“天堂在剑影之下”。具有讽刺意味的是，日本寻求和平合作的努力最终以公开敌对行动告终。希望当前的事态不会证明只是一场更可怕悲剧中的一幕——即以中国为舞台的东西方冲突。

盎格鲁-撒克逊人以其令人钦佩的务实精神，或许会将“中国事变”视为日本扩张的必然结果，这种扩张注定要垄断该领域，从而排斥他们自身的利益。事实上，代表北太平洋国家成长的日本轴心（Japan Axes），在不同观察者的想象中，确实像普罗透斯（Proteus）一样呈现出各种形态。

日本作为东亚稳定力量的地位，本身就承载着具有历史意义的使命，这必然导致《九国公约》的自然消亡。换言之，从1922年该条约签订之时到今天，当日本的轴心已经确立之际，世界各地发生了剧烈的变化，如果不承认日本在远东格局中的新地位，就不可能解决任何亚洲问题。

page_data.en:
- 3 -
from the state of a quasi-colony of Occidental Powers.
Asia should realize to its noble obligation to promote its
unique and sublime spiritual life and to contribute to the
advancement of mankind through free and whole-hearted co-
operation with the rest of the world. The spirit of Asia
awoke from its long sleep of centuries first in Japan
through contact with Western civilization. The emergence
of Japan as a new living force marked only the opening page
of the history of the Asiatic race. With the China Affair
begins its main chapter.
Thus, the military operations that Japan was
compelled to take in China should be looked upon as a
manifestation of the creative power of the Asiatic spirit,
from which we may well expect the consummation of a constructive
peace. The China Affair, which has rudely shaken the world,
is destined to prove the very centre of the stream in the
swift current of world history.
The Brussels Conference, which was summoned for
the purpose of settling the Sino-Japanese conflict, served
as an antidote against the poison of European imperialism
which has paralyzed China since the time of the Opium War.
It is time the Nine Power Treaty was re-examined and diagnosed
to clarify its basic pollution.
The Asiatic peoples should cast aside all the
selfish individualism and materialism of Europe. They
should embrace one common faith of Asia and live an Asiatic
life. The Confucianism that originated in China and was
perfected in Japan, as if anticipating the needs of to-day,
long ago laid down the stern and solemn code of "self-mastery
and return to decorum". Herein lies the common ideal for
Japan, Manchukuo and China.
Through the mastery of self and the purification
of group life, all the nations of Asia may be united in the
Asiatic spirit and under Asiatic order and discipline, while
page_data.zh:
- 3 -
摆脱西方列强半殖民地的状态。亚洲应认识到其促进其独特而崇高的精神生活、并通过与世界其他地区自由且全心全意的合作来推动人类进步的崇高义务。亚洲的精神首先在日本通过与西方文明的接触而从数个世纪的长眠中苏醒。日本作为一种新生力量的出现，仅标志着亚细亚种族历史的开篇。随着“中国事变”的开始，其主要篇章由此展开。
因此，日本被迫在中国采取的军事行动应被视为亚洲精神创造力的体现，我们可以从中期待建设性和平的实现。震撼世界的“中国事变”注定将成为世界历史急速潮流中的中心。
为解决中日冲突而召开的布鲁塞尔会议，起到了对抗自鸦片战争以来使中国瘫痪的欧洲帝国主义毒药的解毒剂作用。现在是重新审查和诊断《九国公约》以澄清其基本污染的时候了。
亚洲人民应摒弃欧洲所有的自私个人主义和物质主义。他们应拥抱共同的亚洲信仰，过一种亚洲式的生活。起源于中国并在日本得到完善的儒家思想，仿佛预见了今日的需求，早已制定了“克己复礼”这一严厉而庄严的准则。此处蕴藏着日本、满洲国和中国的共同理想。

Subject (in full) Anti Municipal Council Poster.

Made by Sub-Inspector Dow Forwarded by R.C.Mac... Officer in charge.

Sir,

I beg to report that I was informed yesterday a.m. 22-2-39
that there was an anti Municipal poster posted on the outside
of the Co-operative Society Building show window at the inter-
section of Dixwell and North Szechuen Roads wording as far as
could be ascertained was as follows;-

"Municipal Council was powerless and could not cope with
the terrorism south of the Creek".

I accompanied J.D.S. 42 to the place but the poster had
been torn down.

（批：East）

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,

William Dow.
Sub-Inspector.

pamphlets in the Settlement
Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

（批：Is this An Ching League activity? E.）

On the afternoon of January 23, 1939, a large number of coloured pamphlets were found scattered on Nanking Road in the vicinity of the Sincere, Wing On and Sun Sun Department stores. These pamphlets contain Domei News Agency reports on such subjects as anti-British labour agitation in Burma; breakdown of the morale of the Chinese armed forces; and press criticism against third powers' assistance to the Chiang Kai-shek Government. A copy of the pamphlet together with a full translation is attached herewith.

"ANTI-BRITISH FEELING RIFE IN BURMA - GENERAL STRIKE
TO TAKE PLACE IN A FEW DAYS - HARBOUR AND RAILWAY
EMPLOYEES LIKELY TO PARTICIPATE IN THE STRIKE -
THIS ACTION MAY BRING ABOUT THE END TO THE
TRANSPORTATION OF MUNITIONS TO YUNNAN"

Rangoon, January 18 (Domei) - Since December last
year, anti-British labour troubles which broke out at
various places in Burma have also affected employees of
government railways.

On the night of January 17, the railway employees
held a general meeting. As the situation was found to be
critical, the authorities prosecuted leaders of the Strike
Group. Nevertheless, the strike movements at various
places have become worse and it is inevitable that a general
strike will take place in a few days. If the general
strike commences, the harbour and the railway employees will
certainly participate, whereupon the transportation of
military weapons and ammunition as well as supplies for
railway reconstruction to Yunnan may be stopped.

The authorities are prosecuting daily some ten
directors of the Dispute Group. On January 18, two
supporters of the movement who came from India in an
attempt to participate in the movement of Indian labourers
were immediately prosecuted.

"ANTI-BRITISH MOVEMENT IN RANGOON BECOMES WORSE -
TERRORIST INCIDENT HAS TAKEN PLACE - BURMA
PREMIER'S MOTOR CAR BOMBED"

Rangoon, January 20 (Domei) - The strike
situation of the anti-British clique in Rangoon has become
worse. At 6 p.m. on January 19, a hand grenade was thrown
at the motor car of Dr. Ba Maw, the Premier of Burma.
page_data.zh:
“缅甸反英情绪高涨——数日内将举行总罢工——港口和铁路员工可能参与罢工——此举可能导致向云南运输军火中断”

仰光，1月18日（同盟社）——自去年12月以来，在缅甸各地爆发的反英劳工纠纷也影响了政府铁路的员工。

1月17日晚，铁路员工举行了一次全体会议。由于局势被认为十分危急，当局起诉了罢工团体的领导人。尽管如此，各地的罢工运动愈演愈烈，数日内发生总罢工已不可避免。如果总罢工开始，港口和铁路员工肯定会参与，届时向云南运输军事武器、弹药以及铁路重建物资可能会停止。

当局每天起诉约十名纠纷团体的负责人。1月18日，两名从印度前来试图参与印度劳工运动的运动支持者立即被起诉。

“仰光的反英运动恶化——发生恐怖事件——缅甸总理的汽车遭炸弹袭击”

仰光，1月20日（同盟社）——仰光反英派系的罢工局势恶化。1月19日下午6时，有人向缅甸总理巴莫博士（Dr. Ba Maw）的汽车投掷了一枚手榴弹。

page_data.en:
(2)

"KUOMINTANG TROOPS WITHDRAW VOLUNTARILY -
FIGHTING STRENGTH WEAK"

Special correspondence from Hankow dated January
15 (United Press of China) - As the Kuomintang troops
have lost confidence, their fighting spirit has become
extraordinarily weak recently. Most of them have aban-
doned and withdrawn from their defence lines voluntarily,
without regard to orders of the Kuomintang Government, while
those army commanders and divisional commanders who are
disappointed at the future of the Kuomintang Government have
hidden their munitions and detained the pay and rations of
soldiers in the interests of their own future.

"EVENING PAPER IN GENEVA CRITIQUES ACTION OF
VARIOUS POWERS IN SUPPORTING CHIANG KAI-SHEK"

Geneva, January 19 (Domei) - The "Jah-mai-erh",
an evening paper in Geneva on January 18 published the
following comment, criticising the action of various Powers
in supporting Chiang Kai-shek.

"It is a very dangerous policy of the various
Powers to use every effort to make Japan exhausted and grant
concessions in connection with the China Incident. The
longer the war of resistance by the Kuomintang authorities
lasts, the firmer Japan's attitude will be, and the results
as expected by the British and American Powers will not be
forthcoming."
page_data.zh:
(2)

“国民党军队自愿撤退——战斗力薄弱”

汉口1月15日专电（中国联合通讯社）——由于国民党军队失去信心，其战斗精神近期变得异常薄弱。大多数人不顾国民党政府的命令，自愿放弃并撤出防线；而那些对国民党政府前途感到失望的军长和师长，为了自己未来的利益，藏匿了军火，并扣留了士兵的薪饷和口粮。

“日内瓦晚报批评列强支持蒋介石的行动”

日内瓦，1月19日（同盟社）——日内瓦晚报《雅迈尔》（Jah-mai-erh）于1月18日发表评论，批评列强支持蒋介石的行动。

“列强竭力使日本疲惫不堪，并在‘中国事变’相关问题上做出让步，这是一种非常危险的政策。国民党当局的抵抗战争持续越久，日本的态度就越坚定，英美列强所预期的结果也不会出现。”

CHINA PRESS.

JAN 25 1939

Anti-British
Propaganda
Found Here

Detectives of the Special Branch,
Shanghai Municipal Police Head-
quarters, are today continuing their
investigations in connection with
the distribution of anti-British
handbills on Nanking and Yu Ya
Ching Roads Monday afternoon.
Only a few of the handbills were
circulated but several copies fell
into the hands of the police
authorities. One of the leaflets
made the bold statement that
"Anti-British sentiment is growing
in Burma and a general strike will
be declared shortly."
The leaflets were distributed by
a single Chinese, according to all
available information. The fellow
managed to disappear, however, be-
fore the police arrived on the scene.
He is believed to have been merely
the hireling of some local organ-
ization trying to engage in anti-
British propaganda in this city.

（批：File 85/1  S.B. R 25/1）

《字林西报》

1939年1月25日

在此发现
反英宣传

上海公共租界警务处总部特别科的侦探今天继续调查周一中午在南京路和虞洽卿路分发反英传单一事。散发的传单数量不多，但有几份落入警方手中。其中一份传单大胆宣称：“缅甸的反英情绪日益增长，不久将宣布总罢工。”

根据所有现有信息，传单是由一名中国人分发的。然而，此人在警察到达现场前设法逃脱。据信他仅仅是某个试图在本市进行反英宣传的地方组织的雇工。

（批注：档案 85/1 特别科登记处 1月25日）

Date August 6, 1938.
Subject Male Chinese youth arrested in possession of anti-Chiang Kai Shek
pamphlets - released.
Made by D.S. Pitts. Forwarded by C. Crawford. D.I.

Chu Yue Fah, aged 16, a native of Yangchow, who
was arrested during the evening of August 4, 1938 by
a plain clothes search party operating from Sinza Station,
for being in possession of some 300 copies of an anti-
Chiang Kai Shek pamphlet, was released at 4.15 p.m.
August 5 in accordance with the instructions of the D.C.
(Special Branch). Before being permitted to leave
Sinza Station he was severely cautioned as to his future
behaviour in the Settlement and warned that any repetition
of the offence would be drastically dealt with.

D.S. Pitts

Sinza
4th August, 38.
1

Male Chinese arrested in possession of pamphlets.

At 8.15 p.m. on 4/8/38 D.S.I. Read, in charge of a plain clothes search party, arrested on Sinza Road near Wenchow Road, a male Chinese named Chu Yue Fah (朱月發), 16, Yangchow, S/Apprentice, No. 3 Wo Sing Li, Tsau Ka Doo, in possession of a bundle of pamphlets of an anti Chiang Kai Shek nature wrapped in a Japanese newspaper. The following is a translation of the pamphlets:-

"Advice to Shanghai Citizens.
We have suffered for a long period under the rule of Chiang's Government. The people are in a miserable state because of exorbitant taxes. Since 1927, Chiang has devoted himself to various atrocious activities to the great dissatisfaction of the public. After the outbreak of the August 13th Incident, Chiang advocated resistance against the Japanese, and adopted a 'scorched earth' policy in co-operation with the Communists. Central China, which is the richest area of our country has suffered unprecedented losses. Industries have been destroyed and people killed. Recently, Communists and members of the "Blue Shirts" were despatched to Shanghai for the purpose of carrying out assassinations. A number of wise and educated people who were alleged to be traitors have been killed. Assassins have done everything in their power to create a reign of terror. For instance, a girl of 18 years of age was also killed in connection with the murder which took place at Doong Shing Lur Restaurant. Refugee merchants were attacked in connection with the case which occurred in the Sun Sun Hotel. Being bribed by Chiang's Government, various newspapers published false news stating that these outrages were made to eliminate traitors. However, the facts have already been brought to the notice of the public.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 5.8.38）

D.S.P.K
Q. 5/8

一名中国男子因持有传单被捕。

1938年8月4日晚上8点15分，便衣搜查队负责人警司里德（D.S.I. Read）在静安寺路近温州路处，逮捕了一名名为朱月發的中国男子，16岁，扬州人，学徒，住址曹家渡伍胜里3号。该男子持有一捆用日文报纸包裹的反蒋介石性质传单。传单译文如下：-

“告上海市民书。
我们长期遭受蒋政府统治之苦。由于苛捐杂税，人民处于悲惨境地。自1927年以来，蒋介石从事各种暴行，引起公众极大不满。八一三事变爆发后，蒋介石主张抗日，并与共产党合作采取‘焦土’政策。我国最富庶的华中地区遭受了前所未有的损失。工业被毁，人民被杀。最近，共产党人和‘蓝衣社’成员被派往上海，旨在进行暗杀活动。许多被指控为汉奸的明智且有学识的人士遭到杀害。刺客们竭尽全力制造恐怖统治。例如，在东兴楼餐馆发生的谋杀案中，一名18岁的女孩也被杀害。在新新旅馆发生的案件中，难民商人遭到袭击。受蒋政府收买，各家报纸发布虚假新闻，称这些暴行是为了铲除汉奸。然而，事实已为公众所知。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处特科 1938年8月5日）

DSPK

Section 1, Special Branch
REPORT
File No. 8509
Sld/ph, 8 38
Date August 4th 19 38.

Subject Anti-Chiang Kai-shek Propaganda.

Made by Inspector Shih Ssu-chien Forwarded by C. Crawford. J.C.

Forwarded herewith is a copy of leaflet of an anti-Chiang Kai-shek nature, entitled "Advice to Shanghai Citizens", which was found on Robison Road, having been thrown from an East-bound trolley 'bus at about 7 p.m. on August 3. This leaflet which gives no source of origin, bitterly denounces General Chiang Kai-shek for having sent to Shanghai a gang of terrorists. A translation follows:-

"Advice to Shanghai Citizens:

We have long been victims of the atrocity of Chiang's regime. Taxes are extremely heavy and people are tired of existence. Ever since traitor Chiang came into power in 1927, cases of corruption have been prevalent in officialdom. Following the August 13th incident, the Chiang regime adopted the so-called scorched-earth policy and, as a result, the most prosperous districts in Central China have been destroyed and all business disrupted. At present a number of blue shirts and communists are being sent to Shanghai to carry out terroristic activities. These acts are conducted under the guise of disposing of traitors, but those who have been assassinated were, in fact, good and intelligent citizens. They even deliberately killed an innocent girl of 16 in the Dong Hsing Lao Restaurant and attacked a refugee merchant in the Sun Sun Hotel without any justification. The greater part of the local press, being subsidised by Chiang's regime, has attempted to conceal the real facts by naming these activities as "Traitor removing acts". As these terrorists intend to ruin Shanghai,

由施思坚督察（Inspector Shih Ssu-chien）制作 经 J.C. 克劳福德（C. Crawford）转呈。

现随函附上一份反蒋介石性质的传单副本，题为“告上海市民书”，该传单于8月3日晚7点左右从一辆东行电车巴士上抛出，在罗别根路被发现。这份未注明出处的传单严厉谴责蒋介石将军派遣一伙恐怖分子前往上海。译文如下：-

“告上海市民书：

我们长期受害于蒋政权的暴行。赋税极重，民不聊生。自卖国贼蒋介石1927年掌权以来，官场腐败盛行。八一三事变后，蒋政权采取了所谓的焦土政策，导致华中最繁荣的地区被毁，所有商业中断。目前，一批蓝衣社成员和共产党人被派往上海进行恐怖活动。这些行为打着处置汉奸的幌子，但被暗杀的实际上是善良且聪明的公民。他们甚至故意在东兴老餐馆杀害了一名16岁的无辜女孩，并无端攻击了新新旅馆的一名难民商人。本地大部分报刊受蒋政权资助，试图将这些活动称为“除奸行动”以掩盖事实真相。由于这些恐怖分子意图毁坏上海，
