SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S. 1, Special Branch.
REPORT
File No. 8500
Date August 2, 19 38.

Subject Finding of an anti-Government booklet.

Made by D.I. Pan Lien Pih Forwarded by C. Crawford. D. I.

At 7.35 a.m. on 1.8.38, a booklet bearing as its title "Knowledge for the Citizens" (國民須知) was found in front of the Temple of the Queen of Heaven on North Honan Road near North Soochow Road. This booklet, the text of which seriously attacks the National Government and its "Scorched Earth" policy, is highly anti-Koumintang in nature, and is believed to be a piece of propaganda of the "Reformed Government". The following is a list of its sub-titles:-

1. Why Japan wants to destroy the Chiang Kai-shek Regime.
2. Hankow Government under the rule of the Chinese Communist Party.
3. The "Five Gods of Wealth" in China.
4. A comment on the "Scorched Earth" Policy by Mr. Wen Tsung-yao.
5. The downfall of "Soong" Dynasty.
6. The Chiang Kai-shek Government heads for ruin.
7. The "Soong" Dynasty in the present century.
8. A plea in defence of "Traitors".
9. Why has Chiang Kai-shek met with failure?
10. The end of Chiang Kai-shek.
11. Chiang kai-shek's political life in a state of coma.
12. The Kuomintang and the Chinese Communist Party - the curses of the nation.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 3.8.38）

Pan Lien-pih
D. I.

D.C. (Special Branch)

Pamphlets
Scattered
In Street
Gang Is Seen In French
Concession But Makes
Good Its Escape

At a late hour last night the police
were maintaining a strict vigil for
a gang of pamphlet throwers which
made an appearance during the
course of the evening in three sec-
tions of the city.
It was reported that shortly after
9 o'clock a number of pamphlets of
a political nature were thrown along
the border of the French Conces-
sion at Avenue Foch and Rue Petiot,
which is the extension of Chengtu
Road.
Somewhat later, additional pam-
phlets, apparently scattered by the
same group, were picked up in the
Louza and Sinza districts, but ap-
parently the evening's activities did
not extend beyond these areas.
The pamphlets were of coloured
paper about six inches square and
were covered with anti-Hankow
polical propaganda written in Chin-
ese characters. The scatterers were
actually seen going about their work
on the Concession side of Avenue
Foch, but they made a getaway
before they could be apprehended.

1938年7月16日

小册子
散落
街头
团伙现身法租界但成功逃脱

昨晚深夜，警方严密监视一群撒传单的团伙，该团伙在当晚出现在城市的三个区域。
据报道，9点过后不久，一些具有政治性质的小册子被抛洒在法租界边界，即福煦路（Avenue Foch）和小彼得路（Rue Petiot，成都路的延伸段）。
稍后，在老闸和新闸地区也捡到了更多显然由同一伙人散布的小册子，但当晚的活动似乎并未超出这些区域。
这些小册子是约六英寸见方的彩色纸张，上面写满了中文的反汉口政治宣传标语。撒传单的人实际上在福煦路的租界一侧被看到正在作案，但在被捕之前他们逃走了。

Who were the devils? The gods of war or the communists. However the youngmen were intoxicated, and their useful future ruined by Chiang Kah Shih. They are on the way to the death.
Wake up young men. If you don't overthrow Chiang Kah Sih, who had fooled and intoxicated you, it would too late for you to regret when you entered the mouths of devils.

2. To lead people to slaughter house.
Due to the unsuccessful situation and heavy loss in the front, Chiang Kah Sih, who has been greatly exited, has forced people to join the army. All the young men can not escape from his devil hands, resembling that a number of pigs and sheeps were taken to slaughter houses.
A man, with parents and wife and children, will never come back if he joins the army.
In view of the above, If you are unwilling to be a pig or a sheep, do your best to anti Chiang and the war.

3. Kwangse people - don't join the army.

4. Proceed to your native place and enjoy your home happiness.

5. The result of recognising a thief as a father.
Since the Sian incident, Koumingtang and the communistic party commenced to work together.
From the beginning of the war, the communist party failed to take any action. After the fall of the Koumingtang communists began to proceed. The Koumingtang party is committing suicide with a rope supplied by the communists which you can see in the picture on the reverse side.

抗战救国是迷惑青年的口号。通过这些口号，所有年轻人都被愚弄了。
结果，大量青年被驱入魔鬼之口。
谁是魔鬼？是战神还是共产党人。然而，年轻人被迷醉，他们有用的未来被蒋介石毁掉。他们正走向死亡。
青年们醒醒吧。如果不推翻愚弄和迷醉你们的蒋介石，当你们进入魔鬼之口时，后悔就太晚了。

2. 引人民入屠宰场。
由于前线局势不利且损失惨重，极度兴奋的蒋介石强迫人们参军。所有年轻人都无法逃脱他的魔掌，就像许多猪羊被赶进屠宰场一样。
一个有父母妻儿的人，如果参军就再也回不来了。
鉴于上述情况，如果你不愿意成为猪或羊，请尽力反对蒋介石和战争。

3. 广西人——不要参军。

4. 返回家乡，享受家庭幸福。

自西安事变以来，国民党和共产党开始合作。
从战争开始，共产党没有采取任何行动。国民党垮台后，共产党开始行动。国民党正在用共产党提供的绳索自杀，你可以在背面的图片中看到这一点。

July 6th, 38.

1.

Arrest of male Chinese in possession
of Anti Government Pamphlets.

At 10.05a.m. on 6/7/38 J.P.S. 154 brought to
Station a male Chinese, Zee Zung Sai (徐忠山), 46,
Soochow, M/unemployed, 60, Chekiang Road, whom he had
arrested on Central Road in possession of a number of
Anti Chiang Kai-shek and Anti Communist Pamphlets.

Questioned by D.S. Guess and C.D.S. 48 the accused
stated that he earns a small living by watching motor
cars in Central District. On the morning of 6/7/38
a man whom he described as, age about 20, height about
5'5", medium build, small face, long hair, dressed in
Foreign style black serge jacket and white pants,
black shoes, no hat, speaking Mandarin, passed him on
Central Road and in passing gave him a bundle of papers
telling him to distribute them. He was standing
looking at the pamphlets when he was arrested by the
J.P.E.

D.S. Monahan of Special Branch attended the
station and a visit was paid to the suspect's home
but nothing incriminating was discovered.

The case was further investigated but the suspect
maintained his statement throughout and the matter was
referred to the D.D.O."A" who instructed that no charge
be preferred but that the suspect be detained.

1.

逮捕持有反政府传单的华籍男子。

1938年7月6日上午10时05分，巡捕 J.P.S. 154 将一名华籍男子徐忠山（Zee Zung Sai），46岁，苏州人，无业，住址浙江路60号，带至警局。该男子是在中央大道因持有多份反蒋介石及反共传单而被捕的。

经警佐 Guess 和华籍侦探副探长 48 号讯问，嫌疑人称他靠在中央区看管汽车谋生。1938年7月6日上午，一名他描述为约20岁、身高约5英尺5英寸、中等身材、小脸、长发、身穿西式黑色哗叽夹克和白裤子、黑鞋、未戴帽子、讲普通话的男子，在中央大道经过他身边时，递给他一捆纸张，让他分发。当他正站着查看这些传单时，被欧洲巡捕逮捕。

政治部警佐 Monahan 来到警局，并对嫌疑人的住所进行了搜查，但未发现任何罪证。

案件经进一步调查，但嫌疑人始终维持其供词，此事遂移交“A”区副警务总监，后者指示不予起诉，但拘留嫌疑人。

Ninghsia and Chinghai.

to be filled by a Soviet citizen.
(e) Reorganisation of the administration of the National
Government.

that the Communist Party is not sincere in its
cooperation with the Kuomintang and will resume its

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
Anti National Government Pamphlets Distributed.

At 11.20a.m. 1-7-38, C.P.C. 1990 was patrolling Szechuen Road near Kiukiang Road when he observed a number of pamphlets, about 50 in number, dropping falling through the air having apparently been thrown from one of the many office windows situated above the Bank of East Asia, corner of Szechuen and Kiukiang Roads.

The pamphlets were found to be of Anti National Government nature to the effect that the present war was caused through the Marco Polo Bridge incident and since that time the National Government have lost many Provinces and the people should now give every help to the new Reformed Government and help the Japanese to make peace.

Enquiries were made in the stated offices the entrance of which, 103, Kiukiang Road, by the undersigned assisted by C.D.C. 347 but no information could be obtained.

Pamphlets have been forwarded to Special Branch.

The "Industrial Guardian" (实業新报), a Chinese newspaper
owned by a Formosan, publishes the following report on June 28,1938:

HANDBILLS MAKE APPEARANCE SUPPORTING THE "REFORMED GOVERNMENT"

Of late, copies of two kinds of handbills have been
distributed at various public amusement resorts in this locality.
These handbills support the "Reformed Government of the Chinese
Republic" and advocate peace for the mutual welfare of China and
Japan.

A reporter of the United Press of China obtained one copy
each of the two handbills. One reads as follows :-

"The Lukouchiao Incident gave rise to the Sino-Japanese
hostilities. People are now praying for peace every day.
Chiang Kai-shek has already lost large areas of territory, thereby
seriously endangering the safety of thousands upon thousands of
brethren, but people dare not say so for fear of Chiang Kai-shek.
The National Government is propagating a war of resistance,
while the people do not know why a war of resistance should have
been started. Those who have a clear brain desire peace, but
Chiang Kai-shek and the Communist Party are so ambitious that
they want to be powerful and enrich themselves by means of the
blood of the 400,000,000 brethren. They have deposited huge
sums of money in foreign banks, claiming that it will be used
for the purchase of firearms. In the meantime, they are
conspiring with Soviet Russia and have accepted Communism in
China. This is a policy of suicide.

"The downfall of Chiang Kai-shek's regime is inevitable.
The disputes between the Kuomintang and the Communist Party,
the dissension among Government officials, the bad economic
condition of China, and the difficulty of procuring firearms
and the complaints among the people---- all constitute fatal
blows to Chiang Kai-shek's war of resistance. The Chinese
people are earnestly hoping for peace. Mr. Wang Te-huei (王克敏)
and others have formed the "Reformed Government of the Chinese

由一名台湾人拥有的中文报纸《实业新报》(Industrial Guardian) 在1938年6月28日刊登了如下报道：

支持“维新政府”的传单出现

近来，两类传单的副本在本市各公共娱乐场所散发。这些传单支持“中华民国维新政府”，并主张为了中日两国的共同福利实现和平。

中华通讯社的一名记者各获得了一份这两类传单。其中一份内容如下：—

“卢沟桥事变引发了中日敌对行动。人民现在每天都在祈祷和平。蒋介石已经失去了大片领土，从而严重危及了成千上万同胞的安全，但人们因畏惧蒋介石而不敢言。国民政府正在宣传抗战，而人民却不知道为什么要开始抗战。头脑清醒的人渴望和平，但蒋介石和共产党野心勃勃，想借四万万同胞的鲜血来夺权发财。他们已在外国银行存入巨款，声称将用于购买军火。与此同时，他们正与苏俄勾结，并在中国接受了共产主义。这是一种自杀政策。

“蒋介石政权的垮台是不可避免的。国民党与共产党之间的争端、政府官员之间的分歧、中国恶劣的经济状况、采购军火的困难以及民间的怨言——所有这些都对抗战构成了致命打击。中国人民正诚挚地希望和平。王克敏先生及其他人已经成立了‘中华民国维新政府’，目的是寻找一条通往和平的道路，并鼓励中日亲善。

E

------
The other handbill reads :-
"Brethren! The Chinese people's weakest point is the
desire to save face; they will not work hard. All this is
due to the poison of Kuomintang propaganda. The National
Government has already lost much territory. It has executed
numerous military officers for their failure in the military
operations. Hankow is about to fall soon. We should have
every confidence in the leaders of the 'Reformed Government of
the Chinese Republic', thereby creating a good chance for Sino-
Japanese rapprochement. In this way, China and Japan may
assist each other mutually.
"Brethren! Come to your senses! Rise and overthrow
the Kuomintang, overthrow the Communist Party, overthrow Chiang
Kai-shek, support the 'Reformed Government', and support Mr. Wong
Tsemei. Long live the 'Reformed Government'."
----------
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 12 29/6/39）

“同胞们！中国人民最弱的一点就是爱面子；他们不愿努力工作。这一切都是由于国民党宣传的毒害。国民政府已经失去了很多领土。它因军官在军事行动中的失败而处决了许多人。汉口很快就要沦陷了。我们应该对‘中华民国维新政府’的领导人充满信心，从而为中日亲善创造良好机会。这样，中日两国可以互助。
“同胞们！觉醒吧！起来推翻国民党，推翻共产党，推翻蒋介石，支持‘维新政府’，支持王子美 (音译) 先生。‘维新政府’万岁。”

Subject Oriental Peace Society (東亚和平会).
Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse Liang Forwarded by C. Crawford. S.J.

Despite enquiries made at all sources, no trace
can be obtained of the organization entitled "Oriental
Peace Society, pamphlets bearing this title being found
distributed on Elgin Road on April 16, 1938 (Vide the
attached report). Since then, no further pamphlets
purporting to emanate from the same organ have made their
appearance and it may therefore be safely concluded that
this title has been possibly adopted by certain so-called
peace organizers for the purpose of propaganda.

A similar copy of this pamphlet was attached together
with translation to Special Branch report dated March 30,
1938, as appendix "D" bearing on the celebration of the
inauguration of the "Reformed Government" in Nanking.

尽管从各方进行了查询，但仍无法找到名为“东亚和平会”的组织的踪迹，印有该名称的传单曾于1938年4月16日在爱而近路被发现散发（见附后的报告）。自那时起，再未出现声称出自该机构的传单，因此可以有把握地断定，该名称可能是某些所谓的和平组织者为了宣传目的而采用的。

Subject Pamphlets advocating support for the Reformed Central Government and
overthrow of Chiang Kai Shek.

Made by D.J. Gibson Forwarded by G. Roads

Sir,
At 6.20 p.m. 16-4-38, U.M.C. 2461 brought to the station
a small boy, Liu Koo Tsi (刘扣子), age 10, Pompo, N.F., who
had been distributing pamphlets on Elgin Road.
Six pamphlets were brought to the station and perusal
revealed that the message advocated the overthrow of Chiang
Kai Shek and the support of the New Reformed Government of
Central China. The pamphlets purported to be issued by the
Far Eastern Peace Society.
Enquiries ascertained that the boy, Liu Koo Tsi, and a
playmate, Tah Ong (大囡), a girl aged 7, residing in a straw
hut on Boundary Road, had picked up a number of the pamphlets
on North Shanse Road between 5 p.m. and 6 p.m. and subsequently
had amused themselves by throwing the pamphlets in open shop
doors.
Detectives were unable to obtain any further information
relative to the manner in which the pamphlets had been left
on the roadway.
Copies of the pamphlets are being forwarded to Special
Branch.

J. Gibson

长官：
1938年4月16日下午6时20分，巡捕2461号将一名在爱而近路散发传单的小男孩刘扣子（10岁，（原文不清），无固定职业）带回捕房。
六份传单被带回捕房，经查阅显示，其信息主张推翻蒋介石并支持新的中华民国维新政府。传单声称由远东和平会发布。
经询问查明，该男孩刘扣子及其玩伴大囡（女孩，7岁，居住在界路的一间草房内）于下午5时至6时之间在北山西路上捡到了一些传单，随后为了好玩将传单扔进开着的商店门内。
侦探们无法获得关于传单是如何被留在马路上的进一步信息。
传单副本正送往政治部。

At 10.50 a.m. on the 5/7/40, complainant
Tsu Tsoong Ling (朱生麟), bicycle shop
proprietor, of No.322, Wuchow Road, reported at
the Kashing Road Police Station that, at 10.45 a.m.
on the 4/7/40, two male Russians, had, on the
security of a Manchukau passport (Exhibit 1)
which is in the name of the 1st accused,
(described on sheet 1) hired two bicycles,
S.M.C.License Nos.32964 and 35428. Also that
the 2nd named person on sheet 1 (not arrested)
had written out a security note, which is
undecipherable, (Exhibit 2). The Russians failed
to return the bicycles.

At 11 a.m. on the 5/7/40, D.S.I. Beloshenko
attached to Hongkew Police Station, brought to
Kashing Road Police Station, the 1st accused,
who was handed over to the Hongkew Police Station
by the J.N.L.Party, Hannen Road Headquarters, at
5.15 p.m. on the 4/7/40.

It appears that the 1st accused and his
accomplice after having hired the two bicycles
proceeded to the Volga Restaurant, No.221, Range
Road, proprietor Tsoh Ong Tau (祝洪珠), and
partook of food and drinks which cost $22.00.
They had no money so offered a bicycle as
security. The accomplice Besterin also got an
advance of $10.00 from Tsoh Ong Tau on his bicycle,
following which he left the restaurant with his
page_data.zh:
1940年7月5日上午10时50分，梧州路322号自行车行店主投诉人朱生麟（Tsu Tsoong Ling，音译）向嘉善路巡捕房报案称，1940年7月4日上午10时45分，两名俄罗斯男子凭一本满洲国护照（证物1，以第一被告名义持有，详见附表1描述）租用了两辆自行车，公共租界执照编号分别为32964和35428。还称，附表1上的第二名人（未被捕）写了一张担保纸条，字迹难以辨认（证物2）。这些俄罗斯人未归还自行车。

1940年7月5日上午11时，隶属虹口巡捕房的副督察别洛申科（D.S.I. Beloshenko）将第一被告带至嘉善路巡捕房，该被告系由汉密尔顿路总部的日本海军陆战队（J.N.L. Party）于1940年7月4日下午5时15分移交给虹口巡捕房的。

经查，第一被告及其同伙在租用两辆自行车后，前往兰路221号伏尔加餐厅（Volga Restaurant），店主祝洪珠（Tsoh Ong Tau，音译），食用了价值22.00美元的食物和饮料。因身无分文，他们提出用一辆自行车作为担保。同伙贝斯特林（Besterin，音译，注：前文为 Boutorin）还以其自行车向祝洪珠预支了10.00美元，随后他骑着自

page_data.en:
301/40

1/3

bicycle and failed to return. The 1st accused
remained in the restaurant, and being the worse
for drink an argument arose, and a member of the
J.N.L.Party was summoned and effected his arrest.
Enquiries were then instituted by D.S.I.Beloshenko
and Tsoh Ong Tsu of the Volga Restaurant was interviewed
and stated he did not wish to take any criminal action
against the 1st accused or his accomplice.
The complainant Tsu Tsoong Ling identified the 1st
accused, and he also identified Eugenie Boutorin in
C.P.Album.
The 1st accused admits to the crime and being
concerned with Boutorin. He maintains that he arrived
in Shanghai from Harbin on the 20th June 1940, with
some Russian Merchants, one known to him as Debriakoff
when he stayed with two or three nights in the French
Concession, after which he took to sleeping out of
doors. That he only met Boutorin on the 3rd July 1940,
on the Szechuen Road, outside of the American Y.M.C.A.
but does not know his whereabouts at the present.
The passport of the 1st accused is invalid,
and combined with the note written by Boutorin which
is undecipherable and their subsequent actions go to
prove that the 1st accused and his accomplices obtained
the bicycles by false pretences.
page_data.zh:
301/40

1/3

行车离开餐厅且未归还。第一被告留在餐厅内，因醉酒引发争执，一名日本海军陆战队成员被召来并将其逮捕。随后副督察别洛申科展开调查，并询问了伏尔加餐厅的祝洪珠（Tsoh Ong Tsu，音译，注：前文为 Tsoh Ong Tau），他表示不愿对第一被告或其同伙采取任何刑事行动。投诉人朱生麟指认了第一被告，并在中央照片相册（C.P. Album）中指认了尤金尼·布托林。
第一被告承认犯罪并与布托林有关联。他坚称自己于1940年6月20日随一些俄罗斯商人从哈尔滨抵达上海，其中一人他认识，名叫德布里亚科夫（Debriakoff，音译），他在法租界住了两三个晚上，之后便开始露宿街头。他声称直到1940年7月3日才在四川路美国青年会（American Y.M.C.A.）外遇到布托林，但目前不知道布托林的下落。
第一被告的护照已失效，结合布托林所写的难以辨认的纸条以及他们随后的行为，足以证明第一被告及其同伙通过虚假借口骗取了自行车。

page_data.en:
At 11 a.m. 27/10/40, the Japanese Con-
sular Police handed over to this station the accused
described on sheet 1 of this report who was arrested
for an attempt to pick the pocket of a Japanese
passenger (soldier in civilian clothes) in the m/bus
whilst proceeding along E. Seward Road near Arthur
Road.

The complainant was allowed to go by the
Consular Police before the suspect was handed over
to this station but the occurrence also was witness-
ed by one R.P. Ozol, Russian bus Inspector No.50,
who was in the m/bus at that time.

According to this witness the accused was
standing next to the Japanese passenger and had in-
terfered with latter inside jacket pocket containing
the wallet. This had been noticed by the passenger
who grabbed hold of the suspect but latter rushed
away and alighted from the m/bus whilst same was in
motion. In doing so the accused fell down on the
footpath and injured himself.

After being arrested by the complt. and
bus inspector at first the accused was taken to the
Japanese Consular Police and then handed over to the
S.M.P. According to the Consular Police the complt.
could not attend the Court but the Russian Inspector
will do so and give evidence.

The accused was sent to the General Hos-
pital and doctor's chit reads as follows:-
Bruises and lacerations left temple
and cheek.
page_data.zh:
1940年10月27日上午11时，日本领事警察将在本报告附表1中描述的被告移交给本巡捕房，该被告因在沿亚瑟路附近的东华德路（E. Seward Road）行驶的公共汽车上企图扒窃一名日本乘客（便衣士兵）而被捕。

在嫌疑人被移交给本巡捕房之前，领事警察已允许投诉人离开，但当时同在公共汽车上的俄罗斯籍50号公交车稽查员 R.P. 奥佐尔（R.P. Ozol）也目睹了事发经过。

据该证人称，被告站在日本乘客旁边，并伸手探入后者装有钱包的内侧上衣口袋。乘客注意到了这一举动并抓住了嫌疑人，但后者挣脱并趁公共汽车行驶时跳车逃跑。在此过程中，被告摔倒在人行道上并受伤。

被告起初被投诉人和公交车稽查员逮捕，先被带往日本领事警察局，随后移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）。据领事警察称，投诉人无法出庭，但俄罗斯稽查员将出庭作证。

被告被送往广慈医院（General Hospital），医生诊断书内容如下：
左太阳穴和脸颊挫伤及撕裂伤。

1940年12月30日上午，第二被告凭拘留令被带至特别法庭（S.S.D. Court），案件延期至1940年12月31日审理，以便被告在上述日期与第一被告一同受审。

侦探于1940年12月30日走访了涉案店铺，从位于上述地址底层的凯利、西蒙斯与米尔恩（Kelley, Simmons & Milne）承包工程公司的经理甘布林先生（Mr. Gambling，音译）处获悉，涉案电钻确系该公司所有，是从店铺 premises 被盗的，但此案此前未向警方报告。

第二被告承认，1940年12月7日晚9时左右，他通过涉案店铺橱窗上方的推拉气窗进入店内，从店内的货架上偷走了一只电钻，并从进入点逃离。次日（1940年12月8日），他将赃物（价值125.00美元）带到第一被告位于东霍华德路686/20号的住所，第一被告以40.00美元的价格从他手中买下，随后又以40.00美元的价格将该物品典当，正如本报告日记部分1中所述。

（批：俄罗斯人驳回，转交 1941年12月30日 [注：原文年份41可能为笔误，结合上下文应为40或41，照录]）

property was stolen by the 2nd accused and was charged
accordingly, the case forming now the subject of (H)
F.I.R. 288/40.

Further questioning of the 2nd accused who is well
known criminal failed to connect him with any other
similar case. He was charged with the above mentioned
crime which was made now subject of (H) F.I.R. 288/40 -
(G) 4014/40.

Reference to the crow bar and one rope ladder found
in the 1st accused's room the 1st accused on being
questioned strongly denied that he had used these
articles in any crime before, but could not explain why
he kept this property in his room. It appears that the
1st accused obtained the mentioned articles with the
intention to commit a crime, though he strongly denied
same; A/M.A. will be requested to obtain permission of
the presiding Judge to confiscate the mentioned crow bar
and the rope ladder.

Both the accused will appear before the S.S.D. Court
on the morning of the 31/12/40 to answer the charges
preferred against them.

D.D.O. "G".    San. Det. 1/6.    D.S.P.

第一被告承认他非常清楚该财产是第二被告偷来的，并据此被起诉，该案现在构成初步调查报告编号 (H) F.I.R. 288/40 的主题。

对身为知名惯犯的第二被告的进一步讯问未能将他与其他类似案件联系起来。他被控上述罪行，该案现列为 (H) F.I.R. 288/40 - (G) 4014/40 号案件。

关于在第一被告房间发现的撬棍和绳梯，第一被告在接受讯问时强烈否认以前曾在任何犯罪中使用过这些物品，但无法解释为何将这些物品保存在房间内。看来第一被告获取上述物品是意图犯罪，尽管他强烈否认；将请求助理法医官（A/M.A.）获得主审法官的许可，没收上述撬棍和绳梯。

page_data.en:
At 2. 20 p.m. 4-3-41, a telephone message was
received from the Ritz Theatre, 330 Haining Road,
requesting to take custody of a Russian whom they
had arrested for stealing of brass fittings from the
doors and windows.

C. D. C. 87 and the undersigned attended and
brought to the station the accused described on sheet
1 of this report. From enquiries made it was ascer-
tained that the accused was arrested by one named
Chiang Shiu Hoo (蔣修琥) employee of the Ritz
Theatre. Chiang made the following statement:

At about 2 p.m. even date he had observed the
accused accompanied by another Russian boy entering
the lavatory. A few minutes later Chiang had followed
them and on entering the lavatory caught them un-
screwing the brass fittings. He grabbed hold of the
accused and same time the second boy rushed away and
disappeared. On being searched the accused was found
to be in possession of one screw driver and quantity
of brass fittings to approximate value of $5.00.

The accused admitted the offence, but strongly
denied having any knowledge of the whereabouts of
his companion as he met him first time only to-day
somewhere near Post Office on N. Szechuan Road.

On 5-3-41, the accused will appear before the
S.S.D. Court on a charge of Larceny when a remand of
one week will be applied for as many reports of this
nature were received at this Station recently.

W. 4/3.
Sen. Det. 1/c.

1941 年 3 月 4 日下午 2:20，接到来自海宁路 330 号丽都大戏院的电话留言，请求羁押一名他们因盗窃门窗黄铜配件而逮捕的俄罗斯人。

C. D. C. 87 号和本人前往现场，并将本报告第一页所述的被告带至警局。经查询查明，被告是由一名名为蒋修琥（Chiang Shiu Hoo）的丽都大戏院雇员逮捕的。蒋作了如下陈述：

当天下午约 2 时，他观察到被告陪同另一名俄罗斯男孩进入洗手间。几分钟后，蒋跟随他们进入洗手间，当场抓获正在拧下黄铜配件的两人。他抓住了被告，与此同时，第二名男孩逃窜并消失。经搜身，发现被告持有一把螺丝刀和数量不等的黄铜配件，估值约为 5.00 美元。

被告承认了罪行，但强烈否认知晓其同伴的下落，声称他是当天才在北四川路邮局附近某处首次与该人见面。

1941 年 3 月 5 日，被告将以盗窃罪被提解至特区地方法院，届时将申请还押一周，因为本分局近期收到多起此类性质的报告。

Several verbal complaints from the residents
of Yuenchang Rd were received recently re disorderly
conduct, begging, insults etc. by the Russian loafers
and criminals, on Yuenchang Rd near Broadway and
Market Street. It was also heard that several
strangers (specially seamen) were robbed by the
loafers, but the cases were not reported to the
Police owing to drunkenness of the victims or imme-
diate departure of the ships to which they (victims)
belong.

Between 10.45 pm and 11.20 pm 13/7/41, a
party of Police under D.S.I. Beloshenko patrolled
the above area and arrested eight Russians described
on sheet 1 of this report.

All of them are well known criminals with
previous records and on being questioned at the
station could not give any reasonable explanation
for their presence in that locality.

On 14/7/41 the accused will be brought
before the S.S.D.Court on a charge of Loitering.

近期收到元昌路居民的多起口头投诉，反映俄罗斯流浪汉和罪犯在百老汇路和市场街附近的元昌路上行为不端、乞讨、侮辱他人等。另据闻，有几名陌生人（特别是海员）被这些流浪汉抢劫，但由于受害者醉酒或其所属船只立即离港，这些案件并未向警方报案。

1941 年 7 月 13 日晚上 10:45 至 11:20 之间，由警司 Beloshenko 率领的一队警察巡逻了上述区域，并逮捕了本报告第一页所述的八名俄罗斯人。

他们均为有前科记录的惯犯，在警局接受讯问时，无法对其出现在该区域的原因给出任何合理的解释。

signed in an effort to apprehend the wanted person in this
case when at 10.20 p.m. 4/8/41 he was observed by the under-
signed walking along Broadway near North Soochow Road and
was arrested and brought to the station. The arrested per-
son Peter Tsingros, 36, Greek, N.F.A. (now the accused)
was immediately identified by the complt. as the man who
struck her with an open razor on the night of 1/8/41 as
explained in previous diary, he was also identified by a
number of other witnesses, one of whom H. Marum, manager

The accused admitted the offence but failed
to disclose where to be disposed the razor in question wit
with which he attacked the complt. the accused was charged
accordingly and will appear before the S.S.D.Court on the
morning of the 5/8/41.
The complt. who is still not recovered from her
injury, daily attending hospital for dressing, will give
her evidence in the court.

饮酒后处于醉酒状态，在咖啡馆门外与咖啡馆业主发生争吵，并用剃刀割伤了这对夫妇中妻子的右耳。

page_data.en:
At 9.45 p.m. on the 1/8/41 a telephone message
was received from 475 Broadway reporting a fight in
progress at the address. F.S. Cutbush attended and
learned that a Greek female was suffering from a
razor cut of her right arm received by her in a fight
with another male Greek who absconded before arrival
of Police. The injured female was removed to the
General Hospital and attended by Dr. Patrick who
issued the following certificate:
"Razor cut right arm -- outer upper 3/4" stitched"
Not detained.
Enquiries by the undersigned and C.D.S. 33
ascertained that at about 9.40 p.m. 1/8/41 a male
Greek, an ex-seaman, well known to the Police for his
bad temper whilst under influence of a drink, named:
Peter Tsingros, 36, Greek S/unemployed, N.F.A.
appeared outside "A la Minute" cafe, 475 Broadway E.
near Yuenchang Road and intended to enter the said
cafe, but was prevented by the proprietress of the
cafe one Mrs. P.P. Karlavitis, Greek, widow, resi-
ding above the cafe premises and who at the time
was sitting on a chair on the footpath outside the
cafe, and who saw that person being under influence
of a drink and knowing his bad temper did not wish
the latter to enter the cafe to avoid any trouble
with the other customers.
A quarrel then started between Tsingros and the
couple, when couplt. noticed an open razor in
Tsingros' right hand. The couplt. then pushed with
both her hands Tsingros' his chest and the latter
page_data.zh:
1941年8月1日晚上9点45分，接到来自百老汇路475号的电话报告，称该地址正在发生斗殴。F.S. Cutbush前往现场，获悉一名希腊妇女在与另一名希腊男子斗殴中被剃刀割伤右臂，该男子在警察到达前逃逸。受伤妇女被送往广慈医院，由Patrick医生诊治，并出具了以下证明：
“右臂外侧上部剃刀割伤——缝合3/4英寸”
未予拘留。
经署名警员及刑事侦缉处33号探员调查查明，约1941年8月1日晚上9点40分，一名希腊男子，前海员，因醉酒后脾气暴躁而为警方所熟知，名为：
彼得·青格罗斯（Peter Tsingros），36岁，希腊人，失业，无固定住所。
出现在元昌路附近的百老汇东路475号“A la Minute”咖啡馆外，意图进入该咖啡馆，但被咖啡馆女店主P.P. Karlavitis夫人（希腊人，寡妇，居住在咖啡馆楼上）阻止。当时她正坐在咖啡馆外人行道的一把椅子上，见此人处于醉酒状态，且知其脾气不好，为避免与其他顾客发生麻烦，不愿让其进入咖啡馆。
随后青格罗斯与该妇人之间发生争吵，此时报案人注意到青格罗斯右手持有一把打开的剃刀。报案人随即用双手推搡青格罗斯的胸部，后者

page_data.en:
1/3

cut her right hand with that razor.
At the time the manager of cafe Mr. H.K. Marum,
German Refugee, 763 Tongshan Road interferred and Tsingros
then left walking west along Broadway. At the time
station was informed by telephone as already mentioned
above. Several Greek cafes were visited by the under-
signed in an effort to locate the absconded Greek, when
at "Acropolis" cafe 32 Broadway was learned that he
had intended to enter the cafe shortly after commission
of the crime but was prevented by the owner of that cafe
and left walking towards Garden Bridge and evidently
proceeded to the French Concession . The wanted person
was last charged at the station for being drunk and
disorderly on the 20/6/41 and has no fixed abode.
Further enquiries Proceeding with a view to apprehend the
wanted person as the complt. wishes to charge him.

鉴于报案人希望对其提出控告，为进一步逮捕该通缉犯，调查正在进行中。

At 10 a.m. 27/7/41 telephone message was
received at this station reporting the offence sub-
ject of this F.I.R.
Enquiries by the undersigned at the scene
ascertained that at about 3 p.m. 25/7/41 whilst he
was alone in the V.D. Ward of the hospital where he is
a patient, the complt. Mr. E.J. Curran, Unemployed ex-
S.A.C./R.A.D. employee received a visit from the
pre-described suspect an ex-V.D. patient of the
hospital.
After having talked for a short period of
time to his visitor, which the complt. only knew by
sight, he took his shoes from on-top of his suitcase
containing the pre-described articles of clothing
and went to the bath room.
On returning from the bathroom the complt.
found his visitor gone and later noticed his suitcase
also gone.
Enquiries by the complt., DR. Patrick resident
physician and Mr. Burgess Hospital Treasurer, result-
ed in it being learned that the pre-described suspect
had been seen by a V.D. Ward boy and the entrance
door boy to leave the premises carrying a suitcase of
the same description of the complt's.
In view of the above pawnshops and other
likely places of disposal will be visited in efforts
to recover the stolen property and to effect the
arrest of the wanted man.
Further enquiries proceeding.

1941年7月27日上午10点，本警局接到电话报告，称发生了本首次情报报告（F.I.R.）所涉之罪行。
署名警员在现场进行调查后查明，约1941年7月25日下午3点，报案人E.J. Curran先生（失业的前S.A.C./R.A.D.雇员）独自在他作为病人所在的医院性病病房内时，接待了前述嫌疑人的来访，该嫌疑人曾是该医院的性病患者。
报案人与这位仅面熟的访客短暂交谈后，从装有前述衣物的手提箱上拿起鞋子，去了浴室。
报案人从浴室回来时，发现访客已离开，随后注意到他的手提箱也不见了。
经报案人、驻院医生Patrick博士以及医院出纳Burgess先生查询，得知性病病房的一名男护工和门口的一名男侍者曾看见前述嫌疑人提着一个与报案人手提箱描述相同的箱子离开院区。
鉴于上述情况，将走访当铺及其他可能的销赃地点，以追回被盗财物并逮捕通缉犯。
进一步调查正在进行中。

在听证过程中，原告沈甘初（Sung Khe Tsoo）所提供的证词，与其在最初报案时向本人所作的陈述存在实质性差异。当时，原告称在其衣物包裹被被告盗窃后，他被卡梅伦击打面部一次，随后卡梅伦立即逃离现场。然而，在英王陛下法院，他却称在交出包裹之前，他曾多次被卡梅伦击打面部，且在他呼救时，卡梅伦还试图堵住他的嘴。

原告面部有瘀伤痕迹（在1941年7月14日并不明显），这倾向于支持其后来的陈述。因此，登记官海姆斯先生（Mr. Haimes）将案件延期至1941年7月17日，以待对原告进行体检，目的是将指控修改为“抢劫罪”。与此同时，警方奉命设法确保负责逮捕被告的日本海军陆战队（J.N.L.P.）哨兵于1941年7月17日出庭。

At 11.30 a.m. 14-7-41, a telephone message
was received from the J.N.L.P. Headquarters at the
North Railway Station, reporting that a foreigner
was held in custody there for being concerned in
larceny, and that the J.N.L.P. Authorities wished
to hand him over to the S.M. Police.

F.S. 747 Kashima and C.D.C. 5 attended and
took into custody Charles Antony Cameron, British
subject by birth, age 25, of no fixed abode, in
possession of British passport No. 11047.

The complainant Sung Khe Tsoo (沈甘祖), 17,
shop assistant, residing 180 Darroch Road, states
that at 9.35 p.m. 13-7-41 he was walking on Darroch
Road near East Wangpang Road carrying under his
right arm a small parcel containing clothing, when
he was approached from behind by the accused who
first questioned him regarding the contents of the
parcel, and then attempted to snatch same from
beneath his arm. Complainant raised an alarm by
shouting whereupon the accused wrested the package
from him, and, striking the complainant a blow with
his hand on the face, commenced to run along Darroch
Road in the direction of N. Szechuen Road. Complai-
nant gave chase, following the accused along Darroch
Road, N. Szechuen Road, Kah Ming Road and Pecking
Road to where he encountered a J.N.L.P. sentry who
arrested the accused with the property in his
possession. Both were then taken to the J.N.L.P.
Headquarters at the North Railway Station where the
accused was detained, the complainant being told to

Statement of J.N.L.P. Authorities in connection with F.I.R.100/4
Re Larceny Case.
Time and Date - 9.35 p.m. 13-7-41.
Place of offence - Darroch Road.
Complainant - Sung Kha Tseu (沈甘初), 17, tailor's shop
assistant, 180 Darroch Road.
Offender - Cameron, 25.
Summary of the occurrence.
At about 8 p.m. 13-7-41, at the request of his master,
the shop assistant Sung Khe Tsoo went to Nanking Road and
brought some articles of clothing after which he boarded a
motor-bus on N. Szechuen Road South of the Szechuen Road
bridge to go home.
He alighted from the M/omnibus at the bus stop on Darroch
Road and whilst he was proceeding to his home, he was accosted
from behind by the offender who asked the shop assistant if
his package contained opium.
Upon approaching complainant, the offender attempted to
snatch the package. Complainant raised an alarm but the
offender took hold of complainant's body and putting his hand
over his mouth from behind robbed him of his package.
Complainant followed the offender along N. Szechuen, Nah
Ming and East Paoching Roads and reported the case to a
Japanese Naval sentry on Paoching Road.
The Sentry immediately gave chase and arrested the
offender, afterwards taking him and complainant to the J.N.L.
P. Headquarters on Paoching Road near North Railway Station.
The property was returned to complainant.
Translated by B.S. Matsushita.
page_data.zh:
日本海军陆战队当局关于首次报案记录100/4
涉及盗窃案的陈述。
时间和日期 - 1941年7月13日晚上9:35。
案发地点 - 达罗克路。
原告 - 沈甘初（Sung Kha Tseu），17岁，裁缝店店员，达罗克路180号。
罪犯 - 卡梅伦，25岁。
事件摘要。
1941年7月13日晚8时许，应店主之要求，店员沈甘初前往南京路取回一些衣物，随后在北四川路桥南侧的北四川路登上一辆公共汽车回家。
他在达罗克路的公交车站下车，在回家的路上，被罪犯从背后搭讪，罪犯询问店员的包裹里是否装有鸦片。
罪犯接近原告后，试图抢夺包裹。原告发出警报，但罪犯抓住原告的身体，从背后用手捂住他的嘴，抢走了他的包裹。
原告沿着北四川路、南昌路（Nah Ming，音译，疑为南昌路或类似路名）和东宝兴路跟随罪犯，并向宝兴路上的一名日本海军哨兵报案。
哨兵立即展开追捕并逮捕了罪犯，随后将他和原告带到北火车站附近的宝兴路日本海军陆战队总部。
财物已归还给原告。
译者：松下（B.S. Matsushita）。

On the 8/9/41, the arrested man, Rodrigues, was taken before the Portuguese Consulate Authorities and the case explained, whereupon, he was released pending Police obtaining full details from the complainant, Mrs. A Yamamoto, who had not been located. During this period, Rodrigues was to report daily to the Consulate.

On the 9/9/41 the complainant attended Dixwell Road Police Station and was interrogated regarding the offence, she stating as under.

The accused entered the shop at No. 501-3 North Szechuen Road on the pretext of purchasing a note-book, value 40 sen, and this was handed to him.. He then proceeded to another part of the shop, where various cloth was on sale, and complainant watched him, she having been previously victimised by shop-lifters.

The actions of accused were suspicious, whereupon complainant approached him and requested what he desired, intimating that he was about to purloin property from the counter. This was denied by accused, who hurriedly left the shop, but he was followed by several customers and complainant, who seized him outside the premises and found the stolen property, which fell to the ground from out of the jacket of accused, who was carrying this portion of his clothing, over his arm. Witnesses were unknown and not located.

1941年9月8日，被捕男子罗德里格斯（Rodrigues）被带至葡萄牙领事馆当局面前，案件情况得到解释，随后他被释放，条件是警方需从尚未找到的原告山本夫人（Mrs. A Yamamoto）处获取完整细节。在此期间，罗德里格斯需每日向领事馆报到。

1941年9月9日，原告来到狄思威路警察局，并就犯罪行为接受讯问，其陈述如下。

被告以购买一本价值40仙的笔记本为借口进入北四川路501-3号的店铺，店员将笔记本交给他。随后他走向店铺的另一部分，那里陈列着各种布料，原告注视着他，因为她此前曾遭受过商店扒窃受害。

被告的行为可疑，于是原告走近他，询问他想要什么，暗示他正企图从柜台窃取财物。被告予以否认，并匆忙离开店铺，但几名顾客和原告紧随其后，在店外将其拦住，并发现了掉落在地上的被盗财物，这些财物是从被告夹克中掉出的，被告当时将夹克搭在手臂上。证人身份不明且未找到。

Mrs. A. Yamamoto, Taishudo Grocer's shop master
Japan                                      D.S. 795 S. Matsusita
Dixwell Rd. Stn        9/9/41

I beg to state that my name is Asano Yamamoto, Taishudo
Grocer's shop proprietor, at 501-3 on North Szechuen Road, O.O.L.
At about 9.30 p.m. 5/9/41 I attended a male foreigner (Portuguese)
as he entered my shop to buy a note-book, value 40 cts. in
Japanese currency.
    After buying the note-book the foreigner proceeded towards
a table on which socks and handkerchiefs were exhibited, then
moved towards the neighbouring table on which a number of Japan-
ese "Yukata" (Japanese summer material) cloth rolls were exhibited
ed, he remained looking at them for a while.
    As I had been victimized of some merchandises by unknown
shop-lifters I suspected him to be a intended shop-lifter in my
shop, and approached him and asked if he had not stolen some
thing from my shop. He stated angrily that he did not steal
any thing and shaking a coat which he was carrying in his left
arm, he went away from the shop very quickly.
    As he went out in a suspicious manner I again suspected
him to be a shop-lifter so I chased after him, and two or three
customers (names unknown) assisted me in arresting him.
    The foreigner resisted me and my collaborators who had
arrested him outside No. 505 North Szechuen Road, pulled him
towards my shop. He still resisted and at this juncture, one
roll of "Yukata" cloth, value $16.00, dropped on the highway.
    I together with my customers handed the arrested person
over to members of "The Japanese Self-Vigilance Organisation"
in the vicinity of my shop, who in turn handed the man over to
the Japanese Special Naval Landing Party Sentry on duty at the
page_data.zh:

日本                                      D.S. 795 S. Matsusita（松田）
狄思威路巡捕房        1941年9月9日

本人谨陈述，本人名为浅野山本（Asano Yamamoto），系北四川路501-3号泰寿堂杂货店店主，位于越界筑路区（O.O.L.）。
1941年9月5日晚约9时30分，一名外籍男子（葡萄牙人）进入本店购买一本笔记本，价值40仙（以日元计）。
    该外籍男子购买笔记本后，走向陈列袜子和手帕的桌子，随后移向邻近陈列数卷日本“浴衣”（Yukata，日本夏季布料）的桌子，他驻足观看了一会儿。
    由于本人此前曾遭不明身份的扒手盗窃商品，故怀疑他是意图在本店行窃的扒手，遂上前询问其是否从本店偷窃了物品。他愤怒地声称未偷窃任何物品，并抖动其左臂夹持的一件外套，迅速离开店铺。
    因其离去方式可疑，本人再次怀疑其为扒手，遂追赶其后，两名或三名顾客（姓名不详）协助本人将其逮捕。
    该外籍男子抗拒本人及协助者在北四川路505号外对其实施的逮捕，我们将他拉回本店方向。他仍在反抗，此时，一卷价值16.00美元的“浴衣”布料掉落在马路上。
    本人与顾客将被捕者移交给本店附近的“日本人自警团”成员，后者随即将该人移交给在

page_data.en:
corner of North Szechuen Road and Jukong Road.
I beg furthe to state that when I saw the coat of the arrested person I found that same was folded towards the lining thus making the coat a square bag which was secured with many safty pins, the stolen property might have been concealed inside the bag.
The above is my true and correct statement.
Signed and chopped by Mr. S Yamamoto.

以上陈述真实无误。

At 3.15 p.m. 18/3/42 the complainant brought to the station
the two accused described on sheet 1 of this report whom he had
arrested for attempted larceny of Yen 200.00 in notes in the offices
of the Hashimoto Gumi Building Contractors at 5 Quisan Gardens.
Enquiries by D.S.Kusumoto and the undersigned.
The complainant reported the following:-
At about 3 p.m. even date whilst he was in his office the
2nd accused had entered the premises and requested the complt. to
change the Yen 5.00 into local currency.
The complainant agreed to do so and opened the safe containing
one bundle of Yen notes about Yen 600.00.
At this time the 1st described also entered the office and
approached the safe. Whilst the complt. was busy in checking the
required notes the 1st described took the bundle of notes from the
safe and after checking same immediately put the money into the safe.
Suspecting that the suspect may have stolen some money the
complt. locked the door and on checking his money discovered shortage
of about Yen 200.00.
When the complt. was about to search the suspect he had
noticed the stolen money laying on the floor apparently being dis-
carded by the 1st accused.
The fact that the money was laying about one yard away from
the safe shows that same was not accidently dropped but had been
stolen by the accused and then discarded as the complt. discovered
the theft.
Both accused are well known criminals specialized in "Ringing
the changes". Both accused charged accordingly.
The complt. could not attend the Court as he is leaving
Shanghai on important business, therefore he wrote the statement which
will be produced in the Court.
Hill.
Supt. I/C.
A. Baracchino
D.S.I.

1942年3月18日下午3时15分，控告人将本报告第一页所述的两名被告带至巡捕房，他因两人在昆山路花园5号桥本组建筑承包商办公室企图盗窃日元纸币200.00元而将其逮捕。
由 D.S. Kusumoto（楠本）和具名人进行调查。
控告人报告如下：
同日午后约3时，当他在办公室时，第二被告进入 premises 并要求控告人将5.00日元兑换成当地货币。
控告人同意这样做，并打开了保险箱，里面有一捆约值600.00日元的日元纸币。
此时，第一被告也进入办公室并走近保险箱。当控告人忙于清点所需纸币时，第一被告从保险箱中取出那捆纸币，在清点后立即将钱放回保险箱。
怀疑嫌疑人可能偷了一些钱，控告人锁上门，并在检查钱财时发现短缺约200.00日元。
当控告人准备搜查嫌疑人时，他注意到被盗的钱放在地板上，显然是被第一被告丢弃的。
钱放置在距离保险箱约一码远的事实表明，这并非意外掉落，而是被被告窃取后，在控告人发现盗窃行为时丢弃的。
两名被告均为专门从事“调包计”的知名罪犯。据此对两名被告提出指控。
控告人因有重要公务需离开上海，无法出庭，因此他撰写了将在法庭上提交的供词。
Hill.
主管督察长。
A. Baracchino
D.S.I.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

During the period of the writ of detention,
the accused Kunevitch still denied being concerned in
pocket-picking.

The chauffeur of omnibus no.61, has been
questioned by I.P.S. 777 Furukawa and the undersigned,
and he stated that, at about 6.30 p.m. on the 21/9/39,
at the running road, bus-stop, oneward road, he saw
the accused Kunevitch, take from the hip-pocket, of a
male foreigner, who has not been located, a leather
wallet. The witness seized the accused, who at that
time dropped the wallet on the floor of the bus, which
he believes was picked up by one of two Russians, whose
descriptions he cannot give, and who left the bus at
that juncture. The chauffeur then handed the accused
over to a Japanese sentry.

The finger-print record of the accused shows
that he was convicted to 1 year and two months imprisonment, for larceny, on the 20/11/34, charged from Louza
Police Station. Against this sentence the accused appealed, and on the 25/1/35, the appeal was dismissed. He

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Writ of Detention.

At 7.05 p.m. on the 21/9/39, in response to a telephone message from the Japanese Consular Police, Boone Road, S.P.C. 777 Furukawa attended and received into his custody a male Russian namely:-

Nicolai Ivanovich, Kunevitch, age 50, married barber, residing 241 Route des Paeours.

It was ascertained that this man at about 6.30 p.m. on the 21/9/39, was a passenger in omnibus No. 61, operated by the Japanese, driven by chauffeur A. Miyasaki, on The Broadway. At the Kungping Road stop, the chauffeur saw the Russian take a wallet from the hip-pocket of a male foreigner, also a passenger . The chauffeur seized the Russian and he was still holding the wallet. The wallet was handed back to the foreigner and the Russian was handed over to a Japanese sentry, who in turn handed him over to the Japanese Consular Police. At the time the chauffeur seized Kunevitch, two other male Russians hastily left the bus.

Kunevitch denies having picked anybody's pocket. In view of the fact that the foreigner who had his wallet stolen, is at present unknown, and that it will take some time to have the chauffeur questioned by S.M.P. detectives, the suspect has been placed on a writ of detention.

1939年9月21日晚上7时05分，响应日本领事警察的电话通知，位于北四川路（Boone Road, S.P.C.）的印度籍警员第777号 Furukawa（音译）到场，并收押了一名俄国男子，即：-

Nicolai Ivanovich Kunevitch（音译），50岁，已婚，理发师，居住于倍高尔路（Route des Paeours）241号。

经查，此人于1939年9月21日下午6时30分许，乘坐由日本人运营、司机为 A. Miyasaki（音译）的61路公共汽车，行驶在百老汇路上。在公平路（Kungping Road）车站，司机看见该俄国人从另一名外籍男乘客的后裤袋中掏出一个钱包。司机抓获该俄国人，当时他仍拿着钱包。钱包被归还给那名外籍人士，该俄国人被移交给一名日本哨兵，后者又将其移交给日本领事警察。当司机抓获 Kunevitch（音译）时，另外两名俄国男子匆忙离开了公交车。

Kunevitch（音译）否认扒窃任何人。鉴于钱包被盗的外籍人士目前身份不明，且由工部局警务处探员讯问司机需要一些时间，嫌疑人已被处以拘留令。

The accused described on sheet 1 of this report
arrested in connection with F.I.R. 1293/39,

On being questioned the accused admitted that

smoking. The accused charged accordingly and will

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

On the morning of the 13/2/40, the accused appeared before the S.S.D. Court when the case was remanded till 20/2/40 for trial.

During the period of remand the accused was frequently removed from cells and carefully interrogated by detectives and admitted the following offences as outlined hereunder:-

9th further Charge against the accused.
Larceny, of one gent's overcoat value $50.00 from complainant at 287 Chaofong Road on the 6/1/40 (W) F.I.R. 53/40. Complainant Mr. M. Wetterhahn, German refugee.

The accused further admitted that at about 1 p.m. on the 6/1/40 he entered one foreign boarding house at 287 Chaofong Road via open front door, proceeded upstairs entered rear room on the 1st. floor via unsecured door and stole from therein one gent's overcoat from a wardrobe in the room. Led by the accused detectives proceeded to above address when the accused pointed out the room in question occupied by one German Refugee M. Wetterhahn. The latter on being questioned corroborated the statement of the accused re theft of his overcoat on the above date but stated that his room was locked at the time and the accused evidently used a skeleton key to open the same. The accused strongly denied that he broke in/the room in question, stating that the door was not secured at the

对被告的第9项追加指控。
盗窃，于1940年1月6日从兆丰路287号的原告处盗窃一件男式大衣，价值50.00美元 (W) F.I.R. 53/40。原告 M. Wetterhahn 先生，德国难民。

被告进一步承认，1940年1月6日下午1时许，他通过敞开的前门进入兆丰路287号的一栋外籍人士寄宿公寓，上楼后通过未锁的门进入一楼的后房间，并从房间内的衣柜中偷走一件男式大衣。在被告的带领下，侦探前往上述地址，被告指出了由德国难民 M. Wetterhahn 居住的相关房间。后者在接受讯问时证实了被告关于上述日期盗窃其大衣的陈述，但称当时他的房间是锁着的，被告显然使用了万能钥匙打开房门。被告强烈否认他闯入/进入相关房间，声称门当时并未锁好

and one raincoat were stolen valued $35.00.
As the complainant in this report stated that the
door of his room was locked at the time when the theft
was committed it is quite possible that the accused
used a skeleton key to open the same, but on being
questioned he strongly denied that the door of the room
in question had been secured by any means.
The accused further stated that he sold the stolen
property to an unknown to him Chinese whom he met in
a Korean heroin den for a few dollars.
There is no hope for recovery of the stolen proper-

On the morning of the 30/1/40 the accused was brought befor the S.C.D. Court when he was allowed to be detained till 6/2/40.

The accused has 9 previous convictions.

During the period of remand the accused had been frequently removed from the cells and carefully interrogated by detectives and admitted the following offences as underlined hereunder and led detectives to the addresses where the offences had been committed and explained how the offences had been perpetrated by him. It was learned by detectives that in each case the accused had arrived to the scene of offence on his bicycle, leaving the machine outside the premises and after committing theft was making good his escape on the said bicycle with the stolen property and taking the stolen property straight to a nearest pawnshop, either destroying received pawn tickets or selling them to second hand hawkers, or unknown to him people on the streets.

Larceny by breaking protective device at room No.12, House 7, Lane 47 Wayside Road on 28/1/40 when 2 gent's suits and one raincoat valued $140.00 were stolen.

此外，被告承认在1940年1月17日中午12时许，他经由未上锁的前门进入华德路50弄20号的处所（外侨寄宿公寓），上楼至二楼，通过一扇未上锁的门进入一个房间，从该房间窃取了4套男式西装和3条裤子。被告离开犯罪现场时未被任何人察觉，并立即前往西华德路（E. Seward Rd.）的一家当铺，将赃物典当。两套夏季西装典当了6.20美元，其余物品典当了23.00美元。被告被捕时，警方扣押了当票。

Remarks
(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be
commented on by investigating officer).

At 5.45 p.m. 29-1-40, complts. Mr. G. Hussainoff
and Mrs. T.S. Legal, hawkers, residing 431 Seward
Road, came to the station and reported having been
assaulted by two Russians, a male and a female,
who had struck them with a knife. Both complts.
were seen to be suffering from injuries to the
face and were accordingly conveyed to the Shanghai
General Hospital where certificates as follows,
were issued: "Mr. Hussainoff, Cut on eye-lid"; "Mrs.
Legal, "Cut on upper lip." Whilst on route to the
above address to conduct enquiries at the scene of
offence, detectives encountered members of the
Japanese Naval Landing Party, who had in their
custody the two accused: G. Mahinoff, 41, s/un-
employed, residing H.S.I Lane 449 Seward Road and
his common-law wife, N. Kronodonova, who, it
appears had been creating a disturbance on Seward
Road, Mahinoff having been threatening various
Chinese pedestrians with the knife which was taken
from him by the Japanese patrol. Subsequent
enquiries elicited the two accused who, it was
apparent, had indulged in drink, to have visited
the home of complts' at approx. 5 p.m. 29-1-40
when a quarrel had arisen and the female had struck
complts' with the knife which she snatched from the
table, the male accused meanwhile attempting to
assault complts. with his fists.

The accused are charged accordingly and will
appear before the S.S.D. Court at A.M. 30-1-40.

1940年1月29日下午5时45分，控告人 G. Hussainoff 先生和 T.S. Legal 女士（原文如此，前文为 Mecal），小贩，居住于西华德路431号，来到巡捕房报案，称遭到两名俄国人（一男一女）袭击，对方用刀击打他们。两名控告人均被发现面部受伤，因此被送往上海总医院，医院出具了如下证明：“Hussainoff 先生，眼睑割伤”；“Legal 女士，上唇割伤。” 在前往上述地址进行案发地调查的途中，侦探遇到了日本海军陆战队成员，后者 custody（羁押）着两名被告：G. Mahinoff（音译），41岁，单身/无业，居住于西华德路449弄 H.S.I.（原文不清），及其同居妻子 N. Kronodonova，据称此二人在西华德路制造骚乱，Mahinoff 曾用刀威胁多名中国行人，该刀被日本巡逻队缴获。随后的调查查明，这两名被告显然曾饮酒，于1940年1月29日下午5时左右到访控告人家中，当时发生争吵，女方从桌上抓起一把刀击打控告人，男方被告则同时试图用拳头袭击控告人。

被告据此被起诉，并将于1940年1月30日上午出庭受审于 S.S.D. 法庭。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Further enquiries were continued by detectives with a view to arrest the wanted person, when at 9.15 a.m 24-1-40, an information was received that he was seen in Shanghai General Hospital. Upon receiving such an information the undersigned proceeded to above hospital and arrested the wanted person I. Milnikoff, 30, Russian, s/unemployed of N.R.A. when the latter was leaving the hospital. On being brought to the station and questioned Milnikoff admitted that he misappropriated the suit, shirt and 1 pair of boots the property of the complt., stating that on the 12-1-40, he gave the suit in question to one of his friends (name unknown) and to him he owed $20.00 to compensate his debt. The accused stated that he does not know the address of that person and the latter was not located. Further more the accused stated that he threw away the complt's shirt after the same became soiled in one of Chinese bath houses. One pair of boots the property of the complt., was recovered, being worn by the accused at the time of his arrest. The accused was charged accordingly at the instigation of the complt., and will be brought before the S.S.D. Court on the morning of the 25-1-40.

Further questioning of the accused could not connect him with any other offence.

Remarks
(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be
commented on by investigating officer).

At 5 p.m. on the 14-1-40, complt., D. Chelpanoff
Russian, unemployed, residing 18 Arthur Road, came
to Wayside Station and reported the theft of his
suit, shirt and 1 pr. of boots, total value $56.00
from above address.

Preliminary enquiries were made by D.S. Darby
(Wayside Station) and the case subsequently
transferred to this station.

Enquiries made by C.D.C. 61 and the undersigned
ascertained that the complt. is residing in room
No.7, 18 Arthur Road, Chinese lodging house.

On the 11-1-40, the complt. had met one named
I. Milnikoff, Russian, s/unemployed of N.F.A., and
the latter having no place to sleep was allowed by
the complt. to sleep that night in his room in above
lodging house. On the morning of the 12-1-40, the
above named person requested the complt. to give
him one of complt's suit, shirt and boots to go
to see his friend and promised to return the property
on the same date.

The complt. gave him the required articles of
clothing and later on at about 7 p.m. 12-1-40, he
met Milnikoff somewhere in French Concession and
requested him to go back to lodging house in question
to return the property given to him by the complt.
Milnikoff agreed and they boarded a tram car but on
their way Milnikoff suddenly got off the tram car
and when the complt. followed him he pushed him away
and disappeared.

（任何突出或特殊的特征，需由调查警官予以评注）。

1940年1月14日下午5时，报案人 D. Chelpanoff（音译），俄籍，无业，居住于亚瑟路18号，来到韦赛德巡捕房（Wayside Station），报称在上述地址被盗西装一套、衬衫一件及靴子一双，总价值56.00美元。

韦赛德巡捕房的警佐 Darby 进行了初步查询，随后本案移交至本巡捕房。

经刑事侦缉处第61号警员及签署人查询，查明报案人居住在亚瑟路18号的一家中式客栈的7号房间。

1940年1月11日，报案人遇见一名名为 I. Milnikoff（音译）的人，俄籍，据报无业，来自北四川路地区（N.F.A.），因后者无处过夜，报案人允许其当晚在上述客栈的房间内留宿。1940年1月12日上午，上述人员请求报案人借给他一套西装、一件衬衫和一双靴子去见朋友，并承诺于当日归还财物。

报案人将所需衣物交予他，随后在1940年1月12日晚7时许，报案人在法租界某处遇见 Milnikoff，要求他返回上述客栈归还报案人给他的财物。Milnikoff 表示同意，两人登上了一辆电车，但在途中 Milnikoff 突然下车，当报案人跟随他时，他将报案人推开后消失不见。

criminal record.

Further enquiries proceeding with a view to
locate and arrest the offender and to recover the
complt's property.

(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be

At 6.15 p.m. 6/2/40, complainant, Mr. Eskull
(Russian) residing House 7, Lane 312 Nanzing Road,
came to the station in company with one V. Chafiner-
inoff (Russian) his house servant, whom he accused
of having stolen one overcoat and one jacket from his
home at above address.

Questioned, accused admitted the offence, he
stated that he had stolen the clothing on the 3rd and
4th 2/40, subsequently disposing of it at pawnshops
in the Hongkew District. He led detectives to the Woo
Chang pawnshop 362 Wochang Road where the overcoat
was redeemed having been pawned by accused for $7.00
and to the Ting Fung pawnshop 410 E. Seward Road where
the jacket, pawned for 60 cents, was also recovered.

He is charged with Larceny, Cont. to Art. 320
Sect. 1 of C.C.C. and will appear before the S.S.D.
Court at A.M. 7/2/40.

1940年2月6日下午6:15，报案人 Eskull 先生（俄籍），居住于南京路312弄7号，在其家仆 V. Chafiner-inoff（音译）（俄籍）的陪同下来到巡捕房，指控该家仆从上述地址的家中窃取大衣一件及夹克一件。

经讯问，被告承认罪行，他陈述称于1940年2月3日和4日窃取衣物，随后在虹口区的一些当铺将其变卖。他带领侦探前往武昌路362号的伍昌当铺，赎回了由被告以7.00美元典当的大衣；并前往东熙华德路410号的鼎丰当铺，追回了以60美分典当的夹克。

他被控犯有盗窃罪，违反《中华民国刑法》第320条第1款，将于1940年2月7日上午出庭受审于特区法院（S.S.D. Court）。

Remarks
(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be

At 3.30 p.m. 19/11/39, a telephone message
was received at the station from Japanese Gendarmerie
Headquarters, Bridge House, N. Szechuen Road request-
ing S.M.Police to take over one foreign female who
was arrested for larceny.

Det.S. Furukawa and the undersigned attended
and brought to the station one named A. Boutakova,
50 years, Russian, S/female, residing 79 Chusan Rd
(now the accused) together with the complainant
described on sheet 1 of this report.

Enquiries made by the undersigned and C.D.C.
Cl ascertained that at about 2 p.m. on the 19/11/39
the accused entered Japanese Porcelain shop situated
at 266 Nanking Road and on being attended by shop
assistant named J. Nakao, selected one silver plated
spoon and tendered in payment for same $5.00 but was
informed by the above shop assistant to make payment
in Japanese currency and as she (the accused) has
no Japanese money the shop assistant left her and
attended to some other customers. When the accused
was about to leave the shop in question the shop
assistant noticed that a quantity of silver plated
knives and spoons which were lying on the counter,
when examined by the accused, were missing.

He (the shop assistant) questioned the
accused re same and she produced 2 paper boxes con-
taining 12 table knives, 11 spoons and 18 tea spoons
which boxes were concealed under the accused's over-
coat.

1939年11月19日下午3时30分，本警署接到位于北四川路百老汇大厦的日本宪兵队总部电话留言，要求上海公共租界工部局警务处接管一名因盗窃被捕的外国女性。

警探古川（Furukawa）及本人前往，将一名名为A. Boutakova、50岁、俄罗斯籍、单身女性、居住于中山路79号（现为被告）的人带至警署，连同本报告第1页所述的报案人一并带回。

经本人及刑事侦缉处Cl探员查询，查明1939年11月19日下午2时许，被告进入位于南京路266号的日本瓷器店，在名为J. Nakao的店员接待下，挑选了一把镀银勺子，并支付5.00美元作为货款，但上述店员告知其需用日元支付，因其（被告）没有日元，店员便离开她去接待其他顾客。当被告准备离开该店时，店员注意到放在柜台上、经被告查看过的一批镀银刀叉勺具不见了。

他（店员）就此事质问被告，被告拿出两个纸盒，里面装有12把餐刀、11把勺子和18把茶匙，这些盒子藏在大衣下面。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

The accused had been arrested by the shop assistant and handed over to Japanese Gend rmerie where from later on she was handed over to the officers of S.M.P. as already stated above.

On being brought to the station and questioned the accused, who is well known to the Police criminal, admitted the offence.

Her room at 79 Chusan Road was visited by detective and searched but nothing of an incriminating nature was found in there and on being carefully interrogated nothing further was found against her to connect her with any other similar offence.

The accused stated that some time ago she was left by her paramour and now being without any means of support, stole the property in question to get some money for her living.

She was charged accordingly and will appear before the S.S.D. Court on the morning of the 20/11/39.

被告已被店员逮捕并移交给日本宪兵队，随后如前所述，由日本宪兵队移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处警官。

被告被带到警署接受讯问，此人是警方熟知的罪犯，承认了罪行。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Information was obtained to the effect that this crime was committed by one named Mihail Sapoff, 29, Russian Gipsy, well known criminal, residing 475 E. Broadway.

At 9.30 a.m. 22-2-40, D.S.I. Fedoroff and the undersigned visited the place and took in custody the above person. On being searched he was found to be in possession of one pawn ticket for tea set (items 2 and 3) which was pawned by him for $10.00 at the Yee Shung Pawn Shop, 524 Ward Road.

On being brought to the station and questioned the accused admitted breaking into the complainant's house and also stated that a Russian known to him by the name "Keshka" was with him. He denied having any knowledge as to whereabouts of his accomplice. Further he stated that one table cover item 1 stolen by him he pawned for $4.00 in one of the pawn shops on Seward Road and the pawn ticket for same, he had disposed for $2.00 to a female Gipsy by the name, A. Orlova, residing 635/45 Tongshan Road. The above place was visited and the table cover was recovered from A. Orlova as she already redeemed same.

Remarks
(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be
commented on by investigating officer).

The complainant is the chief tenant at 45
Frenching Road occupying himself the front room on
the ground floor which is divided into two rooms by
wooden partitions. The room door is facing the street
and secured with a "Yale" lock fixed near the glass-
pane

The rear door of the room is leading to the
corridor and always locked in the complainant's absen-
ce.

At about 10 p.m. 13/4/10, the complainant left
the house locking the front door and on his returning
about two hours later he discovered that the room and
some of the drawers were ransacked and some of the
properties had been taken away. He examined the pre-
mises and discovered that entry was gained by breaking
the pane of glass in the front door and opening the "Yale"
lock by inserting the hand.

It was also discovered that two bundles of
linens and clothing were already been prepared by the
culprits but left behind as they (culprits) probably
were disturbed by some one.

It is believed that the complainant is known
to some of the culprits who was on watch and on
seeing the complainant approaching his house had in-
formed the culprits and they made good their escape
leaving prepared bundles behind. The complainant did
not notice any suspects loitering about at the time
when he returned home. The Finger Prints Bureau were
not informed as the premises were cleaned before the
case was reported to the police.

备注
（任何突出或特殊的特征需由调查警官评论）。

控告人是 Frenching Road（法伦路）45号的主要租户，他自己占用底楼的前间，该房间由木制隔板分成两间。房门朝向街道，并装有固定在玻璃窗附近的“耶鲁”锁。

房间的后门通向走廊，在控告人不在时总是锁着。

1910年4月13日晚上10点左右（注：原文年份似有误，结合上下文应为1940年2月13日），控告人离开家并锁上前门，约两小时后返回时，发现房间和一些抽屉被翻乱，部分财物被盗。他检查了现场，发现罪犯是通过打破前门的玻璃嵌板并伸手打开“耶鲁”锁进入的。

还发现罪犯已经准备好了两包亚麻织品和衣物，但将其留下，可能是因为罪犯受到了某人的惊扰。

据信，控告人为某些罪犯所认识，其中一人在放哨，看到控告人走近其住所后通知了其他罪犯，他们随即逃脱，留下了准备好的包裹。控告人回家时未注意到周围有任何可疑人员徘徊。由于在报警前现场已被清理，故未通知指纹局。

" I. Ahmetoff, 40 years, Russian, was seen in
Casualty Room on 20th November 1939 for treatment of
injury to right wrist.
" Colles's" fracture was diagnosed. X ray examina-
tion confirmed this, showing fracture of lower ends of both
both bones of forearm. Splint was applied for fixation as
there was no displacement requiring operation. Patient
is still under observation and will require splint for
two weeks more. Full use of arm at normal strength may
require two months. Signed. Dr. H.C. Patrick'.

Remarks
(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be
commented on by investigating officer).

At 3.50 p.m. 20/11/39, a telephone message
was received from one named J. Groschinsky, residing
at 40 Yuenchang Road reporting some trouble on
Yuenchang Road.

P.S. Cutbush and P.C. 639 immediately attended
and were informed by the above person that a foreigner
after assaulting two persons (one with causing
grievous bodily harm) and attempting to snatch the
gold watch had escaped into the house No.16 B. Yuen-
chang Road.

The above officers went to the above address
and knocked the front door as the same was locked.
At this time P.S. Cutbush saw the culprit in the
ground floor room through window. The room is occu-
pied by one Miss D. Cherishersky who attended and
opened the door. When the police officers had entered
the room they discovered that wanted man was not
there and it was learned that he made good his escape
through the back door.

Whilst the Police officers were making search
for the culprit in the vicinity Miss D. Cherishersky
had approached them and reported that the culprit
on leaving her room had stolen from her hand bag
one cigarette case and $70.00 in notes. As the search
of the culprit gave no results the Police officers
returned to the station with the complainant's and
reported the occurrence.

Then another Police party under Inspector
Sugden proceeded to that locality with a view to
make thorough search of the houses.

1939年11月20日下午3时50分，接到一名名为 J. Groschinsky 的人打来的电话，此人居住于元昌路40号，报告元昌路发生了一些纠纷。

巡佐 Cutbush 和警员 639 号立即前往现场，并被告知上述人员称，一名外国人在袭击两人（其中一人造成严重身体伤害）并试图抢夺金表后，逃入了元昌路 B 段 16 号的屋内。

上述警官前往上述地址，因前门紧锁，遂敲门。此时，Cutbush 巡佐透过窗户看到底楼房间内的罪犯。该房间由 D. Cherishersky 小姐居住，她前来开门。当警官进入房间后，发现通缉犯不在那里，并得知他已从后门逃脱。

正当警官在附近搜寻罪犯时，D. Cherishersky 小姐走近他们并报告说，罪犯离开她的房间时，从她的手提包里偷走了一个烟盒和 70.00 美元纸币。由于对罪犯的搜寻没有结果，警官带着投诉人返回警局并报告了此事。

随后，另一组由 Sugden 督察率领的警队前往该地区，旨在对房屋进行彻底搜查。

On arrival the police was informed that there was
possibility for the culprit being in the house No.5
Yuenchang road. The house is occupied by one named
Lovaleff, Russian, who also keeps small provision store
on the ground floor.

The premises were entered and all rooms searched
resulting that the wanted man was found concealing himself
under the bed in one of the upstairs rooms. On being
searched the culprit was found to be in possession of
$12.00 in notes and one cigarette case which was identi-
fied by Miss D. Sherishersky as her own and stolen from
her by the accused together with the money.

The room in which the accused was found had been
searched but no money found. The culprit ( now accused )
was brought to the station. From enquiries made by the
undersigned the following particulars were ascertained:-
At about 3.30 p.m. even date the accused was in the pro-
vision shop at 5 Yuenchang road and drinking "Vodka" (the
owner already summoned for this offence and case pending)
Accordingly to witnesses the accused was slightly into-
xicated by liquor but was not in state to not responsible
for his actions and about half an hour later when he was
arrested he appeared to be quite sober.

警方进入 premises 并搜查了所有房间，结果在楼上其中一个房间的床下发现了藏匿的通缉犯。经搜查，发现罪犯身上持有 12.00 美元纸币和一个烟盒，D. Sherishersky 小姐确认为其所有，并称是被被告连同钱款一起偷走的。

Remarks
(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be
commented on by investigating officer).

In response to a telephone message at 10.10 p.m.
on 29-11-39 from the owner of the Central Beer
Hall, 14 Yuenchang Road, reporting that 4 Russians
were breaking up the establishment. D.S. Muir
accompanied by C.P.C. 2927 at once proceeded to
this address to conduct investigation.

On arrival of Police the proprietor of the
restaurant, now complainant, reported that at
about 10 p.m. 29-11-39, 4 Russians, entered the
Beer Hall and demanded money, cigarettes and Vodka.
Upon the complainant's wife replying that on
account of bad business she could not afford to
meet their demands, the Russians however then
commenced to threaten to break up the establishment
but were ejected by a customer named Henrich Hans,
24 Yuenchang Road, a Netherlander.

After being ejected, the Russians returned
to the beer hall one of whom then carried a long
brush handle and after striking the manager of
beer hall named Walter Kulmann, German, 245 Ping-
liang Road, across the chest they re-entered the
shop and from inside they smashed the glass
window of the door and commenced throwing chairs
about before being finally overpowered and again
ejected by the already mentioned customer, manager
and others who had arrived.

At this instance the now 1st accused obtained
a pot of putty (about 5 lbs in weight) from
somewhere and threw it into the shop.

针对1939年11月29日晚上10点10分来自元昌路14号中央啤酒馆业主的电话留言，报告称4名俄国人正在破坏该场所。侦探长 Muir  accompanied by C.P.C. 2927 立即前往该地址进行调查。

警方到达时，餐馆老板（现控告人）报告称，1939年11月29日晚上10点左右，4名俄国人进入啤酒馆，索要钱财、香烟和伏特加。当控告人的妻子回答说由于生意不好，她无力满足他们的要求时，俄国人随即开始威胁要破坏该场所，但被一名名为 Henrich Hans 的顾客驱逐，该顾客为荷兰人，住元昌路24号。

被驱逐后，俄国人返回啤酒馆，其中一人手持一根长刷柄，在击中啤酒馆经理 Walter Kulmann（德国人，住平凉路245号）胸部后，他们重新进入店内，从内部砸碎门上的玻璃窗，并开始乱扔椅子，直到最终被前述顾客、经理及其他赶到的人制服并再次驱逐。

在此刻，现在的第1被告不知从何处弄来一桶油灰（重约5磅）并扔进店内。

During the attack on the shop several of the Russians
received cuts from the broken glass and blows from the
persons assisting in having them ejected.

Before the arrival of Police two of Russians had
absconded however the 2nd accused was found lying on
the footpath near the shop whilst the 1st accused was
located further along Yuenchang Road. Both were placed
under arrest.

The particulars of the accomplices who absconded
are alleged to be unknown to the accused.

The accused slightly under the influence of drink
deny the attack on the beer hall, they however are
known to frequent this neighbourhood and prey on the
sympathy of the owners and customers of the beer halls
in this area.

Both accused are now charged with Attempted
Extortion with Violence and will appear before the
Court on the morning of 30-11-39.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Le Nicolas Andreeff (Russian) arrested on Garden Bridge and handed over to French Police.

At 1.45 p.m. 20/3/40, Le Au Tsoong (朱宝铃), shop-master, residing 233 Rue Kratzer S.C., brought to the station a male Russian, Nikolas Andreeff, 20, -/un-employed, S.S.A., whom he had arrested on the Garden Bridge, at 1.30 p.m. for having been concerned with two other foreigners in the trick known as "ringing the changes" at his shop at above address.

It appears that at about 1 p.m. today the accused together with two other foreigners, entered complainant's shop at 233 Rue Kratzer and, by means of the above-mentioned trick, defrauded him of $20.00. Following their departure complainant proceeded immediately to the Garden Bridge, thinking that the men might reside in Hongkew or Wayside districts, which action resulted, at 1.30 p.m. in him locating the accused and effecting his arrest.

The above details were communicated to the French Police and at 5 p.m. 20/3/40, the accused was handed over to D.S. Stobodchikoff of that unit, with the permission of D.O. "C".

Le Nicolas Andreeff（俄国人）在外白渡桥被捕并移交给法国警察。

1940年3月20日下午1点45分，店主 Le Au Tsoong (朱宝铃)，住法租界克拉泽尔路233号，将一名俄国男子 Nikolas Andreeff，20岁，-/无业，S.S.A.，带到巡捕房。此人于当天下午1点30分在外白渡桥被其逮捕，原因是他伙同另外两名外国人在上述地址的其店内实施了一种称为“掉包计”的骗局。

看来，今天下午1点左右，被告伙同另外两名外国人进入控告人位于克拉泽尔路233号的商店，并通过上述骗局诈骗其20.00美元。在他们离开后，控告人立即前往外白渡桥，心想这些人可能居住在虹口或越界筑路区，这一行动使他在下午1点30分找到了被告并将其逮捕。

上述详情已通报法国警察，经"C"区总监许可，被告于1940年3月20日下午5点移交给该部门的 D.S. Stobodchikoff。

咖啡馆的三名中国“侍者”的宿舍位于咖啡馆上方的二楼，而一楼目前无人居住。

经理 Gundlah 向负责调查的警官移交了一把损坏的挂锁，该挂锁系被告从守卫该处所前门的铁栅栏上撬下的，同一把锁将作为证物在法庭出示。

侦探走访了两名被告的住所，但未发现任何具有指控性质的物品。

The accused stated that at about 10 pm on the 30/10/3
he entered the ground floor sitting room of the above
address through the window of that room by breaking glass
of the window and then inserting his hand through the
hole and slipping back the catch of the window to open
the same. From the above mentioned room the accused
stole one radio set, one cigar box and a quantity of
cigars and left the premises being unobserved by any one.
As it was ascertained by detectives from the complainant
one Robert Patterson, British, residing above address
that all inmates were asleep at the time of the commission
of the offence. The accused stated that he sold the
stolen cigar box to a street hawker for $1.00 and the
stolen radio set was pawned by him in a pawnshop on
Woosung Rd and the pawn receipt sold to a Chinese on
Nwakes Rd for $6.00 on 2/11/39. The accused led detective
to Neu Fong ( 于家丰 ) Pawnshop, 116 Woosung Rd where it
was learned that the radio set in question was pawned by
the accused on 31/10/39 and redeemed by an unknown
Chinese on 23/11/39.

There is no hope for recovering of the stolen
property now.

The accused was further charged with this offence
and the complt. warned to attend the Court on 15/12/39
to give his evidence.

被告称，1939年10月30日晚上10时许，他打碎上述地址房间窗户的玻璃，将手伸入洞中拨开窗扣打开窗户，从而进入该处一楼的客厅。被告从上述房间窃取了一台收音机、一个雪茄盒和若干雪茄，随后离开该处所，未被任何人察觉。经探员向居住于上述地址的英国人Robert Patterson先生（原告）核实，案发时屋内所有人均在熟睡。被告称，他将盗得的雪茄盒以1.00美元的价格卖给了一名街头小贩，并将盗得的收音机典当在吴淞路（Woosung Rd）的一家当铺，随后于1939年11月2日在宁波路（Nwakes Rd）将当票以6.00美元的价格卖给了一名华人。被告带领探员前往吴淞路116号的“于家丰”（Neu Fong）当铺，经查证，涉案收音机系被告于1939年10月31日典当，并于1939年11月23日被一名不知名华人赎回。

目前赃物已无追回希望。

被告被就此罪行追加起诉，并告诫原告于1939年12月15日出庭作证。

of one dark blue gaberdine gent's overcoat perpetrated

    The accused stated that he sold the stolen overcoat

with assistance of D.P.S. Furukawa failed to locate the

of the Judge.

    Further interrogation of both the accused could not
connect them with any more offence, therefore they will
be brought before the S.S.D. Court on the morning of the

一件深蓝色华达呢男士大衣，系其于1939年9月1日左右所为，并带领探员前往北四川路843号，指认了二楼的一条后走廊，称其从那里的一张桌子上拿走了该财物。

    被告称，他将盗得的大衣在外滩以4.00美元的价格卖给了一名不知名华人。探员在古川（Furukawa）警官的协助下，对上述地址（日籍人士住宅）进行调查，未能找到原告，但从该处所的另一名住户、日本商人山崎（K. Yamasaki）处获悉，所述盗窃案确如被告所述，发生在上述大致日期，但原告未向警局报案。被盗大衣的价值约为50.00美元。由于本案未能找到原告，且赃物未追回，故未就此事对第一被告提出进一步指控，但将请求助理副督察长（A/M.A.）提请法官注意此事。

    经进一步讯问，两名被告均无法与更多罪行建立联系，因此他们将于1939年12月15日上午被提解至特别巡捕法庭（S.S.D. Court），以应对针对他们的指控。

Remarks
(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be

At 12.50 a.m. 1-12-39, a telephone message
was received from Woosung Road Sub-Station of the
Japanese Consular Police requesting to take custody
of a Russian thief.

The place was visited and the accused
described on sheet 1 of this report was received
in custody who was arrested for larceny of a
bicycle.

Enquiries by C.D.C. 327 and the undersigned.
The complt. in this case is one named Siau
Ken Ji who is working as a boy at 190 Haining Road.
At about 12 m.n. 30-11-39, he placed his
unlocked bicycle outside the premises and a few
minutes later he saw the accused mounted same and
rode away towards Woosung Road. The complt. together
with one named Siau Poo Dah gave chase and succeeded
in arrest of the accused on Woosung Road near
Haining Road. Then they handed over the accused to
their employer (Japanese) who in turn took the
accused to the Woosung Road Sub-Station of the
Japanese Consular Police.

On being questioned the accused admitted the
theft.

On being searched the accused was found to be
in possession of one screw driver, one pair of
pliers and small wrench. The accused was questioned
re possession of the above instruments, but he
could not give any satisfactory explanation for
carrying same. The accused is an old criminal.

1939年12月1日凌晨12时50分，
收到来自日本领事警察吴淞路分驻所的
电话留言，要求收押一名俄国窃贼。

经前往该地，本报告第1页所述的
被告被收押，其因盗窃自行车
被捕。

经刑事侦缉处警长（C.D.C.）327号及下述签署人查询。
本案报案人名叫 Siau Ken Ji，
在海宁路190号做男孩（侍役）。
1939年11月30日午夜12时许，他将
未上锁的自行车放在屋外，几分钟后，
他看见被告骑上该车并向吴淞路方向
骑去。报案人与一名叫 Siau Poo Dah 的人
一同追赶，并在靠近海宁路的吴淞路上
成功逮捕了被告。随后他们将被告移交给
他们的雇主（日本人），该雇主又将被告
送往日本领事警察吴淞路分驻所。

经讯问，被告承认了盗窃行为。

经搜身，发现被告持有
一把螺丝刀、一把钳子和一个小扳手。
就持有上述工具一事对被告进行讯问，
但他无法对携带这些工具给出任何
令人满意的解释。被告是一名惯犯。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Death of a Male Russian in a Korean Heroin Den
at 163 Market Street.
--------------------------------------------------

At 4.30 p.m. on the 7/3/40, an information was
received by the undersigned to the effect that a male
Russian had died in a Korean heroin den at 163 Market
Street. Acting on instructions of Senior Detective 1/c,
Japanese Consular Police was requested to give assis-
tance to visit the above address and at about 7 p.m.
7/3/40 a party of Police consisting of C. D. C.s 234, 274,
D.P.S.Shimizu and the undersigned accompanied by Japanese
Consular Police officer Kawamura visited No.163 Market
Street a Chinese dwelling house where in the rear
ground floor room used as a heroin den discovered the
dead body of a male Russian lying on the especially
made bread bed in that room used by narcotic addicts
to smoke heroin.

The dead body was immediately identified by the
undersigned as one named Lee Shenke, 25 years, Russian,
s/unemployed, of N.P.A. who was charged at this station
in connection with (W) F.I.R.1295/39 and sentenced in
the S.S.D. Court on the 22/12/39 to 3 months imprisonment
for larceny at night and who recently had been released
from Ward M Gaol. 6 male Russians, 2 male and 2
female Chinese were arrested by detectives in above den

一名俄国男子死于市场街163号的一家朝鲜人海洛因烟馆
--------------------------------------------------

1940年3月7日下午4时30分，具名者收到情报，称一名俄国男子死于市场街163号的一家朝鲜人海洛因烟馆。根据高级警长（主管）的指示，请求日本领事警察协助前往上述地址。约于1940年3月7日晚上7时，由刑事侦探课警员234号、274号、特别巡捕清水（Shimizu）及具名者组成的一队警员，在日本领事警察官员川村（Kawamura）的陪同下，造访了市场街163号。这是一处华人住宅，在其后楼底层的房间内（该房间被用作海洛因烟馆），发现一具俄国男子的尸体，躺在那间房里专为吸毒者吸食海洛因而特制的“面包床”上。

具名者立即确认死者名为李申克（Lee Shenke），25岁，俄国人，职业无业，属北公共活动区（N.P.A.）。此人曾因涉嫌卷入本捕房受理的 (W) F.I.R.1295/39 号案件，并于1939年12月22日在特区地方法院（S.S.D. Court）因夜间盗窃罪被判处三个月监禁，最近刚从提篮桥监狱（Ward M Gaol）获释。侦探在上述烟馆内逮捕了6名俄国男子、2名中国男子和2名中国女子

at the time of enquiries for smoking heroin together with one Korean female named Lee Do Ka, 37, Korean, m/female, residing in above mentioned room and who admitted of having conducted heroin den at the address.

The above Korean female on being questioned stated that she did not know that the above Russian died and thought that he was only asleep, but admitted that he was a customer of her den injecting heroin into vein of his arm. She was handed over to Japanese Consular Police together with a quantity of heroin found in her possession.

Enquiries made amongst the arrested Russians revealed that the deceased came to the said den at about 4 p.m. 7/3/40 and injected heroin into the vein of his arm and then was lying on the bed. At about 4.30 p.m. some one noticed that the deceased became unconscious and few minutes later had died.

Examination of the body could not find any marks of violence and no foul play suspected. The deceased is known to the Police as a narcotic addict. The brother of the deceased G.Shenkoff, residing 810/36 E.Seward Rd was located by the undersigned and identified the body of his brother name and particulars as already stated above.

当时正在询问有关吸食海洛因的情况，同时涉及一名名叫李多卡（Lee Do Ka）的朝鲜女子，37岁，朝鲜人，已婚女性，居住在上述房间内，并承认在该地址经营海洛因烟馆。

在接受讯问时，上述朝鲜女子表示她不知道上述俄国男子已死亡，以为他只是睡着了，但承认他是她烟馆的客人，她将海洛因注射进其手臂静脉。她连同在其身上发现的一定数量海洛因被移交给日本领事警察。

对被捕俄国人的问询显示，死者于1940年3月7日下午4时许来到该烟馆，将海洛因注射进其手臂静脉，随后躺在床上。约下午4时30分，有人注意到死者失去知觉，几分钟后死亡。

尸检未发现任何暴力痕迹，亦不怀疑有他杀情节。警方已知死者为吸毒成瘾者。具名者找到了死者的兄弟 G.Shenkoff，其居住在西华德路（E.Seward Rd）810/36号，由其辨认了尸体，死者姓名及详情如上所述。

Remarks
(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be
commented on by investigating officer).

At 4 a.m. 26/3/40, plain-clothes officers
F.C.702 and P.C.851 brought to the station the two
accused as described on Sheet 1, whom they had
arrested in the Koong An Li alleyway (Lane 260),
Woosung Road at 3.45 a.m. even date.

It appears that the above two police-officers
were patrolling on Woosung Rd, when they saw the two
accused standing at the entrance to the above alley-
way in company with a female, the officers entered
the alleyway where they saw on a bench at the side of
the entrance four cases of Johnny Walker Whisky which
were afterwards found to have been stolen from a
godown at No.49 in the Koong An Li alleyway. They
waited in this alleyway until they saw the female
depart in a ricksha when the two accused turned and
entered the Koong An Li, on the approach of the
officers the two accused attempted to escape, they
were, however, arrested and brought to the station.

1st. accused was found to have in his possession
a pair of dirty cotton gloves which, it is thought,
may have been worn when breaking the door of the
godown, while 2nd accused had a candle and a screw-
driver on his person at the time of arrest. Both
deny being concerned in this breaking but neither
can give a satisfactory explanation as to their
reasons for being abroad at this hour or why they
should be in possession of house-breaking implement,
in view of which a charge of godown-breaking cont.to
Art.381 (1) of C.C.C. will be preferred when the
accused appear before the Court at a.m. 26/3/40.

备注
（任何突出或特殊的特征需由调查警官评论）。

1940年3月26日凌晨4时，便衣警员 F.C.702 和 P.C.851 将第1页所述的两名被告带至捕房，他们于同日凌晨3时45分在吴淞路恭安里（Koong An Li）弄堂（260弄）内将二人逮捕。

据悉，上述两名警员当时正在吴淞路巡逻，看见两名被告与一名女子站在上述弄堂入口处，警员进入弄堂，看见入口旁的一条长凳上有四箱尊尼获加（Johnny Walker）威士忌，后经查实系从恭安里弄堂49号的一间仓库盗出。他们在弄堂内守候，直到看见该女子乘黄包车离开，此时两名被告转身进入恭安里，当警员靠近时，两名被告试图逃跑，但随后被逮捕并带至捕房。

经查，第一被告身上藏有一双脏棉手套，推测可能是在撬仓库门时佩戴；第二被告在被捕时身上藏有一支蜡烛和一把螺丝刀。两人均否认参与此次破门行窃，但均无法对其在此时段外出或持有破门工具的原因给出令人满意的解释，鉴于此，当被告于1940年3月26日上午出庭法院时，将依据《中华民国刑法》第381条第(1)款指控其犯有破仓盗窃罪。

At 12.35 p.m. 24/2/40, this case was
transferred from Hongkew Police Station. The
complainant, M.Kokagi, is the proprietor of a
shoe shop at No.162, Yalu Road.

It appears that at 11.50 a.m. 24/2/40, the
accused with another foreigner, not arrested, enter-
ed the complainant's shop on the pretext that the
accused wanted one of his shoes repaired. They
argued with the complainant over the price but
could not agree, and the accused and his accomplice
left the shop. A few moments after they had gone,
the complainant found that a pair of black leather
shoes were missing from the shop counter. He left
the shop in pursuit of the foreigners and caught
up with them on Yalu Road near Point Road and arrest-
ed the accused who had the shoes under his overcoat.

The accused quickly passed the shoes to his
accomplice who decamped down a nearby alleyway. The
complainant took the accused to Hongkew Station.

Questioned by detectives the accused admitted
that he entered the complainant's shop, but denies
that he had a companion or that he stole the shoes.
He has been previously convicted for larceny.

Charged under Art. 320 Section 1 of the C.C.R.C.
the accused will be arraigned before the S.S.D.Court
during the morning of 26/2/40. A remand of one week
will be requested.

1940年2月24日下午12点35分，此案从虹口巡捕房移交。控告人 M.Kokagi 是鸭绿江路（Yalu Road）162号一家鞋店的店主。

情况显示，1940年2月24日上午11点50分，被告与另一名未被逮捕的外籍男子以被告想修理一只鞋为借口进入控告人的店铺。他们就价格与控告人发生争执但未达成一致，随后被告及其同伙离开了店铺。他们离开几分钟后，控告人发现店柜台上少了一双黑色皮鞋。他离开店铺追赶那些外国人，并在靠近波因特路（Point Road）的鸭绿江路上追上了他们，并逮捕了将鞋子藏在大衣下的被告。

被告迅速将鞋子递给其同伙，同伙逃入附近的一条小巷。控告人将被告带到虹口巡捕房。

经侦探审讯，被告承认进入了控告人的店铺，但否认有同伴或偷窃鞋子。
他此前曾因盗窃罪被判刑。

依据《中华民国刑法》第320条第1款提出指控，被告将于1940年2月26日上午在 S.S.D. 法庭（上海特区地方法院）受审。将申请还押一周。

Remarks

At p.m. 4/4/40, C.P.C.2665 came to the
station and reported an accident in which the
m/car licence No.7771 collided with the bicycle
licence No.1997 on Broadway near Nanzing Road.
Further the above C.P.C. stated that when
he requested the driver of m/car (foreigner) to
produce the licence latter drew the pistol and
after intimidating him (C.P.C.) went away in his
m/car.
Immediately the message was circulated
resulting that at about 1.35 a.m. 4/4/40 the
owner of the above m/car one named Rootilevsky
Russian, was arrested by the French Police at his
home, 3 Route Pershing and handed over to the
undersigned to be dealt with.
At the time of arrest Rootilevsky produced
an automatic pistol "Ortgies" make No.171401 and
also a permit No.882 to carry same and issued
to him by the French Police on 12//7/39.
On being questioned Rootilevsky denied
threaten/ the C.P.C. with his pistol, but stated
that on being requested to produce his driving
permit he did so and as the permit and pistol
were in same pocket he took it together but
immediately placed the pistol back in his pocket.
The C.P.C.2665 was questioned again when
he definitely stated that the driver attaining
a threatening attitude drew a pistol and pointed
at him.
Copy of a statement attached.
The cyclist was named Tang Zoh Chen

1940年4月4日下午，华捕第2665号来到捕房，报告了一起事故，其中车牌号为7771的机动车与车牌号为1997的自行车在百老汇路靠近南京路处相撞。此外，上述华捕称，当他要求机动车司机（外国人）出示执照时，后者拔出手枪，在恐吓他（华捕）后驾车离去。
消息随即发出通报，结果在1940年4月4日凌晨约1时35分，上述机动车车主，一名叫 Rootilevsky 的俄国人，在其住所霞飞路（Route Pershing）3号被法国警察逮捕，并移交给下文签署人处理。
逮捕时，Rootilevsky 出示了一支“Ortgies”牌自动手枪，编号171401，以及一张携带该枪的许可证，编号882，由法国警察于1939年7月12日签发给他。
经讯问，Rootilevsky 否认用手枪威胁华捕，但称当被要求出示驾驶执照时，他照做了，由于执照和手枪在同一口袋中，他便一起取出，但随即将手枪放回口袋。
华捕第2665号再次接受讯问，他明确陈述司机摆出威胁姿态，拔出手枪并指向他。

The following is the statement of C.P.C.2665 Tseu Pong Gih
native of Honan ........................................taken by me Translated
at Hongkew Stn. on the 4-4-40 ............and interpreted by Chen (Clerk)

At 5.55 p.m. 3-4-40 whilst on traffic duty at Broadway
and Nanzing Road corner I observed a m/car No.7771 and a bicycle
No.1997 both proceeding west on Broadway near Nanzing Road,
bicycle in front. When the m/car overtook the bicycle, the left
front bumper collided with the rear wheel of the bicycle, causing
the cyclist to fall to the ground. I then went up to make en-
quiries, and asked the driver, a foreigner, to have a look at
his driving permit. He got out of the m/car, and took out his
pistol, and pointed it towards me. I then caught hold of his
pistol, but was unable to take it away from him. The foreigner
put back his pistol into his pocket and drove away. Therefore
I brought the cyclist to the Station to make a report. This is
my true statement.

Signed by C.P.C.2665(Tseu Pong Gih)

1940年4月3日下午5时55分，当我在百老汇路与南京路拐角处执行交通勤务时，我看到一辆车牌号为7771的机动车和一辆车牌号为1997的自行车均在百老汇路上向西行驶，自行车在前。当机动车超过自行车时，左前保险杠撞上了自行车的后轮，导致骑车人摔倒在地。我随即上前询问，并要求司机，一名外国人，出示其驾驶执照。他走出机动车，掏出手枪，指向我。我随即抓住他的手枪，但未能从他手中夺下。该外国人将手枪放回口袋并驾车离去。因此，我将骑车人带回捕房报案。这是我的真实陈述。

华捕第2665号 (Tseu Pong Gih) 签名
