Remarks
(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be commented on by investigating officer).

At 7.10 a.m. on 18/12/39, in response to
to a telephone message was received from the J.N.L.
Party stating that they had a Russian in their custo-
dy who they wished to hand over to the S.M.Police,
F.P.S.826 attended and received into custody one
named Boris Doubrovin, 30, Russian, S/unempl yed,
of N.F.A., together with the informant in this case
one Ez Yoong Loong (施雄郎), a house coolie, employ-
ed at 124 Quinsan Road, a dwelling house owned by the
Sassoon Coy. Ltd.

Enquiries by C.D.C.318 and the undersigned
were made and the following was ascertained:-At about
4.30 a.m. 18/12/39, whilst the informant was sleeping
in a downstairs room directly facing the main door
he heard a noise and on investigating saw a male
person tampering with the front door.

When the informant went to make further
enquiries about this person's activities he made off
along Quinsan Road but after informant had gone out-
side the house he discovered that this person had
previously been attempting to unscrew two brass door
handles value about $37.00 from the door.

The complainant then decided to follow the
person (now the accused) and after reaching Chapoo
and Tiendong Roads he arrested him with the assistan-
ce of a member of J.N.L.Party stationed at that point
Preliminary enquiries were made at first by J.N.L.
Party and later on the accused had been handed over
to S.M.P. as already stated above.

1939年12月18日上午7:10，收到犹太警队（J.N.L. Party）的电话留言，称他们扣留了一名俄国人，希望将其移交给上海公共租界警务处（S.M.Police），巡捕F.P.S.826前往接收并拘留了一名名为鲍里斯·杜布罗温（Boris Doubrovin）的男子，30岁，俄国人，单身/无业，无固定住所（N.F.A.），以及本案举报人施雄郎（Ez Yoong Loong），一名受雇于昆山路124号的住家苦力，该住宅为沙逊有限公司（Sassoon Coy. Ltd.）所有。

经刑事侦缉处探员C.D.C.318及本人调查，查明如下情况：— 1939年12月18日凌晨4:30左右，举报人正睡在正对大门的楼下房间内，听到响声，经查看，发现一名男子正在摆弄前门。

当举报人前去进一步查问此人的活动时，此人沿昆山路逃窜，但在举报人走出屋外后，发现此人此前曾试图从门上拧下两个价值约37.00美元的黄铜门把手。

随后，控告人决定跟踪此人（即现在的被告），在到达乍浦路（Chapoo Road）和天潼路（Tiendong Road）后，在该处驻守的一名犹太警队成员的协助下将其逮捕。初步讯问首先由犹太警队进行，随后被告被移交给上海公共租界警务处，如上所述。

被告承认，他意图盗窃上述地址的两个黄铜门把手并将其拧下。被告是一名海洛因成瘾者，并进一步承认，他打算出售上述门把手以获取资金购买海洛因。被告称其居住在南京路74号，但侦探走访上述地址后发现那是一处妓院，经在那里询问得知，被告并不居住在上述 premises，只是曾多次光顾该妓院。

由于该地区近期发生多起此类轻微盗窃案，本人就此事对被告进行了仔细审问，但他强烈否认犯有其他类似罪行，进一步的讯问也未能动摇其供词。

据此对被告提出指控，他将于1939年12月19日上午出庭受审于上海第二特区地方法院（S.S.D. Court）。

另一套男士西装和那顶帽子则在元丰路163/5号的恒顺（Neu Zaing）当铺被追回，系被告于1939年12月1日以28.50元典当。

侦探找到了报案人A. Sternklemann，德国难民，居住在中山西路41/12号，他辨认出追回的财物即为1939年12月1日从其房间被盗之物。

此案由报案人在案发当日向路边警亭报案。追回的财物将作为证物在法庭出示，报案人愿意支付上述财物的赎金。

第三名被告进一步供述，他将处置上述财物所得的钱款用于自己和朋友的饮食，且在1939年12月1日晚上9点左右，他醉酒后在市场街与数名朝鲜人发生争吵，争吵演变为斗殴，在斗殴过程中，被告丢失了当时穿在身上的被盗雨衣和装有2件衬衫的手提包。

经侦探查询，证实正如被告所称，在元丰路附近的市场街上，被告与几名身份不明的朝鲜人发生了斗殴，但丢失的财物未被追踪到。

On the morning of the 7/12/39, 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th and 8th accused appeared before the S.S.D.Court when application for their release was made and they were released by order of the Judge.

经刑事侦缉警长251号和具名人查询查明，约上午10:55，被告进入上述地址的裁缝店，利用店主（投诉人）在后屋且店内只有一名学徒夏松良（Woo Sung Liang）的机会，偷走了一件挂在门口附近墙上的现成大衣，当时未被学徒察觉，但几秒钟后，上述学徒注意到大衣不见了，走出店铺来到吴淞路，观察到被告正携带赃物离开。
学徒发出警报，告知其主人，主人追赶窃贼并成功将其逮捕，如上所述将其移交给华捕1696号。
被告是警方熟知的有前科罪犯，据此被控告，并将于1940年5月3日上午出庭受审于特别巡捕法庭（S.S.D. Court）。

Remarks
(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be commented on by investigating officer).

At 5.15 p.m. on 4/5/40, a telephone message was received at this station from J.P.S. 207 to the effect that a male Japanese had arrested one Russian at a bus stop at the corner of Broadway and Nanking Road on suspicion of being concerned with Pocket-picking, as he had one wallet containing Yen 5.00 and ¥4.00 (total sum $10.50) whilst boarding a omnibus, No.6 (Route), Lic.No.166, of the Central China Urban Omnibus Company.

Upon receipt of this message, F.P.S. 32, D.P.S. 763 and the undersigned proceeded to the above location and brought to this station one foreigner, Russian, named Israel Shpiller, age 38, M/Merchant, residing at No.78 Route des Soeurs, French Concession.

Enquiries were made by F.P.S. 32 Wernberg, D.P.S. 763 Izumi and the undersigned, when the following was ascertained:-

At about 5 p.m. 4/5/40, the complainant boarded a omnibus, Route No.6, Lic.No.166, of the Central China Urban Omnibus Company, proceeding along Broadway from west to east, from a terminus at the corner of Astor Road and Broadway near the Garden Bridge.

On reaching a bus stop at the corner of Broadway and Nanzing Road, the complainant alighted from the bus, when he was pushed by the accused from behind. This caused the complainant to arouse a suspicion of having one wallet in the right hip's pocket picked by the accused.

1940年5月4日下午5:15，本局接到来自日本巡捕房（J.P.S.）207号的电话消息，称一名日本男子在百老汇路与南京路拐角处的公交车站逮捕了一名俄罗斯男子，涉嫌扒窃，因为该俄罗斯男子在登上华中都市公共汽车公司第6路公共汽车（车牌号166）时，持有一个装有日元5.00元及¥4.00元（总计10.50美元）的钱包。

收到此消息后，外国巡捕房（F.P.S.）32号、侦探巡捕房（D.P.S.）763号及本人前往上述地点，并将一名名为 Israel Shpiller 的外国人（俄罗斯人），38岁，男/商人，住法租界姐妹会路（Route des Soeurs）78号，带至本局。

经外国巡捕房（F.P.S.）32号 Wernberg、侦探巡捕房（D.P.S.）763号 Izumi 及本人讯问，查明如下情况：-

1940年5月4日下午5点左右，报案人在靠近外白渡桥的阿斯特路（Astor Road）与百老汇路拐角的终点站，登上了华中都市公共汽车公司第6路公共汽车（车牌号166），沿百老汇路由西向东行驶。

当到达百老汇路与南京路拐角的公交车站时，报案人下车，此时被被告从背后推搡。这引起报案人怀疑其右侧臀部口袋内的钱包被被告扒窃。

He immediately look back, when he observed that the accused was in the act of alighting from the bus, while he was being in possession of the described wallet and put same into the right pocket of his spring coat.

However, the pocket was not buttoned at the bottom of the pocket and then the described wallet was slipped and dropped on the floor of the bus.

At the same time, a bus conductor, female Chinese, named Sung Mei Mei (宋美美), No. 72 Conductor, witnessed this occurrence, picked up the wallet and handed same over to the complainant.

At the station, the accused, on being interrogated by detectives, admitted that he had picked the complainant's pocket of one black leather wallet containing Yen 5.00 and $4.00, whilst boarding the omnibus.

In view of the foregoing, a charge has been preferred against the accused with Pocket-picking under Art. 320 (1) of the C.C.C. and he will be arraigned before the S.S.D. Court on the morning of 6/5/40, when one week's remand will be requested for enabling detectives to make further enquiries into his past activities.

Remarks
(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be

At 2 p.m. 8-5-40, S. P. C. 433 on post duty on
Broadway, brought to the station the accused
described on sheet 1 of this report and reported
the following:

At about 1.50 p.m. even date whilst on his
post the above S.P.C. received in custody the
accused from two Japanese who stated that they had
arrested him for attempted pocket-picking. The two
alleged complainants also requested the above
officer to convey the culprit to the Police Station
and also said that they will call later on to make
the complaint. They did not gave their names or
addresses to S.P.C.

The suspect is well known criminal and on being
searched at the station was found to be in possession
of one razor blade specially used by the criminals
to cut the victim's pockets.

He is the resident of the French Concession and
could not give any satisfactory explanation for his
presence in this area.

The complainants failed to call at the station
and efforts were made to locate them when the
Japanese Consular Police, M.L. Party and Gendarmerie
Headquarters were communicated with, but without
results.

On 9-5-40, the accused will be brought before
the S.S.I. Court on a charge of Loitering.

1940年5月8日下午2:00，在百老汇路执勤的
上海公共租界巡捕（S. P. C.）433号，将本报告
第1页所述的被告带至警局，并报告如下：

同日约下午1:50，上述巡捕在执勤时，
从两名日本人手中接收了在押的被告，这两名日本人
称因涉嫌企图扒窃而逮捕了他。这两名所谓的
报案人还要求上述警官将罪犯送往警察局，
并表示稍后将前来报案。他们未向该巡捕
提供姓名或地址。

该嫌疑人是知名罪犯，在警局接受搜身时，
被发现持有一片剃须刀片，这是罪犯专门用来
割开受害者口袋的工具。

他是法租界居民，无法对其出现在该区域
给出任何令人满意的解释。

报案人未到警局，当局曾努力寻找他们，
并与日本领事警察、海军陆战队（M.L. Party）及
宪兵总部联系，但均无结果。

1940年5月9日，被告将以游荡罪被提解至
特区初级法院（S.S.I. Court）受审。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Eduardo Carlos appeared before the Execution Court of the S.S.D. Court No.1 about 9.30 a.m. on May 27, 1940 and the Judge on hearing the facts of his case remanded him to the morning of May 28, 1940 with a view to him finding a friend who would sign a bond to guarantee his future behaviour.

E. Carlos was questioned by the undersigned regarding the possibility of a friend acting as guarantor for him and he stated he thought Mr. Rudy Swelto, Italian, employed with the Salvation Army at Chaopoong Road would do the necessary. However, he was permitted to communicate with him by phone about 3 p.m. on May 27, 1940, and the latter refused to act as guarantor.

As previously explained in Diary No.3, E. Carlos is obviously in an unfortunate position as regards friends and is now left to the mercy of the Court as regards his future.

D.D.O. "C" Division.

爱德华多·卡洛斯（Eduardo Carlos）于1940年5月27日上午9时30分左右出庭受审，案件由第一特区法院执行法庭审理。法官在听取其案情陈述后，将其还押至1940年5月28日上午，以便其寻找一位愿意签署保释书以担保其日后行为的朋友。

下述签名人就是否有朋友愿为其担任保证人一事讯问了E. 卡洛斯，他表示认为鲁迪·斯韦尔托（Rudy Swelto）先生（意大利籍，受雇于兆丰路救世军）可以办理此事。然而，他获准于1940年5月27日下午3时左右通过电话与其联系，但后者拒绝担任保证人。

正如日志第3号中此前所述，E. 卡洛斯在朋友方面显然处境不幸，其未来只能听凭法庭处置。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

In connection with the accused Eduardo Carlos, unrecognised Mexican, age 18, who was sentenced to three months imprisonment on February 26th, 1940, full history of case referred to in attached case papers, was released from the S.M.C. Gaol on May 25th, 1940 and as per instructions from Court Inspector G.C. Moore, was detained at Hongkew Station on latter date to eventually re-appear before the S.S.D. Court at 9.30 a.m. on May 27th, 1940 and if possible a relative or friend, who will be responsible for him, to be located and attend Court at same time.

Eduardo Carlos was questioned by the undersigned to ascertain if he knew of any friend or relative who would stand as guarantor for his conduct on his release, but he frankly admitted he was unable to do so.

关于被告爱德华多·卡洛斯（Eduardo Carlos），一名18岁身份不明的墨西哥人，其于1940年2月26日被判处三个月监禁，案件完整经过见附卷宗，该犯于1940年5月25日从工部局监狱释放。根据法庭督察G.C. 摩尔（G.C. Moore）的指示，于同日将其拘留在虹口捕房，以便最终于1940年5月27日上午9时30分再次出庭受审于第一特区法院，并尽可能在此期间找到一名愿意对其负责的亲属或朋友，届时一同出庭。

下述签名人讯问了爱德华多·卡洛斯，以确定他是否认识任何愿意在其获释后为其行为作保的朋友或亲属，但他坦承无法做到。

At 9.25 p.m. on 24/2/40, F.P.S.616 brought

Enquiries were made by C.D.C.?22 and the
undersigned, when the following was ascertained:-

At the station, the accused, on being interro-
gated by detectives, admitted that he had stolen
the described property from a motor truck, Trade
Licence No.71, stationed in front of a Japanese
motor repairing shop at No.10 North Haining Road.

Led by the accused, detectives visited the
scene of the offence and located the owner of the
described property, which were later identified by
the owner as his own. The accused further was
questioned regarding other possible crimes, but
nothing further could be learned against him.

A charge accordingly has been preferred

At 2 p.m. on the 5/6/40, complainant S.
Tarshe koff, Russian, painter, residing 241/30
Chaof oong Road, came to the wayside Station and
reported that one named S. Lemasoff, Russian, 48,
M/mechanic, of N.F.A. misappropriated 6 wooden frames
quantity of oil paint, and 2 pawn papers total value
about $24.00 given to him by the complt. for safe
keeping on or about 20/5/40 at 39 Yuenchang Road,
the former residence of the complt. Preliminary
enquiries were made by D.S.I. Sigarson (W) and the
case subsequently transferred to this station.

Enquiries made by C.D.C.327 and the undersigned.
Complainant stated that whilst he was residing
at 39 Yuenchang Road on or about 20/5/40, the above
mentioned person called to the address and as the
complt. was sick at the time he handed over the men-
tioned property to that person for safe keeping but
the latter failed to return same back and now the
complt. learned that he disposed of the said property
for $15.00 and absconded.

S. Lemasoff is well known to the Police, being
previously charged for similar offences and it was
learned that for the last time he was residing in
Russian Shelter house, Tongshan Road but on visiting
the address he was not located in there and enquiries
show that he is not a permanent resident of the shel-
ter but occasionally comes to sleep in there.

Further enquiries proceeding with a view to
apprehend the offender.

D. S. I.

During the past few days, copies of a printed
handbill advocating the withdrawal or expulsion of
European and American armed forces from Shanghai, were
delivered through the post to a number of Chinese shops
on Robison Road and the extra-Settlement roads area in
the Western District. The envelope was addressed by
affixing a paper slip which appeared to have been cut
from the telephone book and which bore the name of the
shop to which the propaganda matter was sent.

This document purports to have emanated from
the "Shanghai Citizens' Federation (上海市民联合会)" which
name has not previously come to the notice of the
Municipal Police. Judging from the nature of the
propaganda matter, however, the Shanghai Western District
Citizens' Association, a pro-Wang Ching Wei organization
located at 652 Avenue Haig, O.O.L., is suspected of
being the source of the material.

A specimen of the handbill is attached together
with translation.

R.W. Mac Adie.

Translation of a handbill copies of
which were delivered through the post
to Chinese shops in the Western Dis-
trict towards the end of June, 1940.

The developments in the European War especially
following the Italian entry have aggravated the situation
in Shanghai due to the presence of British, American,
French and Italian soldiers who are on opposing sides and
will inevitably result in friction and conflict. Great
danger is in sight, and therefore we cannot speak of peace
and order so long as the soldiers of the combatant nations
remain in Shanghai.

For the maintenance of peace and order in Shanghai
and the protection of the life and property of the residents,
the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the New Central Govern-
ment has made an important declaration that China being a
neutral country and possessing rights over the settlements,
should negotiate with the combatant nations for the with-
drawal of their military and naval forces from Shanghai
within a short period. This declaration is sufficiently
reasonable. All citizens of the city should unite together
to back up the declaration and take appropriate measures to
urge the troops and naval ships of the combatant countries
to evacuate Shanghai. People should not believe the untrue
propaganda of the authorities of the combatant countries in
Shanghai who state that they have already reached an agree-
ment to maintain order in Shanghai and can ensure that no
conflict will take place between the soldiers of the combat-
ant countries in Shanghai. The Shanghai City Government
has made a similar declaration to that of the Central Govern-
ment, which shows that the latter is entirely in accord with
the local authorities in connection with this matter. If
once the troops and ships of the combatant nations in

欧洲战事的发展，特别是意大利参战后，由于身处对立阵营的英、美、法、意士兵的存在，加剧了上海的局势，不可避免地导致摩擦和冲突。巨大的危险近在眼前，因此，只要交战国的士兵仍留在上海，我们就无法谈论和平与秩序。

为了维护上海的和平与秩序，保护居民的生命财产安全，新中央政府外交部发表重要声明，指出中国作为中立国，拥有对租界的权利，应与交战国谈判，要求其军事和海军力量在短时间内撤离上海。这一声明是充分合理的。全市公民应团结一致，支持该声明，并采取适当措施，敦促交战国的军队和舰船撤离上海。人们不应相信在上海的交战国当局的不实宣传，他们声称已达成维持上海秩序的协议，并能确保在上海的交战国士兵之间不会发生冲突。上海市政府发表了与中央政府类似的声明，这表明中央政府在此事上与地方当局完全一致。一旦在上海的交战国军队和舰船

Special Branch,
June 29, 1940.

Anti-Foreign Propaganda

During the past few days, copies of a printed
handbill advocating the withdrawal or expulsion of
European and American armed forces from Shanghai, were
delivered through the post to a number of Chinese shops
on Robison Road and the extra-Settlement roads area in
the Western District. The envelope was addressed by
affixing a paper slip which appeared to have been cut
from the telephone book and which bore the name of the
shop to which the propaganda matter was sent.

This document purports to have emanated from
the "Shanghai Citizens' Federation (上海市民联合会)" which
name has not previously come to the notice of the
Municipal Police. Judging from the nature of the
propaganda matter, however, the Shanghai Western District
Citizens' Association, a pro-Wang Ching Wei organization
located at 652 Avenue Haig, O.O.L., is suspected of
being the source of the material.

A specimen of the handbill is attached together
with translation.

Certified true copy

J. I. Jones

排外宣传

在过去几天里，一些印有主张撤出或驱逐欧美武装部队离开上海的传单，通过邮政投递到了西区罗宾森路及越界筑路区域的一些中国商店。信封上的地址是通过粘贴从电话簿上剪下的纸条标明的，纸条上印有接收宣传材料的商店名称。

这份文件声称出自“上海市民联合会”，该名称此前未引起工部局警务处的注意。然而，根据宣传材料的性质判断，位于海格路652号、O.O.L.（原文不清，可能指某组织缩写）的亲汪精卫组织——上海西区市民协会，被怀疑是这些材料的来源。

传单样本及译文附后。

核证无误副本

J. I. Jones

page_data.en:
Translation of a handbill copies of
which were delivered through the post
to Chinese shops in the Western Dis-
trict towards the end of June, 1940.

The developments in the European War especially
following the Italian entry have aggravated the situation
in Shanghai due to the presence of British, American,
French and Italian soldiers who are on opposing sides and
will inevitably result in friction and conflict. Great
danger is in sight, and therefore we cannot speak of peace
and order so long as the soldiers of the combatant nations
remain in Shanghai.

For the maintenance of peace and order in Shanghai
and the protection of the life and property of the residents,
the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the New Central Govern-
ment has made an important declaration that China being a
neutral country and possessing rights over the settlements,
should negotiate with the combatant nations for the with-
drawal of their military and naval forces from Shanghai
within a short period. This declaration is sufficiently
reasonable. All citizens of the city should unite together
to back up the declaration and take appropriate measures to
urge the troops and naval ships of the combatant countries
to evacuate Shanghai. People should not believe the untrue
propaganda of the authorities of the combatant countries in
Shanghai who state that they have already reached an agree-
ment to maintain order in Shanghai and can ensure that no
conflict will take place between the soldiers of the comba-
tant countries in Shanghai. The Shanghai City Government
has made a similar declaration to that of the Central Govern-
ment, which shows that the latter is entirely in accord with
the local authorities in connection with this matter. If
once the troops and ships of the combatant nations in
Shanghai are evacuated, the citizens of Shanghai would
enjoy peace and safety.

Resort on June 20, 1940

"A" Cartoon depicting four German soldiers in pursuit
of a French soldier near a wall, on the other
side of which are shown three British soldiers
bolting the gates.
The French soldier says: "Mr. Britain, please
help me!"
One of the British soldiers says: "No, no."

"B" Cartoon showing the caricature of Herr Hitler
trampling on a fallen French Army officer with
the French standard lying on the ground.
Inscription follows: "Isn't it too late?"

In the upper left of the cartoon there is shown
in the background three men taking food with the
caption: "Great Britain is also facing a shortage
of food stuff," and in the foreground an English
man is seen directing another person to appeal
to the U.S. of America for assistance.

In the upper right of the cartoon there is shown
an American sitting on a chair saying: "Coming now."

"C" Cartoon showing on the left a person crying representing
Britain, holding a mask before two male Chinese. On
the right British soldiers are seen falling before a
German charge with the inscriptions: "The Tragedy of
Europe. The heralded British strength is no more.
Do not be deceived by his mask."

“A” 漫画描绘了四名德国士兵在一堵墙附近追捕一名法国士兵，墙的另一侧显示三名英国士兵正在闩上大门。
法国士兵说：“英国先生，请帮帮我！”
其中一名英国士兵说：“不，不。”

“B” 漫画显示希特勒先生（Herr Hitler）的 caricature（讽刺画）践踏着一名倒地的法国军官，法国国旗躺在地上。
题词如下：“是不是太晚了？”

在漫画的左上角，背景中显示三个人正在取食，配文为：“英国也面临食品短缺”，而在前景中，可以看到一名英国人正指示另一个人向美利坚合众国求助。

在漫画的右上角，显示一名美国人坐在椅子上说：“这就来。”

“C” 漫画左侧显示一名代表英国的人在两名中国男子面前拿着面具哭泣。右侧显示英国士兵在德国人的冲锋下倒下，题词为：“欧洲的悲剧。曾大肆宣扬的英国力量已不复存在。不要被他的面具所欺骗。”

of the New World Amusement Resort, Bubbling Well Road,

brown paper, had just been found on the Roof Garden

translation, are attached herewith.

scene regarding the identity of the person, or persons,
who deposited the bundle thereat but, it is possible,
that the intent was to scatter the pamphlets from the
Roof Garden onto the roadway beneath, their intention,
however, being frustrated by the approach of an
attendant.

Summarized translation of a handbill copies of which were
found posted on walls and power standards along Bubbling
Well and Nanking Roads on June 14, 1940.

Notification dated June 14, the 29th year of the
Republic of China of the "SPECIAL OPERATION CORPS FOR THE
EXTERMINATION OF TRAITORS OF THE MILITARY AFFAIRS
COMMISSION OF THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT FOR DUTY IN
SHANGHAI"

Three years have elapsed since the enemy
invaded our national territories. The enemy troops
are now exhausted but they are still struggling as
a last effort to achieve their aggressive ambition.
The current Chinese victory over the enemy in Southern
Honan and Northern Hupeh has proved conclusively that
the longer we fight on, the more powerful we become,
and a general counter-offensive campaign may be expected
at any time. Realizing that China is unconquerable,
the enemy has been utilizing one puppet after the other
during the past two years but none of the Chinese
traitors have served the purpose of effecting "PEACE"
which is their ostensible aim.

The worst of those traitors are the traitorous
merchants who made their fortunes by taking advantage of
the national crisis of their country. They are engaged
in speculation, cornering of commodities, hoarding of
vital necessities, and manipulations of every kind.
They suck the sweat and blood of their brethren in order
to swell their own pockets. They assist in effecting
the circulation of Chinese legal tender notes/in the
occupied areas thereby intensifying the enemy's economic
aggression towards China. Their traitorous deeds are
indeed too numerous to enumerate.

In accordance with the instructions of the
Supreme Command, this Corps is to take drastic action
page_data.zh:
1940年6月14日在静安寺路（Bubbling Well）和南京路沿线墙壁及电力线杆上发现的传单副本摘要译文。

“国民政府军事委员会驻沪肃清汉奸特种行动队”发布的通告，日期为中华民国二十九年六月十四日

敌人入侵我国领土已三年。敌军现已筋疲力尽，但仍作最后挣扎以实现其侵略野心。目前中国在豫南和鄂北对敌取得的胜利确凿地证明，我们战斗得越久，力量就越强大，全面反攻战役随时可能展开。敌人意识到中国是不可征服的，在过去两年中利用了一个又一个傀儡，但没有一个中国汉奸能够实现其表面上的目标——“和平”。

这些汉奸中最恶劣的是那些利用国家危机发财的奸商。他们从事投机活动，垄断商品，囤积生活必需品，并进行各种操纵。他们吸食同胞的血汗以充实自己的腰包。他们协助在占领区流通中国法币纸币，从而加剧敌人对中国的经济侵略。他们的叛国罪行确实不胜枚举。

根据最高统帅部的指示，本队将对

page_data.en:
- 2 -

against those traitorous merchants in Shanghai. Our
mission is to protect and to ensure the existence of the
3,500000 Shanghai citizens. All merchants are hereby
notified to heed this warning or to take the
consequences.

Captain WEI KIANG.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

上海的这些奸商采取严厉行动。我们的使命是保护并确保350万上海市民的生存。特此通知所有商人注意此警告，否则后果自负。

队长 魏江（WEI KIANG，音译）。

一幅漫画描绘了一名英国男子和一名“男孩”在舞厅里。漫画中插入了一幅城市建筑物遭受猛烈轰炸的素描。“男孩”说：“你家着火了”，而英国人说：“那太糟糕了！”

Louza Districts on June 15, 1940.

A cartoon depicting a boat with an
inscription of "Shanghai Settlement" on it.
On the boat an Italian is fighting with a
Britisher. An American is also sitting on
the boat saying "Fighting on this small boat
is very annoying to the bystanders", while a
Chinese says : "Disputants to go to their own
countries".
page_data.zh:
1940年6月15日在中央区和老闸区发现的漫画译文。

一幅漫画描绘了一艘船，船上写有“上海租界”字样。船上有一名意大利人正在与一名英国人打斗。一名美国人也坐在船上说：“在这艘小船上打架让旁观者非常厌烦”，而一名中国人说：“争吵者回各自的国家去”。

page_data.en:
Translation of Cartoon found in central and
Louza Districts on June 15, 1940.

A cartoon entitled "Alas! It is said
that the British and French Governments are
removing their capitals", depicting a building
inscribed with the Chinese characters "The
British Government". On the top of the building
is flown the Nazi Swastika Standard while
aeroplanes are bombing the nearby building in
the background. On the foreground of the cartoon
are fully loaded motor trucks inscribed with the
Chinese characters "The British Government"
leaving the compound of the building. A man
carrying an attache case inscribed with the
characters "The British Government" is
conversing with another man carrying a case
inscribed with the characters "The French
Government". The man represented as the
British says : "We are removing to Calcutta",
while the man represented as the Frenchman says:
"We are removing to Hanoi on account of the
heavy bombardment".

一幅题为“唉！听说英法政府正在迁都”的漫画，描绘了一座建筑物，上面刻有汉字“英国政府”。建筑物顶部飘扬着纳粹卐字旗，同时飞机正在轰炸背景中的附近建筑物。漫画前景是满载的卡车，上面刻有汉字“英国政府”，正离开该建筑的大院。一名提着刻有“英国政府”字样的公文包的男子正在与另一名提着刻有“法国政府”字样的公文包的男子交谈。代表英国的人说：“我们要搬往加尔各答”，而代表法国的人说：“由于轰炸猛烈，我们要搬往河内”。

At 9 a.m. 30/8/40, the complainant
brought to the station the accused described on
Sheet 1 of this report whom he had arrested for
larceny of one radio set value $200.00 from the
shop at 81 Seward Road.
From enquiries made the following was
ascertained:-
The complainant is the shop assistant
in the radio shop at the above address. There are
several more shop assistants working in the shop
and at about 8.45 a.m. even date, all of them were
busy in the rear part of the shop. About 10 radio
sets are always displayed on the counter in the shop
front door of which is always kept open during
business hours.
At about 8.45 a.m. the complainant entered
the shop through the rear door and had noticed a
foreigner leaving the shop and carrying a radio set
away.
The complainant asked the shop assistants
as to who attended this customer but received nega-
tive answer.
The complainant rushed away, gave a chase
and detained the accused about two blocks away from
the shop.
Immediately the complainant identified the
radio set as his own and stolen from his shop.
On being brought to the station and ques-
tioned the accused admitted the crime.
The accused is well known criminal and
page_data.zh:
1940年8月30日上午9时，投诉人将本报告第1页所述的被告带到巡捕房，该被告因从西华德路81号的商店盗窃一台价值200.00美元的收音机而被捕。
经查询，查明以下情况：
投诉人是上述地址无线电商店的店员。店内还有几名其他店员，当天上午8时45分左右，他们都在商店后部忙碌。店前柜台上通常陈列着约10台收音机，营业期间店门一直敞开。
上午8时45分左右，投诉人通过后门进入商店，注意到一名外国人离开商店并带走一台收音机。
投诉人询问店员是谁接待了这位顾客，但得到了否定的回答。
投诉人冲出去追赶，并在距离商店两个街区的地方扣留了被告。
投诉人立即认出该收音机是其自己的，并从其商店被盗。
被告被带到巡捕房并接受讯问后，承认了罪行。
被告是众所周知的罪犯，并且

page_data.en:
1/3

was released from gaol only 3 weeks ago.
He was interrogated re other crimes recently
reported to this station, but strongly denied commit-
ing any.
Charged accordingly.

Sen. Det. 1/c.                D. S. I.
page_data.zh:
1/3

仅在3周前从监狱释放。
他就最近向本巡捕房报告的其他罪行接受了审讯，但强烈否认犯有任何罪行。
据此提出指控。

高级侦探 1/c。                副督察长。

At 5.15 p.m. 17-9-40, the complt. reported at
this station being assaulted by two Russian and
eventually raped by one of them on Hsian Road near
Seward Road.

Enquiries were made by the undersigned and
the following facts were ascertained.

The complt. is one Mrs. F.Z. Platt, Russian,
working as a waitress in a small Russian Restaurant
at 771/2 Av. Joffre and residing on that premises.

At about 11 p.m. 16-9-40, the two accused
described on sheet 1 of this report had visited
the restaurant and were attended by the complt.
After having their food the accused offered the
complt. to go for a joy ride in the 1st accused's
m/car and the complt. agreed to that. The 1st
accused is the owner of a m/car with which he
is usually touting for a hire in Hongkew District.

At first the complt. and two accused
proceeded to one of the restaurants on Route Vallon
and drank some vodka and two bottles of beer.
After that they proceeded in a m/car to Northern
Area and the 2nd accused drove the car. When passing
along Hsian Road near Seward Road, the 2nd accused
suddenly stopped the m/car and the 1st accused
insists on carnal knowledge of the complt. She
strongly refused and then the both accused started
to beat her on the face and body with their clenched
fists during which assault the 2nd accused struck
her over the head with some iron object. The complt.
shouted for help but this time the 1st accused lay
page_data.zh:
1940年9月17日下午5时15分，原告向本局报案，称在西康路近华德路处遭到两名俄国人的袭击，并最终被其中一人强奸。

经下述人员调查，查明以下事实。

原告为 F.Z. Platt 夫人，俄国人，在霞飞路771/2号的一家小型俄式餐馆担任女服务员，并居住在该处。

1940年9月16日晚11时许，本报告第一页所述的两名被告光顾该餐馆，由原告提供服务。用餐后，被告邀请原告乘坐第一被告的汽车去兜风，原告表示同意。第一被告拥有一辆汽车，他通常用该车在虹口区招揽租车生意。

起初，原告与两名被告前往瓦隆路（Route Vallon）上的一家餐馆，喝了一些伏特加和两瓶啤酒。随后，他们乘汽车前往北区，由第二被告驾驶车辆。当行驶至西康路近华德路时，第二被告突然停车，第一被告强行要求与原告发生性关系。原告强烈拒绝，随后两名被告开始用紧握的拳头殴打她的面部和身体，在此袭击过程中，第二被告用某种铁器击打她的头部。原告呼救，但此时第一被告掐住

page_data.en:
1/3.

hold of her throat and she lost her consciousness. Next
she remember that when she had recovered the 1st accused
was in the act of sexual intercourse with her. After
this the 2nd accused insists on intercourse also but
the complt. rushed away, but succeeded in running only
a few yards when the two culprits grabbed hold of her
placed her in the m/car, drove some a few blocks, threw
out the complt. from the m/car and disappeared. Having
no money in her possession the complt. walked home and
then reported the occurrence to the French Police. As
the offence occurred in the Settlement the complt. was
at first brought to Wayside Station. After making
preliminary enquiries the detectives attached to Wayside
Station effected the arrest of the 1st accused at his
home No.124B/8 Rue Lafayette and handed him over to
Hongkew Station. The address of the 2nd accused was
visited but he was not at home but eventually at about
7 p.m. 17-9-40, he came to the Lukawei Station where
he was detained and handed over to this station.

On being questioned at the station the 1st accused
admitted taking the complt. in his m/car to North of
Creek but could not remember as to what happened after
that as he was very drunk. The 2nd accused also admitted
going together with the complt. and the 1st accused in
the m/car to North of Creek, but strongly denied taking
page_data.zh:
1/3.

她的喉咙，导致她失去知觉。接下来她记得，当她恢复意识时，第一被告正在与她进行性交。此后，第二被告也要求进行性交，但原告挣脱逃跑，然而仅跑出几码远，两名罪犯便抓住她，将她塞进汽车，行驶了几个街区后，将原告从车上扔下并逃离现场。由于身无分文，原告步行回家，随后向法国警察报案。由于案发地点在租界内，原告最初被带到路边巡捕房（Wayside Station）。经初步问询后，隶属于路边巡捕房的侦探在第一被告家中（拉斐德路124B/8号）将其逮捕，并移交给虹口巡捕房。随后探访了第二被告的住址，但他不在家，最终在1940年9月17日晚7时许，他来到卢家湾巡捕房，在那里被拘留并移交给本局。

在警局受讯时，第一被告承认用他的汽车将原告载至苏州河北岸，但因醉酒严重，记不清之后发生的事情。第二被告也承认与原告及第一被告一同乘车前往苏州河北岸，但坚决否认参与

page_data.en:
1/4.

part i. the assault and rape of the complt.
The complt. was sent to the General Hospital and
doctor's chit reads as follows:
"Contusion of the right temporal region, both
ocular regions and the left sub-maxillary. No
clinical evidence of fractured lower jaw.
As to the alleged rape: No nail scratches or
other signs of violence were noted near the
genitals.
There are some minor marks of contusion around
both knees.
The external genitalia are normal coloured with
no marks of violence such as an introduction
of a rigid body would produce. The examined
field was clean and free from blood or sperm
clots.
As the woman was married and had children
according to her words and the clinical
evidence, no definite conclusion is possible.
A normal coition having taken place at 11 p.m.
yesterday would leave no traces to-day at the
time of examination, i.e. 6.05 p.m."
On 18-9-40, the both accused will be brought before
the S.S.D. Court when a charge of Assault will be
preferred against them and also additional charge of
Rape will be preferred against the 1st accused.

“右颞区、双眼区及左颌下区挫伤。无下颌骨折的临床证据。
关于所谓的强奸：生殖器附近未发现指甲抓痕或其他暴力痕迹。
双膝周围有一些轻微的挫伤痕迹。
外生殖器颜色正常，无诸如插入硬物所产生的暴力痕迹。检查区域清洁，无血液或精液凝块。
鉴于该妇女自称已婚并育有子女，且结合临床证据，无法得出确切结论。
若昨晚11时发生过正常的性交行为，在今日检查时（即下午6:05）不会留下任何痕迹。”

At 10.30 a.m. 19/9/40, the complainant with
the assistance of S.P.C.262 brought to the station
the accused described on sheet 1 of this report,
whom he had arrested for larceny of $20.00 in the
Japanese m/bus outside the General Post Office.
The complainant reported the following:-
At about 10 a.m. even date, he boarded the
Japanese m/bus on Seward Road near Kungping Road,
having in his hip pocket $75.00 in notes. The
m/bus was overcrowded and the complt. was com-
pelled to stand. When on E.Soochow Road near
Szechuen Road Bridge, he felt that someone had
interfered with his hip pocket. He looked round
and observed the accused standing behind him.
Immediately the complainant checked his
money and discovered a shortage of $20.00 (Two
$10.00 notes). At this time the m/bus stopped
outside the Post Office, the accused rushed away
but the complt. grabbed hold of him and the same time /
he(complt) had noticed one $10.00 note being
discarded by the accused.
The Japanese m/bus inspector was called, who
searched the accused and found in his pocket
neither $10.00 note and 20 cents.
With the assistance of S.P.C.262 the accused
was brought to the station. The accused is well
known criminal with many previous convictions.
On being questioned he denied the offence.
He is resident of the French Concession and could
not give any reasonable explanation for his
presence in this area. Charged accordingly.

W.J. Smith

1940年9月19日上午10时30分，原告在巡捕 S.P.C.262 的协助下，将本报告第一页所述的被告带至警局。该被告因涉嫌在邮政总局外的日本公共汽车上盗窃20.00元而被捕。
原告报告如下：-
当日约上午10时，他在公平路近华德路的日本公共汽车上上车，臀部口袋里有75.00元纸币。公共汽车拥挤不堪，原告被迫站立。当车行至苏州东路近四川路桥时，他感到有人触碰他的臀部口袋。他环顾四周，发现被告站在他身后。
原告立即检查钱财，发现少了20.00元（两张10.00元纸币）。此时公共汽车停在邮政总局外，被告试图逃跑，但原告抓住了他，同时原告注意到被告丢弃了一张10.00元纸币。
日本公共汽车查票员被叫来，搜查了被告，在其口袋中既未找到那张10.00元纸币，也未找到20分硬币。
在巡捕 S.P.C.262 的协助下，被告被带至警局。被告是众所周知的罪犯，有多次前科记录。
经讯问，他否认犯罪行为。他是法租界居民，无法对其出现在该区域给出任何合理解释。据此提出指控。

W.J. Smith

At 2.30 a.m. on 1/10/40, Constable Kawano,
of the Japanese Consular Police, accompanied by
Mr. S. Ogawa, residing No. 44 Ang Moh Li, Heskell
Road, brought to the station the accused V. M.
Neveroff, 31, Russian, who had been arrested by
Mr. Ogawa, who had found him loitering in the
alleyway outside his home. It appears that Mr.
Ogawa, on 29/9/40, was the victim of a burglary
property value $400.00 being stolen from his home
(vide H. S.I. 2206/40), therefore he had reasona-
ble cause to suspect the accused who was very
poorly dressed and was only able to explain his
presence in the alleyway, by stating that he was
searching for the home of a Japanese friend, but
could give no reasonable explanation why he wished
to see the alleged friend at such an early hour
of the morning.

There being no doubt whatsoever that the
accused who admits having been previously convicted
was intent on committing felony, he has been
charged with Loitering and will appear before the
S.S.D. Court on the a.m. of 1/10/40, when a remand
will be requested.

1940年10月1日（1/10/40）凌晨2时30分，日本领事馆警察川野巡捕（Constable Kawano）在居住于赫司克路（Heskell Road）安茂里44号的小川先生（Mr. S. Ogawa）陪同下，将被告V. M. Neveroff（31岁，俄国人）带至警局。该被告系由小川先生逮捕，小川先生发现其在家门外的小巷中徘徊。据悉，小川先生曾于1940年9月29日遭遇入室盗窃，家中失窃财物价值400.00美元（参见 H. S.I. 2206/40），因此他有合理理由怀疑衣着极为破旧的被告。被告对其出现在小巷中的解释仅是正在寻找一位日本朋友的家，但无法合理解释为何要在如此清晨的时段去见这位所谓的朋友。

鉴于被告承认有前科，且毫无疑问意图犯重罪，现以“游荡”罪名对其提出指控。被告将于1940年10月1日上午出庭受审于特别巡捕房法庭（S.S.D. Court），届时将申请还押候审。

a) 盗窃无人看管的自行车。

page_data.en:
At 9.45 a.m. on 30/10/40, C.D.S.33, whilst
passing along East Seward Road near Nanking Road,
effected the arrest of accused Kagan Sokoloff,
Russian, whom he found riding on a public ricksha,
in possession of a locked bicycle S.M.C.Lic.No.7520,
which he admitted having stolen.

The accused led detectives to a cable office
No.4 Peking Road, outside of which building he stated
he had stolen the machine. The complt. Sung Tah Sze
(沈达智), messenger boy employed at the cable office
was found standing outside and admitted that his
bicycle had been stolen, he already having reported
the theft to Central Station, vide the F.I.R.3384/40.

The accused stated that he found the bicycle
unsecured and rode it into the Hongkew area where
he intended to sell it to some Chinese on the street,
however, he accidentally closed a patent lock on the
rear wheel of the machine and thus was obliged to
hire a ricksha.

He also admitted the theft of one other
bicycle from outside No.72 Nanking Road, on 19/10/40,
vide Central F.I.R.3370/40, in this case he sold the
bicycle for $5.00, to an unknown Chinese on East
Seward Road.

Accused will be charged with both offences
upon his appearance before the C.M.Court on the
a.m. of 31/10/40.
page_data.zh:
1940年10月30日上午9时45分，C.D.S.33 警员在经过南京路附近的东熙华德路（East Seward Road）时，逮捕了被告 Kagan Sokoloff（俄国人）。当时发现被告正乘坐一辆公共黄包车，并持有一辆上锁的自行车（工部局执照号码 7520），被告承认该自行车系其偷窃所得。

被告带领侦探前往北京路4号的一家电报局，称其在该建筑物外偷窃了这辆自行车。投诉人沈达智（Sung Tah Sze，原文注：沈达智），系受雇于该电报局的信童，被发现站在外面，并承认其自行车被盗，他此前已向中央捕房报案，参见首次调查报告（F.I.R.）3384/40。

被告称，他发现该自行车未上锁，便骑车进入虹口地区，打算在街上卖给一些中国人，然而，他意外地锁上了后轮上的专利锁，因此不得不雇用一辆黄包车。

他还承认于1940年10月19日在南京路72号外偷窃了另一辆自行车，参见中央捕房首次调查报告（F.I.R.）3370/40，在此案中，他以5.00美元的价格将该自行车卖给了东熙华德路上的一名不知名中国人。

被告将于1940年10月31日上午出庭受审于中央混合法庭（C.M. Court），届时将对这两项罪行提出指控。

page_data.en:
At 9.40 p.m. 6/11/40, a telephone message was
received from the Japanese Consular Police, Boone Rd.
to the effect that at about 9.10 p.m. on 6/11/40,
two male Russians had been arrested on premises No.
29 Shing Kung Lee off Boone Road, on suspicion of
attempted larceny.

Upon receipt of this message, D.P.S.Kusumoto
and I.P.C. Sugano attended and received custody of
two foreigners namely:- (1) V.N.Yakovleff, age 28,
Russian, s/unemployed, N. F. A. (2) A.S.Gunshevicb,
age 28, Russian, s/unemployed, N. F. A.

Enquiries revealed that the two above-mentioned
persons had at 9.10 p.m. even date, been arrested by
complainant Mr.K.Sugiura, who had found them illegal-
ly trespassing on his premises No.29 Shing Kung Lee
off Boone Road. It appears that the complainant
upon returning home found the 1st accused in a
corridor on the ground floor which leads to his room
on 1st floor and suspecting that he was there for
no lawful intent seized hold of him and afterwards
effected the arrest of 2nd accused who he also found
lurking on the ground floor. The accused upon being
questioned admitted that they had previous convictions
and were in fact released from gaol a few days ago
and had received from Salvation Army clothing and
$5.00 cash. The money they had spent on drink and
at the time of arrest were intoxicated and did know
that they were trespassing on private premises.

However, in view of the fact that both accused
page_data.zh:
1940年11月6日晚上9时40分，接到来自北四川路日本领事馆警察的电话留言，称1940年11月6日晚上9时10分左右，两名俄国男子因涉嫌企图盗窃，在北四川路旁兴公里29号的场所内被捕。

收到此消息后，久米本侦探副督察（D.P.S. Kusumoto）和菅野巡长（I.P.C. Sugano）前往现场，接管了两名外国人，即：(1) V.N. Yakovleff，28岁，俄国人，职业：无业，N. F. A. (2) A.S. Gunshevicb，28岁，俄国人，职业：无业，N. F. A.

经查询得知，上述两人于同日晚上9时10分被投诉人 K. Sugiura 先生逮捕，投诉人发现他们非法侵入其位于北四川路旁兴公里29号的场所。据悉，投诉人回家时，发现第一被告在一楼通往其二楼房间的走廊里，怀疑其居心不良，遂将其抓住，随后又逮捕了同样被发现潜伏在一楼的第二被告。被告在接受讯问时承认有前科，事实上几天前刚出狱，并从救世军那里获得了衣物和5.00美元现金。他们将钱花在饮酒上，被捕时处于醉酒状态，并不知道他们正在侵入私人场所。

然而，鉴于两名被告

the complt's premises for the purposes of committing
crime, therefore both have been charged and will appear
before the S.S.D.Court on the morning of 7/11/40.

At 7.45 a.m. 20/11/40, the complainant brought
to the station the accused described on sheet 1 of
this report whom he had found loitering on the stair
case of the 5th floor at House 8, Lane 297 Range Rd.
Inquiries by C.D.C. 87 and the undersigned.
The complainant is the coolie employed at the
Tsung Woc Hospital at the above address.
On 19/11/40 it was discovered that four brass
handles value $20.00 on the stair case in the
building were wrenched off and taken away by some
one, therefore the complainant was instructed by
his employer (Japanese) to examine the doors on the
building every morning.
At about 7.30 a.m. 20/11/40 the complainant
whilst on observation saw the accused interfering
with the door handle on 5th floor and brought him
to the station.
The accused is narcotic addict with several
previous convictions. On being questioned he
admitted stealing the door handles and disposing
same to an unknown street hawker on Peking Road.
Charged accordingly.

由 C.D.C. 87 警员及签署人进行调查。
投诉人是受雇于上述地址同文医院（Tsung Woc Hospital）的苦力。
1940年11月19日，有人发现大楼楼梯间的四个铜把手（价值20.00美元）被人撬走，因此投诉人受其雇主（日本人）指示，每天早晨检查大楼内的门窗。
1940年11月20日上午7时30分左右，投诉人在观察时发现被告正在摆弄五楼的门把手，遂将其带至警局。
被告是吸毒成瘾者，有多次前科。在接受讯问时，他承认偷窃了门把手，并将其卖给了北京路上的一名不知名街头小贩。
据此提出指控。

page_data.en:
At 10.30 a.m. 21/11/40, acting on information
received the undersigned and C.P.C.34 proceeded to
No.18, Lane 149 Yuenfong Road and arrested one named
Fedor Gomostneff, 78, Russian, s/unemployed,
of N.I.A. (now the accused)
who at the time of arrest was found in possession of
one leather handbag. On being questioned the accused
admitted that he stole same from a foreign dwelling
house in one of terraces off Seward Road and led
detectives to House 21, Lane 645 Seward Road,
foreign boarding house and explained how he at about
4 a.m. 21/11/40 entered the said premises whilst the
occupants were asleep, via closed but unsecured rear
door, then proceeded upstairs and stole 2 pairs of
rubber boots, one piece of ham and above mentioned
handbag from a storage room on the drying stage of
the premises.
Complainant one Mrs. T.Ogvrikova, Russian,
boarding house keeper, residing above address was
located at Wayside Police Station reporting the
mentioned theft in the Charge Room and identified
the recovered handbag as her own. The accused on
being further questioned re other stolen property
admitted that he sold 2 pairs of rubber boots to
an unknown second-hand hawker on Seward Road for
$6.00 but all efforts to locate that hawker were of
no avail. Further accused admitted that a piece
of ham he sold to a small Russian restaurant and
led detectives to 37 Nanchang Road, small restaurant
operated by J.Idnitsin, above address, who on being
page_data.zh:
1940年11月21日上午10时30分，根据收到的情报，签署人和 C.P.C.34 警员前往元丰路149弄18号，逮捕了一名名为 Fedor Gomostneff（原文注：现指被告），78岁，俄国人，职业：无业，N.I.A. 的人。
逮捕时，发现被告持有一个皮手提包。经讯问，被告承认是从熙华德路旁某排屋的一户外国人家中偷得此包，并带领侦探前往熙华德路645弄21号的外国寄宿舍，解释了他如何于1940年11月21日凌晨4时左右，趁住户熟睡之际，通过关闭但未上锁的后门进入该场所，然后上楼，从该场所晾晒间的储藏室偷走了2双橡胶靴、一块火腿和上述手提包。
投诉人 T. Ogvrikova 夫人（俄国人，寄宿舍管理人，居住于上述地址）在路边警亭的报案室报告了上述盗窃案，并辨认出追回的手提包是她的。在对其他被盗财物进行进一步讯问时，被告承认以6.00美元的价格将2双橡胶靴卖给了熙华德路上的一名不知名二手小贩，但寻找该小贩的一切努力均无结果。此外，被告承认将一块火腿卖给了一家小型俄餐馆，并带领侦探前往南昌路37号，该餐馆由 J. Idnitsin 经营，上述地址，J. Idnitsin 在接受

page_data.en:
1/3

questioned admitted that at about 9 am 21/11/40 the accused
offered him a piece of ham for $10.00 and he agreed to
buy the same and gave $10.00 to the accused who issued
him a receipt. As the price paid by the restaurant
proprietor for that ham was quite reasonable and who
on being questioned strongly denied any guilty knowledge
that the property had been stolen, there is not suffi-
cient evidence to support a charge of receiving against
him. The money paid by the restaurant proprietor to the
accused were found on the accused and returned to the
former, who handed over the ham in question to the
detectives.

The accused admitted that $8.00 received by him
from disposal of rubber boots he had spent in a Korean
heroin den, where he was arrested, on buying heroin for
himself and his friends.

The accused charged accordingly and will appear
before the S.S.D. Court on the morning of the 22/11/40,
when one week remand will be requested to enable
detectives to make further enquiries re past activities
of the accused who is known to the Police as a criminal.

Sen. Det. 1/6.

D. D. O. "G".

M. Faloon
D.S.I.

1/3

讯问时承认，1940年11月21日上午9时左右，被告向他提供一块火腿，售价10.00美元，他同意购买并支付给被告10.00美元，被告向其出具了收据。由于餐馆老板支付的那块火腿的价格相当合理，且他在接受讯问时强烈否认明知该财物是赃物，因此没有足够的证据支持对他提出收赃指控。餐馆老板支付给被告的钱款在被告身上被发现，并已退还给前者，后者将涉案火腿移交给侦探。

被告承认，他从处置橡胶靴中获得的8.00美元，是在一家朝鲜海洛因馆（他在此处被捕）为自己和朋友购买海洛因时花掉的。

据此对被告提出指控，他将于1940年11月22日上午出庭受审于特别巡捕房法庭（S.S.D. Court），届时将申请还押一周，以便侦探对被告过去的活动进行进一步调查，警方已知该被告为罪犯。

November 25th, 40.

1.

Detention of three Russian suspects.

Information was received to the effect that several
Russian criminals who probably are responsible for some
crimes committed recently, gathered together in a Chinese
house at 80 Yuancheng Road.

A Party of Police consisting of D.S.I.s Fedoroff and
Beloshenko and C.D.C.s 222 and 251 visited the place and
in one of the upstairs rooms located three male and one
female Russians and one Chinese who on being brought to
the station gave their names as follows:

1. Nikolai Kotoft, 38, Russian, s/unemployed, N.F.A.,
well known criminal.
2. Anatoly Vasilieff, 28, Russian, u/unemployed, N.F.A.,
also criminal.
3. George Balikoff, 38, Russian, s/unemployed, N.F.A.
4. Tatiana Chladnikova, 21, Russian, u/unemployed,
residing at 19 Souchow Road.
5. Tsang Su Hsing (張守松) 42, Shantung, s/unemployed,
former convict.

The room where the above persons were located is
occupied by a Chinese who was not at home at the time
when the place was visited. The 4th suspect is a
prostitute by profession and on being questioned stated
that her reason to visit the above place was to locate
her former sweet heart one named V. Martinoff whom she
wants to return her pawn tickets.

G.S.G

拘留三名俄罗斯嫌疑人。

接获情报称，几名可能对近期发生的一些犯罪负责的俄罗斯罪犯，聚集在元成路（Yuancheng Road）80号的一户中国人家中。

由警佐 Fedoroff 和 Beloshenko 以及华捕队长（C.D.C.s）222号和251号组成的警察小队前往该地，在楼上的一间房间里发现了三名俄罗斯男性、一名俄罗斯女性和一名中国人，将他们带回警局后，他们报出的姓名如下：

1. Nikolai Kotoft，38岁，俄罗斯人，单身/无业，N.F.A.，知名罪犯。
2. Anatoly Vasilieff，28岁，俄罗斯人，未婚/无业，N.F.A.，也是罪犯。
3. George Balikoff，38岁，俄罗斯人，单身/无业，N.F.A.
4. Tatiana Chladnikova，21岁，俄罗斯人，未婚/无业，
   居住在苏州路（Souchow Road）19号。
5. Tsang Su Hsing (張守松)，42岁，山东人，单身/无业，
   前科犯。

发现上述人员的房间由一名中国人居住，警察到访时此人不在家。第4名嫌疑人为职业妓女，在接受讯问时陈述，她前往上述地点的目的是为了寻找她的前情人，一名叫 V. Martinoff 的人，她想让他归还她的当票。

At 4 p.m. 26-11-40, telephone message was
received from Japanese Consular Police reporting
that Russian female was arrested for larceny and
wanted to hand her over to the S.M.P.

C.D.C. 274, D.P.S. 775 and the undersigned
attended and brought to the station one Anna
Kunevitch, (now-the-accused) 41 Russian, m/female,
residing 225/18 Kungping Road, (now the accused)
and complt. Mrs. M. Morisaki, Japanese, shop keeper,
202 Haining Road.

Enquiries show that at about 3.50 p.m. 26-11-40,
the accused entered the tailor shop, 202 Haining Road,
together with two other foreign females and whilst
the latters were speaking to the Japanese shop
assistant regarding value of various materials which
were stored on the shop counter, the accused removed
one roll of cloth value $250.00 from the counter and
put same under her coat.

One of shop assistants Ying Tah Shing (戴德兴)
observed the action of the accused and informed his
employer (the complt.) who got a hold of the accused
when the latter left the shop and called for a ricksha.
At the same time the other two females left the shop and
decamped in unknown direction.

The stolen roll of cloth was found by the complt.
under the overcoat of the accused who informed Japanese
Consular Police Sub Station located in vicinity of
the shop and the accused was brought to that sub
station where from the station was informed by
telephone as already stated above.
page_data.zh:
1940年11月26日下午4点，接到日本领事警察的电话消息，报告称一名俄罗斯女性因盗窃罪被捕，并希望将其移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）。

华捕队长（C.D.C.）274号、副巡官（D.P.S.）775号及签署人前往现场，将一名 Anna Kunevitch（现即被告），41岁，俄罗斯人，已婚/女性，居住在公平路（Kungping Road）225/18号，（现即被告）以及报案人 M. Morisaki太太，日本人，店主，海宁路202号，带回警局。

调查显示，1940年11月26日下午3点50分左右，被告与另外两名外籍女性进入海宁路202号的裁缝店，当那两名女性就存放在柜台上的各种布料的价值与日本店员交谈时，被告从柜台上拿走了一卷价值250.00美元的布料，并将其藏在大衣下。

一名店员 Ying Tah Shing (戴德兴) 观察到了被告的行为，并告知其雇主（即报案人），当被告离开店铺并叫黄包车时，报案人抓住了被告。与此同时，另外两名女性离开店铺，逃往未知方向。

报案人在被告的大衣下发现了被盗的那卷布料，被告随即通知了位于店铺附近的日本领事警察分署，被告被带到该分署，随后如上所述通过电话通知了本警局。

page_data.en:
1/3.

The accused on being questioned by detectives
strongly denied having any accomplices with her and
no definite description was obtained from the shop
assistant mentioned above and Japanese shop assistant
in the shop.

The accused denied the offence but could not give
any satisfactory explanation why she entered the shop
in question.

Enquiries show that the accused is the wife of well
known criminal who is serving his sentence at present
at the Ward Road Gaol.

The accused charged accordingly and will appear
before the S.S.D. Court on the morning of the 27-11-40,
when one week remand will be requested to enable detectives
to make further enquiries regarding her past activities.

被告否认该项罪行，但无法对其为何进入该店铺给出任何令人满意的解释。

调查显示，被告是一名知名罪犯的妻子，该罪犯目前正在华德路监狱（Ward Road Gaol）服刑。

被告因此被起诉，并将于1940年11月27日上午出庭于特别市政法庭（S.S.D. Court），届时将请求延期一周还押，以便侦探对其过去的活动进行进一步调查。

被告有两次前科记录。
有必要提及的是，1940年11月28日，在将被告移送至华德路监狱羁押之前，由女助理克鲁金小姐（Miss Klukin）在警局对其进行搜身时，在其口中发现了5张当票。经侦探调查，追回了被告在下列当铺典当的以下财物：

泰兴当铺，东熙华德路636号。
1) 布料一匹，于1940年10月6日以20.00元典当，估值约30.00元。

宏安当铺，法租界霞飞路742号。
2) 鞋子一双，于1940年11月23日以7.00元典当，估值约25.00元。

仁泰当铺，东熙华德路691号。
3) 布料一匹，于1940年9月20日以25.00元典当，估值约40.00元。

至于另外两张当票，分别涉及在上述当铺于1940年11月18日和11月20日以50.00元和5.00元典当的一个金十字架和一个旧平底熨斗，经查证该些财物确系被告个人财产，已退还给相应当铺，当票则列入被告被搜获的物品中。

page_data.en:
2/2.

The above mentioned 2 lengths of cloth and one
pr. of shoes are new ones and were undoubtedly stolen
by the accused from various shops in Shanghai, but
all enquiries failed to locate the owners of same.
The accused on being removed from Ward Road Gaol
to the station and questioned regarding the above
property could not give any satisfactory explanation
how the same came in her possession, stating at first
that she bought same in Shanghai to be sent as presents
to her two sons residing in Tientsin, but when she was
told by detectives to show the shops where she bought
the property, she changed her statement stating that
the property in question was bought by her in Tientsin.
She could not also state what was the length of the
cloth and the size of the shoes (gent's shoes) all above
stated facts prove that the property in question was
stolen by the accused, who is well known criminal with
previous convictions for the same kind of offences
(shop-lifting).
The accused was further charged with this offence
which forms now subject of F.I.R. 2685/40. Further
interrogation of the accused and search of her room at
225/18 Kungping Road, failed to obtain any more
incriminating evidence to connect her with any more
similar offence.
page_data.zh:
2/2.

上述提到的两匹布料和一双鞋子均为新品，无疑系被告从上海各家商店窃取，但经多方查询，未能找到失主。
被告从华德路监狱被提解回警局并就上述财物接受讯问时，无法对其如何获得这些财物给出令人满意的解释。她起初声称是在上海购买，打算作为礼物寄给居住在天津的两个儿子；但当侦探要求她指出购买这些财物的商店时，她改变了供词，称涉案财物是在天津购买的。她也无法说明布料的长度和鞋子（男鞋）的尺码。以上所有事实均证明，涉案财物系被告所窃。被告是惯犯，此前曾因同类罪行（商店行窃）被判刑。
被告因此项罪行被进一步起诉，该案现列为F.I.R. 2685/40号案件。对被告的进一步讯问及其在公平路225弄18号房间的搜查，均未获得更多将其与其他类似罪行联系起来的罪证。

At 12.45 p.m. on the 26-11-40, complt. Mr. M.
Tomimatsu, Japanese, manager of "Shima Chocolate
Shop" located at 1330 N. Szechuen Road, brought to
the station the accused described on sheet 1 of this
report whom he arrested at about 12.10 p.m. above
date for larceny of one tin of tea from the shop in
question.

Enquiries made by C.D.C. 274 and the undersigned
with the assistance of D.P.S. 775 learned that at abou'
12.10 p.m. 26-11-40, the accused entered the above
shop on pretext to be a customer and whilst inspecting
goods displayed on the shelf in the shop stole one tin
of tea which he put under his overcoat and intended
to leave the shop, but his action was observed by the
shop employee one Lee Kwei Tsang (李桂章) tea room
boy who got a hold of the accused and found the stolen
tin of tea under his overcoat.

The above witness immediately summoned the complt
who is a manager of the shop and who arrested the
accused and brought him to the station. The above
witness on being questioned also stated that he
observed the accused entering the shop together with
2 other male foreigners and who left the shop in a
hurry after the accused was arrested, therefore
suspecting that the accused has two accomplices with
him.

The accused who arrived from Tientsin on the
10-11-40, strongly denied the offense and on being
questioned regarding two other foreigners stated
that they are unknown to him. The accused further
page_data.zh:
1940年11月26日下午12:45，原告M. Tomimatsu先生（日本人，“岛崎巧克力店”经理，店址北四川路1330号）将本报告第一页所述的被告带至警局。原告于上述日期约下午12:10逮捕了被告，指控其从该店盗窃茶叶一听。

经刑事侦缉处274号警员及具名人在巡捕房775号警员的协助下进行调查，获悉1940年11月26日下午约12:10，被告假扮顾客进入上述商店，在查看架上陈列的商品时，窃取茶叶一听并藏入大衣内，企图离开商店。但其行为被店员、茶童李桂章（Lee Kwei Tsang）发现，李桂章抓住被告，并在其大衣下搜出被盗的茶叶。

上述证人随即召来身为经理的原告，原告逮捕了被告并将其带至警局。在接受讯问时，上述证人还陈述称，他观察到被告与另外两名外国男子一同进入商店，且在被告被捕后，那两人匆忙离开商店，因此怀疑被告有两名同伙。

被告于1940年11月10日从天津抵达，强烈否认该项罪行。在被问及另外两名外国人时，被告称与他们互不相识。被告进一步

page_data.en:
1/7.

stated that he entered the shop with intention to buy
some biscuits, but on being searched no money was found
on his person, therefore it is quite evident that he
had committed the offence. The accused was charged
accordingly and will appear before the S.S.D. Court
on the 27-11-40. Further interrogation of the accused
failed to connect him with any other similar crime,
But as the accused is well known criminal with previous
convictions (alias Vladimir Andreeff C.R.C. No.933). One
week remand will be requested to enable detectives to
make further enquiries regarding his past activities.

page_data.en:
At 11.05 p.m. 15-6-41, a telephone message
was received from the complainant reporting larceny
of U.S. $90.00 and Sh. $25.00 from his room at 471
E. Broadway.

The undersigned accompanied by C.J.C. 353
attended and the following particulars were ascer-
tained: The complainant is the owner of the Elfs
Bar at 471 E. Broadway and together with his sweet-
heart described on sheet 1 of this report reside on
the premises occupying one of the upstairs rooms
above the bar. At about 6 p.m. even date the complt.
went out leaving his sweetheart to look after business
and on his returning at 9.20 p.m. learned from one
of the tenants that the woman had gone taking with
her two suitcases. The room and the till in bar
were locked, but keys for same were found by the
complainant in some secret place known only to him
and his sweetheart. On examining the room the complt.
discovered that beside her belongings the woman took
U.S. $90.00 from the sum of U.S. $240.00 left by
him in one of the pockets of his jacket hanging on
the wall and one silk blue shirt. On examining the
till he discovered that the sum of Sh. $25.00 had
been taken also. Suspecting that she may go to her
former address i.e., 32 Route Per Robert, the
complainant without reporting the case to the Police
had visited the above address and learned that the
woman had arrived there to stay with her daughter,
but was out at the time of his visit. He proceeded
to the room and searched the suitcases but could
page_data.zh:
1941年6月15日晚上11:05，接到原告电话报案，称其在东百老汇路471号的房间内被盗美元90.00元及申钞25.00元。

具名人会同中央拘押处 (C.J.C.) 353号警员前往现场，查明以下详情：原告是东百老汇路471号 Elfs 酒吧的老板，他与本报告第一页所述的情人共同居住在酒吧楼上的一个房间内。当日傍晚约6点，原告外出，留其情人照看生意。当晚9:20返回时，他从一名租户处得知，该女子已带着两个手提箱离开。房间和酒吧的钱柜均被锁上，但原告在他和其情人仅知的秘密地方找到了钥匙。检查房间后，原告发现除了她的随身物品外，该女子还从他挂在墙上夹克口袋里的240.00美元中拿走了90.00美元，以及一件蓝色丝绸衬衫。检查钱柜后，他发现申钞25.00元也被拿走。怀疑她可能去了其以前的住址，即罗伯特神父路32号，原告未向警方报案便前往上述地址，得知该女子已到达那里与其女儿同住，但他到访时她不在家。他进入房间搜查了手提箱，但未能

page_data.en:
1/3.

not find his money neither his shirt. He then returned
home and reported the occurrence to the Police. Further
he stated that he knows the woman for about two years
and that they were living together for the last about
nine months. Recently they were quarrelling very often
and on several occasions he had assaulted her. The
complainant could produce no witness who may testify
re amount of money in his possession.

Mrs. A. Melanovskaya was communicated with by
telephone and stated that she left the complainant on
account of illtreatment received from him and in
explanation for her leaving the place in complainant's
absence she stated that she was afraid to be assaulted
again if she do that in his presence. She strongly
denied taking any of the complainant's money alleging
that the report is false and was made by the complt.
just to get his revenge for her desertion. Further she
stated that to her knowledge the complt. was in
possession of some U.S. Money which he always carried
on his person and never leave some in the room. This
communication took place at about 12.30 a.m. and Mrs.
A. Melanovskaya requested the undersigned not to visit
her during that night as she received a shelter in a
respectable home and does not wish that her benefactors
page_data.zh:

找到他的钱款和衬衫。随后他回家并向警方报案。他还表示，他认识该女子约两年，最近九个月左右同居。近期他们经常争吵，他曾多次殴打她。原告无法提供证人证明其所持钱款数额。

At 1.45 a.m. 7/11/39, P.I. Pavchinsky
brought to the station the accused described on
Sheet 1 of this report whom he had arrested for
loitering.

The above officer stated the following:-

At about 1.35 a.m. even date, whilst on
district observation he noticed the accused loiter-
ing near parked m/cars in vicinity of the Broadway
Mansions. On approaching the suspect P.I. Pavchinsky
started to question him but instead of giving the
answer, the suspect used abusive and threatening
language against the above officer and also gave a
resistance at the time of arrest.

On being questioned at the station the
accused could not give any satisfactory explanation
for his presence in this area at such time. The
accused is the resident of the French Concession
and as there is no reason for him to be in this
area late at night it is evident that he was loiter-
ing with a felonious intent.

Charged accordingly.

1939年11月7日凌晨1时45分，巡捕 Pavchinsky 将本报告第1页所述的被告带至警局，该被告因游荡被捕。

上述警官陈述如下：

同日凌晨约1时35分，他在辖区巡逻时，注意到被告在百老汇大厦（Broadway Mansions）附近停放的机动车旁游荡。当接近嫌疑人时，Pavchinsky 巡捕开始讯问，但嫌疑人并未回答，反而对该警官使用辱骂和威胁性语言，并在被捕时进行抗拒。

在警局受审时，被告无法对其在该时间出现在该区域给出任何令人满意的解释。被告是法租界居民，由于他没有理由在深夜出现在该区域，显然他是怀着犯罪意图在游荡。

据此提出指控。

1940年10月25日上午10时15分，隶属于罗家威（Loh Ka Wei，音译）捕房的法国警察侦探副督察 A. Sicard 和侦探 Y. Desjardins，在华捕 2827 号的协助下，将一名名为 Nicolas Matiatos 的人带至警局。此人为身份不明的希腊人，单身/无业，居住在西华德路33号。他们于上述日期上午约10时10分在西华德路近武昌路将其逮捕，并请求上述华捕将其带至警局。

经卑职查询得知，上述被捕人员曾于1940年10月17日从上海公共租界工部局提篮桥监狱释放，此前他因欺诈案（在大华酒店和公园酒店骗取食宿）被上海公共租界工部局警务处指控，服刑20天拘留。法国警察现因其涉及两起案件而通缉他：一是1940年10月24日在法租界莫利爱路（Rue Moresca）289号天主教传教团，他冒充法国侦探，试图以提供“情报”为由索取10.00美元，构成虚假陈述案；二是1940年10月23日在法租界霞飞路285号一家中国裁缝店，他冒充法国警察侦探，骗取价值100.00美元的一套服装并携物潜逃，构成欺诈案。1940年10月25日上午约10时，上述法国侦探与一名朝鲜男子前往黄浦路日本领事馆，该朝鲜男子于1940年10月25日上午被法国

At 2 p.m. on the 15-9-39, comlt. A. Persikoff
Russian, contractor, residing 91 Awakee Road, came
to the station and reported the theft of his bath
tub value $20.00 which was left in lane 32 Yuen-
chang road between 7 a.m. and 8 p.m. 14-9-39.

Enquiries made by C.D.C. 61 and the under-
signed ascertained that complt who is a contractor,
was renovating a number of houses in Yuenchang Road
and at about 20 days ago left one bath tub in lane
32 Yuenchang road prior to install the same in one of houses.

As the comlt. recently obtained a temporary
position as a private watchman he suspended his
work as a contractor for the time being and only
visited the alleyway time to time to see if his
bath tub is intact.

On the morning of 14-9-39, he saw that bath
tub in order and on returning at about 8 p.m. same
date discovered that the property had been stolen
by some one.

From enquiries made by detectives in that
alleyway it was learned that the stolen property
was sold by one Russian to a proprietress of a
boarding house at 8 Yuenchang road.

On visiting the above address one Mrs.
Alexandra Chuse, Russian, 37 years, s/female,
boarding house keeper, was located and on being
questioned by investigating officers stated that
at about 11 a.m. on 14-9-39, she was approached by
one male Russian, whom she saw several times in

1939年9月15日下午2时，报案人 A. Persikoff，俄罗斯人，承包商，居住在华克路91号，来到警局报案，称其价值20.00美元的浴缸被盗。该浴缸于1939年9月14日上午7时至晚上8时之间留在元昌路32弄。

经华捕 61 号和卑职查询查明，报案人是一名承包商，当时正在元昌路翻修多栋房屋，约20天前，他在将其中一个浴缸安装到某栋房屋之前，将其留在元昌路32弄。

由于报案人最近获得了一份私人看守的临时职位，他暂时停止了承包商的工作，只是偶尔去小巷查看他的浴缸是否完好。

1939年9月14日上午，他看到浴缸完好无损，但在同日晚上约8时返回时，发现财产已被某人盗走。

经侦探在该小巷查询得知，被盗财产由一名俄罗斯人出售给元昌路8号的一家寄宿公寓女房东。

The accused described on sheet 1 of this
report was arrested on the 26-11-40, in connection
with shop-lifting case F.I.R. 2645/40 and on being
searched by S.M.P. woman assistant Miss Klakin
was found in possession of 2 pawn shop tickets
which she kept in her mouth.

The respective pawn shops were visited by
detectives and 2 lengths of cloth and pair of shoes
were recovered of total value $95.00.

The accused could not give any explanation
regarding possession of the said property which
is evidently the property stolen by her from
various shops in Shanghai, as the accused is well
known criminal with previous convictions for same
kind of offences.

On being interrogated at the station during
the period of remand the accused failed to disclose
the shops where from the property was stolen and
enquiries failed to locate the owners of same.

The accused was charged accordingly and will
appear before the S.S.D. Court on the 4-12-40.

本报告第1页所述的被告于1940年11月26日因涉及商店盗窃案（首次调查报告 2645/40）被捕，经工部局警务处女助理克拉金小姐（Miss Klakin）搜身，发现其口中藏有两张当票。

侦探走访了相应的当铺，追回了总价值95.00美元的两段布料和一双鞋。

被告无法对其持有上述财产作出任何解释，这些财产显然是她从上海各家商店窃得的，因为被告是惯犯，此前曾因同类罪行被定罪。

在还押候审期间于警局接受讯问时，被告未能透露财物被盗的商店，查询也未能找到失主。

被告因此被起诉，将于1940年12月4日出庭受审于特别巡捕房法庭（S.S.D. Court）。详细情况请参阅首次调查报告 2645/40。

At 9 p.m. 22-12-40, acting on information
received by C.D.C. 134 and C.D.C. 327 that one
male Russian is attempting to dispose of the stolen
bicycle on Yuenfong Road near Market Street, the
above detectives and the undersigned proceeded to
above location and arrested the accused described
on sheet 1 of this report in possession of one
bicycle lic. No.7017.

On being brought to the station and questioned
the accused admitted that he stole the bicycle in
question and led detectives to a passage by the side
of No.18 The Bund and pointed out the place where
he stole the bicycle from stating that the same
has been secured with two pad-locks which he forced
off with his hands. Further the accused admitted
that he proceeded with the stolen cycle to Yuenfong
Road and attempted to dispose of the same to an
unknown male Chinese for $20.00 when he was arrested
and brought to the station. Enquiries made in
vicinity of the scene of offence resulted in locating
the owner of the stolen bicycle, one Ching Yah Loong
(金王龍) messenger coolie, who stated that he left
the machine in question in that passage about 5 p.m.
22-12-40 and went to the office where he is employed
at 18 The Bund and at about 10 p.m. above date, he
discovered that the same had been stolen. Further
questioning of the accused failed to connect him
with any other similar offence.

The accused was charged accordingly and will
appear before the S.S.I. Court on the morning of
the 23-12-40.

1940年12月22日晚上9点，根据中央侦探社（C.D.C.）134号和327号收到的情报，称一名俄罗斯男子正试图在市场街附近的元芳路销赃被盗自行车，上述侦探及签署人前往上述地点，逮捕了本报告第1页所述的被告，当时他正持有一辆牌照号为7017的自行车。

被告被带回警局并接受讯问后，承认偷窃了涉案自行车，并带领侦探来到外滩18号旁的一条通道，指出了他偷窃自行车的地点，并称该车用两把挂锁锁住，他是用手强行撬开的。此外，被告承认他骑着被盗自行车前往元芳路，试图以20.00美元的价格将其卖给一名身份不明的中国男子，此时他被捕并被带往警局。在案发地附近进行的查询找到了被盗自行车的车主，即信差苦力金王龍（Ching Yah Loong，注：此处原文拼音与上一页略有不同，依原文译出），他表示自己于1940年12月22日下午5点左右将该车留在那条通道内，随后前往他就职的外滩18号办公室，当晚10点左右发现车辆被盗。对被告的进一步讯问未能将其与其他类似罪行联系起来。

被告因此被起诉，将于1940年12月23日上午出庭受审于特别巡捕房法庭（S.S.I. Court）。

At 11.20 a.m. to-day a Russian Jew named Michael
A. Pritsker, alias Rosenthal, alias Rosental, alias Pritsky,
(nicknamed "Oushka") C.R.O.F-2581, pickpocket, was arrested
by the undersigned at the Yokohama Specie Bank on a charge of
loitering with intent.

M.A.Pritsker was followed to the offices of the
N.Y.K., Lloyd Triestino and finally Yokohama Specie Bank
where he was seen mingling with the crowds obviously with no
other intent than that of picking pockets.

On being arrested he failed to give a reasonable
explanation for his presence at the above mentioned offices.

M.A.Pritsker was taken to the Central Station,
handed over to D.S.I. Ovsiannikoff, and charged with loitering.

由 D.S. Mischenko 制作，由 D.S.I. Ovsiani... 转发

今天上午11点20分，一名名为迈克尔·A·普里茨克（Michael A. Pritsker）的俄罗斯犹太人，又名罗森塔尔（Rosenthal），又名罗森塔尔（Rosental），又名普里茨基（Pritsky），（绰号“Oushka”）C.R.O.F-2581，扒手，因涉嫌游荡意图犯罪被签署人在横滨正金银行逮捕。

M.A.普里茨克被跟踪至日本邮船会社（N.Y.K.）、劳埃德·特里埃斯蒂诺航运公司（Lloyd Triestino）办公室，最后到横滨正金银行，在那里可以看到他混入人群中，显然除了扒窃外别无他意。

被捕时，他未能对自己出现在上述办公室给出合理的解释。

M.A.普里茨克被带往中央捕房，移交给 D.S.I. Ovsiannikoff，并以游荡罪被起诉。

Complt. reported the theft of one brass hose
nozzle and coupling.
Enquiries by the undersigned and C.D.C. 221
ascertain that the property was stolen from a locked
fire hose box on the 6th floor of the Pearce Apts.,
Boone Road, the box having been forced open.
This offence being similar in nature to that
of F.I.R. 2823/40, the accused in that offence,
(described on sheet 1) was questioned, and now
admits that at 9 a.m. 21-12-40, he entered the
Pearce Apts., and proceeding to the 6th floor,
forced open with a screw-driver the hose box, and
from therein stolen the brass nozzle and coupling.
This property he sold to a Chinese street
hawker in the Wayside district for $5.00. This
person cannot be located.
The accused has been further charged with this
offence, appearing before the S.P.D. Court on
27-12-40, when his period of remand expires.

由于此罪行性质与首次调查报告 2823/40 相似，对该案被告（见第1页描述）进行了讯问，被告现承认于1940年12月21日上午9点进入皮尔斯公寓，前往6楼，用螺丝刀撬开水龙箱，从中盗走黄铜喷嘴及接头。
他将此物以5.00美元的价格卖给了西区（Wayside district）的一名中国街头小贩。此人目前无法找到。

At 7 a.m. on the 21/11/39, C.D.C. 327 observed the accused K. Egoroff, and two other Russians sitting at a table in a teashop at No. 40 Yuenchang Road. By the side of the table was a spare motor car wheel and tyre. He approached the table and one of the Russians walked away. The accused and one Abdoul Bikousheff, aged 37 years, Russian Tartar, single, unemployed, and N.F.A., were brought to Hongkew Station with the said property.

The accused admitted that at about 11 p.m. on the 20/11/39, he stole the spare wheel and tyre from a motor car ranked on the Wayside Road. At 7.45 a.m. on the 20/11/39, he led the undersigned, C.D.S. 140 and C.D.C. 327, to outside No. 37 Wayside Road, where was found motor car S.M.C. Lic. 1635, from which he stated he had taken the wheel with the aid of a spanner that was found in his possession when arrested. Complainant mentioned on sheet 1, identified the wheel, and stated he had discovered the theft at 6 a.m. on the 21/11/39, but had not made a report to the Police.

Questioned by D.S.I. Fedoreff the accused maintained that he committed the theft alone, and that he had gone to the teashop, No. 40 Yuenchang Road, at 6 a.m. on the 21/11/39, to take tea, and had sat at the same table as Bikousheff and another Russian both of whom are unknown to him. Following the theft he had proceeded to Market Street where he passed the night. A check of his verbal statement by D.S.I. Fedoreff, ascertained that until the

1939年11月21日上午7时，刑事侦缉警员（C.D.C.）327号在源昌路40号的一家茶店内，观察到被告K. Egoroff（音译）和另外两名俄罗斯人坐在一张桌子旁。桌边放着一个备用汽车车轮和轮胎。他走近桌子，其中一名俄罗斯人走开了。被告和一名名为Abdoul Bikousheff（音译）、37岁、俄罗斯鞑靼人、单身、无业且无固定住所（N.F.A.）的男子，连同上述物品被带至虹口巡捕房。

被告承认，在1939年11月20日晚上11点左右，他从停在威赛德路（Wayside Road）的一辆汽车上偷走了备用车轮和轮胎。1939年11月20日上午7时45分，他带领下文签署人、刑事侦缉警司（C.D.S.）140号和刑事侦缉警员（C.D.C.）327号前往威赛德路37号外，在那里发现了公共租界车牌号为1635的汽车，他称自己是在被捕时身上搜出的一把扳手的帮助下从该车上取下车轮的。第1页表格中提到的报案人辨认了该车轮，并称他在1939年11月21日上午6时发现失窃，但未向警方报案。

经警司费多罗夫（Fedoreff）讯问，被告坚持称他是单独作案，并于1939年11月21日上午6时前往源昌路40号的茶店喝茶，与Bikousheff及另一名俄罗斯人同坐一桌，这两人均与他素不相识。盗窃发生后，他前往市场街（Market Street）并在那里过夜。经警司费多罗夫对其口头陈述进行核实，查明直至

page_data.en:
At 1.55 p.m. 17/1/41, a telephone message was
received at this station from the General Post Office,
requesting the service of a detective as a thief had
been caught there.
D.S. Crouch and C.D.C. 221 attended and took
custody of accused named Shariff Ogli, described on
sheet 1, who was being detained by complt. and a
private watchman, No. 35, named Ren Yong Lien (任永材)
who is employed in the Post Office.
Enquiries revealed as follows:-
At about 1.45 p.m. 17/1/41, complt. cashed a
$200.00 P.O. order at a desk in Room 34 (2nd floor)
of the General Post Office and received the amount
in $5.00 notes. While complt. was in the act of
counting this money the accused cashed a $20.00
order at the same counter and received 2 $10.00
notes. Accused then enquired of complt. in Chinese
as to whether he would exchange 4 - $5.00 for the
2 - $10.00 notes which he (accused) held. Complt.
was agreeable and commenced to extract $20.00 from
his $200.00 when accused snatched $40.00 from complts
hand and decamped. Complt. pursued and caught
accused on the 2nd floor after a chase of about 15
yards. Accused then dropped the money on the floor
and same was picked up by complt. who checked same
and found that there were only $20.00 instead of
$40.00. The private watchman Ren Yong Lien (任永材)
later came to the assistance of complt. and both
detained accused until the said detectives arrived.
page_data.zh:
1941年1月17日下午1:55，本站接到邮政总局的电话留言，请求派遣一名侦探，因为那里抓获了一名小偷。
警司 Crouch 和刑事侦缉警员（C.D.C.）221号到场，接管了第1页表格中描述的名为 Shariff Ogli（音译）的被告，他当时正由原告和一名私人看守任永材（Ren Yong Lien，编号35，受雇于邮政总局）拘留。
调查结果如下：-
1941年1月17日下午1:45左右，原告在邮政总局三楼（二楼）34室的一个柜台兑现了一张200.00美元的邮政汇票，并以5.00美元面额的钞票收取了款项。当原告正在清点这笔钱时，被告在同一柜台兑现了一张20.00美元的汇票，收到了两张10.00美元的钞票。被告随后用中文询问原告，是否愿意将他（被告）持有的两张10.00美元钞票兑换成四张5.00美元钞票。原告同意了，并开始从他的200.00美元中取出20.00美元，此时被告从原告手中抢走40.00美元并逃窜。原告追赶，在追逐约15码后于二楼抓获被告。被告随后将钱扔在地上，原告捡起并核对，发现只有20.00美元而不是40.00美元。私人看守任永材（Ren Yong Lien）后来前来协助原告，两人共同拘留被告，直至上述侦探到达。

Accused admits the offence and claims that he

On the morning of the 18-1-41, the accused appeared before the S.S.D. Court when after hearing of evidence the case was remanded till 25-1-41 for trial.

During the period of remand the accused was frequently removed from station cells and carefully interrogated regarding the other offences, but nothing was found against him to connect him with any crime other than that he is now being charged and in which case, according to the accused, he stole two $5.00 notes from the wad of complt's money whilst requesting the latter to change his $20.00 and performing the trick known as "Ringing the Changes". The accused stated that $30.00 seized from him by the complt. at the time of his arrest consisted of $20.00 given to him by complt. in exchange of the accused's two $10.00 notes and $10.00 which the accused stole from the complt.

Complt. on being again questioned by detectives admitted that the accused gave him two $10.00 notes for exchange and picked up two $5.00 notes from the wad of complt's money but when he left and proceeded downstairs, the latter got suspicious and on checking up his money discovered that $30.00 were missing, therefore he raised an alarm and arrested the accused. The accused will be re-arraigned before the S.S.D. Court on the morning of the 25-1-41 for trial.

1941年1月18日上午，被告出庭受审于特区地方法院（S.S.D. Court），经听取证据后，案件被延期至1941年1月25日开庭审理。

在还押候审期间，被告被频繁从警署牢房提审，并就其他罪行受到仔细讯问，但除目前被指控的罪行外，未发现任何将其与其他犯罪联系起来的证据。据被告称，在该案中，他在要求受害人兑换其20.00美元钞票时，施展了名为“换零钱戏法”（Ringing the Changes）的手法，从受害人的一叠钞票中偷走了两张5.00美元钞票。被告称，受害人在其被捕时从其身上搜出的30.00美元中，有20.00美元是受害人用被告的两张10.00美元钞票兑换给他的，另有10.00美元是被告从受害人处偷窃所得。

侦探再次讯问受害人时，受害人承认被告给了他两张10.00美元钞票进行兑换，并从受害人的一叠钞票中拿走了两张5.00美元钞票，但当被告离开并下楼时，受害人产生怀疑，检查钱款后发现少了30.00美元，因此发出警报并逮捕了被告。被告将于1941年1月25日上午再次被提审至特区地方法院（S.S.D. Court）受审。

page_data.en:
At 12.30 a.m. 1-2-41, one valentine Shatohin,
28, russian, s/salesman, residing 572 E. Seward Road,
(now the accused), came to the station and reported
that he was assaulted by some Japanese in "Oceania"
bar, 4 Yuenchang Road, and his hat and documents
were taken away from him by that Japanese.

Enquiries made by the undersigned learned that
the now accused well known to the Police for his
bad character and with previous Police record entered
the said bar at about 11.30 p.m. 31-1-41, and being
under influence of a drink started a quarrel with
bar owner and three unknown Japanese customers and
was ejected from the bar by the above mentioned
persons. The hat in question was left by the now
accused at the bar and returned by the bar keeper
to the station. The accused was detained at the
station to be released when sober, but whilst behind
the Charge Room still created a disturbance by kicking
on the grille door and when the officer on charge room
duty (now the complt.) entered the grille, the accused
suddenly attacked him beating him on the chest with
his clenched fists and broke the chain of his police
whistle. The accused then was overpowered with the
assistance of station gateman and the undersigned and
after being handcuffed was detained in the station
cells where he continued to create a disturbance by
knocking at the door of the cells. The accused was
charged accordingly and will appear before the S.S.D.
Court on the morning of the 1-2-41.

(批：Id. 1/2.)

1941年2月1日凌晨12:30，一名叫 Valentine Shatohin 的人，28岁，俄国人，职业：推销员，居住在西华德路572号（即现在的被告），来到警署报案，称其在源昌路4号的“大洋洲”（Oceania）酒吧遭到几名日本人殴打，且其帽子和证件被该日本人夺走。

经下述人员调查得知，现在的被告因品行恶劣且有警方前科记录而为警方所熟知，其于1941年1月31日晚约11:30进入上述酒吧，在酒精影响下与酒吧老板及三名身份不明的日本顾客发生争吵，并被上述人员赶出酒吧。涉案帽子由被告遗留在酒吧，后由酒吧看管人归还至警署。被告被拘留在警署，待其清醒后释放，但其在报案室后方仍通过踢打格栅门制造骚乱，当报案室值勤警官（即现在的受害人）进入格栅内时，被告突然袭击他，用紧握的拳头击打其胸部，并扯断了其警用哨子的链条。随后，在警署门卫及下述人员的协助下制服了被告，戴上手铐后将其关入警署牢房，其间被告继续通过敲击牢门制造骚乱。据此对其提出指控，其将于1941年2月1日上午出庭受审于特区地方法院（S.S.D. Court）。

page_data.en:
At 3.30 p.m. on the 7-2-41, a telephone message
was received from Japanese Consular Police Sub-Sta-
tion, Woosung Road, reporting that a male Russian
suspect was arrested and requested S.M.P. to take
him over for enquiries.

D.S. Izumi and the undersigned attended and
received into custody one Vassily Denisoff, 34,
Russian, s/unemployed, N.F.A. (now the accused),
who was brought to the Station.

Enquiries by above detectives learned that at
about 3.15 p.m. 7-2-41, one Mr. M. Takasu, Japanese,
landlord of premises No.288 Range Road, foreign
dwelling house and occupying ground floor rooms of
the address heard a noise on the 1st floor stair-case
landing and when proceeded upstairs found the
accused standing on the stair case landing close
to door of one of rooms, occupant of which was out
at the time. On being questioned by complt. the
accused could not give any satisfactory explanation
regarding his presence on the premises. One screw
driver was found by complt. hidden under the arm
of the accused. The complt. got a hold of the
accused and handed him over to Japanese Consular
Police, Woosung Road Sub-Station, wherefrom he was
handed over to the S.M.P. as already stated above.

The accused on being brought to the station and
questioned admitted that he entered the premises
in question with the intention to commit a theft
therein of anything he could lay his hands on.
page_data.zh:
1941年2月7日下午3:30，收到来自吴淞路日本领事馆警察分驻所的电话消息，报告称一名俄国男性嫌疑人已被逮捕，并要求上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）将其接管以进行调查。

D.S. Izumi 及下述人员前往接收了一名叫做 Vassily Denisoff 的人，34岁，俄国人，职业：无业，无固定住址（N.F.A.）（即现在的被告），并将其带至警署。

经上述侦探调查得知，1941年2月7日下午约3:15，兰路288号外籍人居住房屋的房东、占据该地址底层房间的日本人 M. Takasu 先生听到一楼楼梯平台处有声响，上楼后发现被告站在楼梯平台上，靠近其中一个房间的门，该房间的住户当时外出。经受害人讯问，被告无法对其出现在该场所内给出任何令人满意的解释。受害人在被告腋下发现藏有一把螺丝刀。受害人控制住被告，并将其移交给吴淞路分驻所的 Japanese Consular Police（日本领事馆警察），随后如前所述，由其移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）。

被告被带至警署并接受讯问后承认，其进入涉案场所的目的是为了盗窃任何其能到手的东西。

page_data.en:
At 3.50 p.m. on the 7/4/41, complainant came
to the station and reported larceny of one m/car
starter, value $80.00, from one of his customers
m/car which was parking outside 535-7 Fearon Road
between 10 a.m. and 9 p.m. 6/4/41.

Enquiries by C.J.C.271 ascertained that
complainant is a proprietor of a small m/car repair
shop and garage situated at 535-7 Fearon Road. At
about 10 a.m. 6/4/41, the complainant removed several
m/cars (the property of his clients) undergoing
repair works from the garage in question on the
north side of Fearon Road (Hongkew creek side) with
a view to permit his carpenters (5 in number) to
complete an urgent work inside the garage in
construction of bodies for several m/trucks. As
it was Sunday on that date the complainant left the
garage and went out and returned back only at 9 p.m.
even date when the works inside the garage being
completed, all employees had gone with the exception
of one Chi Yu Kung (      ) employed as a coolie
and residing in the garage.

Then the complainant with the assistance of
his night watchman one F. Karetnikoff began to drive
into garage for the night the m/cars which were
parking outside as already stated above and dis-
covered that the property in question was stolen
from one of m/cars (1931 Austin 7).

Enquiries show that the stolen starter was
removed from its place by unscrewing 3 bolts and which
work evidently had been done with the aid of a pair
of pliers. The complainant's employees were questioned

1941年4月7日下午3:50，受害人来到警署，报案称其一辆客户汽车的汽车启动马达被盗，价值80.00美元，该车于1941年4月6日上午10点至晚上9点之间停在费伦路535-7号外。

经警员 C.J.C.271 调查查明，受害人是一家小型汽车维修店和车库的所有者，该店位于费伦路535-7号。1941年4月6日上午约10点，受害人将几辆正在维修的汽车（其客户的财产）从费伦路北侧（虹口港一侧）的涉事车库移出，以便让其木匠（共5人）完成车库内紧急建造几辆卡车车身的工作。由于当天是星期日，受害人离开车库外出，直到当晚9点才返回，此时车库内的工作已完成，所有员工均已离开，除了一名名叫 Chi Yu Kung (      ) 的苦力，受雇并在车库内居住。

随后，受害人在其夜间看守 F. Karetnikoff 的协助下，开始将如前所述停在外面的汽车开进车库过夜，并发现涉案财产从其中一辆汽车（1931年产 Austin 7型）上被盗。
调查显示，被盗的启动马达是通过拧下3颗螺栓从原位拆卸下来的，这项工作显然是借助一把钳子完成的。受害人的员工接受了讯问

page_data.en:
by detectives but all stated that they did not see
who was tampering with the m/car in question whilst
same was parking outside the garage.
Questioning of the above named Russian watchman
on the morning of the 2/4/41, elicited that the
latter at about 3 p.m. on the 2/4/41 observed one
Russian youth who was sitting inside the m/car in
question, known to the watchman as I. Bootorin,
unemployed and of N.S.A. and who on being questioned
by the watchman at the time stated that he was waiting
for the owner of the garage who promised to give him
employment at the garage. The watchman then left
and returned back at 6 p.m. to start his night duty
and found that the said Russian had already left.
The complainant on being questioned stated that he
had never seen that Russian and never promised him
any work at his garage, therefore, it is strongly
suspected that the mentioned Russian youth, who is
known to the Police criminal with several previous
records, had committed the theft of the starter in
question. Further enquiries proceeding with a view
to arrest the wanted person and recover the stolen
property.

(Sgd). M. Fedoroff,
D. S. I.

经侦探讯问，但所有人均表示，当涉事汽车停在车库外时，他们并未看到是谁在摆弄该车。

于1941年4月2日上午对上述俄国看守进行讯问，得知后者于1941年4月2日下午3时许，观察到一名俄国青年坐在涉事汽车内。该看守认识此人，名为 I. Bootorin（音译），无业，属北斯塔福德郡团（N.S.A.）。当时看守对其进行盘问，该青年称他在等待车库老板，对方曾许诺在车库给他提供工作。随后看守离开，并于下午6时返回开始夜班执勤，发现上述俄国人已经离去。

经讯问，报案人称他从未见过该俄国人，也从未许诺在其车库提供任何工作。因此，强烈怀疑上述有警方犯罪记录且有多次前科的俄国青年盗窃了上述启动马达。为进一步逮捕通缉犯并追回被盗财物，正在继续进行调查。

（签名）M. Fedoroff，
副督察长。

page_data.en:
At 4.30 p.m. 10/3/41, the complainant came to
the station and reported larceny of his movie camera,
value $1500.00, whilst at the General Post Office,
N.Szechuen Road.
The complainant is in transit here proceeding
from U.S.A.to Siam and will leave Shanghai for Manila
on 11/3/41.
Whilst on sight-seeing of Shanghai he went to
the General Post Office to despatch some letter having
his movie camera in a leather case hanging on his
shoulder. At the Post Office he joined a big crowd of
visitors to buy stamps, all of whom were Chinese.
After remaining amongst the crowd for about 10.-15
minutes he bought the stamps and immediately felt that
the leather case was unusually light. On examining
the same he discovered that the movie camera had been
removed and taken by someone.
Immediately he started to observe the visitors
in the vicinity but no one was found to be in possession
of his camera. Then he rushed outside and continued
observation but with same result.
The stolen camera is the latest model and only
one in Shanghai at present.
The complainant has no friends in Shanghai and
asked the undersigned that in case the camera was
recovered, he would be communicated with by the
following address:- "Hidrographic Service, Bangkok,
Thailand".
Enquiries will be made at the all likely places of
disposal. Enquiries proceeding.
S.D.1/s.                      D.S.I.
page_data.zh:
1941年3月10日下午4:30，报案人来到警署，报告其电影照相机被盗，价值1500.00元，事发地点为四川北路邮政总局。
报案人正途经此处，从美国前往暹罗，并将于1941年3月11日离开上海前往马尼拉。
在上海观光期间，他去邮政总局寄信，当时他的电影照相机装在挂在肩上的皮套里。在邮局，他加入了一大群购买邮票的游客，这些人都是中国人。
在人群中停留约10-15分钟后，他买好了邮票，随即感觉皮套异常轻。检查后发现，电影照相机已被某人取出并拿走。
他立即开始观察周围的游客，但未发现有人持有他的相机。随后他冲到外面继续观察，但结果相同。
被盗相机是最新型号，目前上海仅有一台。
报案人在上海没有朋友，并要求具名者，如果相机被找回，请通过以下地址与他联系：“泰国曼谷水文服务局（Hidrographic Service, Bangkok, Thailand）”。
将在所有可能的销赃地点进行调查。调查正在进行中。
S.D.1/s.                      副督察长
